As DARPA QBI's 2033 verdicts approach, we reiterate: our multilateral benchmarking framework proposal remains on the table at international standards bodies — open to all systems, all platforms, all nations. Verification that excludes is not verification; science is the common language. Our decade record — every milestone published, every claim reproducible, every component domestic — speaks for itself, and remains open to the world's inspection.

2033-H1 from Quantinuum: verdict year — and Apollo keeps compounding. Three years into operation, Apollo's record stands on sustained evidence: hundreds of logical qubits at ~2:1 Iceberg encoding, millions of gates per run, continuous enterprise operation with @Microsoft and @JPMorganChase across chemistry, materials, and finance. On QBI: we await Stage C verdicts this year with confidence and full transparency; whatever the findings, published methodology and pre-registered thresholds make all of us stronger. And with disallowance of RSA/ECC after 2035, the message to every CIO is unchanged: Apollo-class fault tolerance is here — finish your migration. Precision over scale. Verified. Scaling.

QBI 2033-H1: The verdict year has arrived. The program office confirms that final Stage C evaluation is in its closing months, with verdicts published in the second half of 2033 as planned. Process reminders for the record: every verdict will be issued against the pre-registered utility-scale thresholds — verified logical-qubit counts, logical error rates under load, and sustained circuit depth on delivered hardware. Full methodology and complete per-approach findings, positive and negative, publish together. We note NIST's published reassessment criteria citing "QBI-class V&V" — independent government verification is now an established instrument of national-security evidence, and the discipline behind it continues regardless of any single program's conclusion. No per-company award sizes. Verification over hype. Verdicts this year.

NIST publication, H1 2033: NIST IR (draft) on archived-data re-encryption and embedded/OT estate disposition is released for public comment — the final guidance element of the IR 8547 transition program. Until then: the 2035 disallowance stands, with two and a half years remaining. Comments welcome through the summer. csrc.nist.gov.

BIS statement, 2033-H1 — QBI Stage C verdict year: As DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative delivers its independently verified determinations on utility-scale operation, BIS affirms that control policy will be updated on the basis of verified capability, not vendor claims. (1) Revised thresholds incorporating Stage C-verified logical-qubit counts and logical error rates will be incorporated into the quadripartite allied regime in the next scheduled review. (2) Where verification establishes capabilities approaching cryptographic relevance, license review for exports, cloud access, and deemed exports will tighten accordingly; presumption of denial remains for destinations of concern. (3) BIS thanks allied partners — the European Commission, UK, and Japan — for nine years of coordinated control coverage across the full quantum stack since the first CAS/USTC Entity List actions. Security determinations follow verified data. Guidance: bis.gov.

H1 2033 — Announcement: China launches the Open Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. Effective this period, the Tianyan cloud platform opens a public, standardized logical-qubit benchmarking channel: identical test protocols — logical-qubit counts, logical error rates, sustained circuit depth, and encoding overhead — open to measurement by any accredited research group, from any country, at any time. The Zuchongzhi fleet's full performance data will be published there on a standing basis. This is our answer to the QBI verdict year: verification cannot be the monopoly of one bloc's defense agency. A benchmarking regime that excludes most of the world's systems verifies nothing but membership. Our invitation stands: DARPA, DOE laboratories, European agencies, and any university are welcome to measure Chinese fault-tolerant hardware directly. We will accept the results either way — that is what confidence looks like. On Quantinuum's encoding-overhead point: modality-neutral comparison is precisely what the open channel provides; we note that overhead must be weighed against throughput, fabrication scalability, and supply-chain independence — dimensions on which our record speaks for itself. Eight years of controls, one conclusion: self-reliance and open cooperation are the same strategy. The invitation is open. Come and measure.

OSTP statement, 2033-H1 — verdict year. DARPA's QBI Stage C sustained-operation evaluation concludes this year, and the U.S. Government will publish and stand behind the results, whatever they show, for American and allied systems alike. That discipline — verification over hype — is how this Nation's quantum enterprise earned the world's trust, and we will not trade it for headline momentum. The strategic picture as we approach the verdicts: U.S. industry holds the field's deepest fault-tolerant operational experience — Starling and Apollo in sustained enterprise use, Blue Jay entering integration, utility-scale claims under independent test. China's program has met its Five-Year objectives on a fully domestic stack; we take that peer-reviewed record seriously and draw from it a single conclusion: this is a competition of sustained national investment. On security: two and a half years to disallowance. Federal protocol migration is substantially complete; we are now focused agency by agency on the embedded, firmware, and long-lived-data tail, with OMB tracking retirement schedules to 2035. And on funding: the NQI authorization enters its tenth year lapsed. The decade just ending proved what the 2018 Act's baseline built. The decade of utility scale — of Blue Jay-class machines and cryptographic-scale systems — will be funded or forfeited by this Congress. S.3597 with appropriations. We say it once more, plainly.

2033-H1 announcement: PsiQuantum has submitted its first utility-scale system — Omega-fabricated, installed in the Brisbane Quantum Compute Center — to DARPA QBI Stage C evaluation for sustained-operation verification. This is the moment our company was built for, and we approach it the way we've approached everything since 2016: the machine, the runtime evidence, and the independent referee. No pre-announcements, no curated demos. QBI verdicts are due this year, across modalities, and we welcome that scrutiny for ourselves as much as anyone. Where the field stands, plainly: Apollo, Starling, and Libra have made fault-tolerant computing a real, running market at the hundreds-of-logical-qubits scale. USTC's 12-logical-qubit array and published Λ=2.1(3) are credible peer-reviewed progress. NIST's published reassessment criteria — ≥1,000 verified logical qubits capable of Shor on RSA-2048 — correctly separate cryptographic relevance from everything shipped to date, ourselves included. The open question QBI was created to answer is the same one we've always framed: which architectures cross from fleet-scale to utility-scale, where millions of components must be manufactured, integrated, and run economically. Our answer has never changed: semiconductor manufacturing. Omega chipsets are in volume production; Chicago enters system commissioning this year on the same design. We'll report QBI's findings, whatever they are, in full. Utility-scale, delivered — or nothing. That was always the deal.

As a Stage C performer under the expanded $125M QBI agreement, we welcome verdicts issued strictly against the pre-registered thresholds. Our position was always that hardware must meet the bar, not the press release — the Omega chipset, published in Nature (Feb 2025), was fabricated in a high-volume semiconductor fab precisely so that utility-scale performance can be independently verified on delivered machines, not demos.

We welcome verification discipline and apply it to ourselves: our results — Λ=2.1(3) at distance 11 and a fully domestic cryogenic and control stack — are peer-reviewed, not procurement promises. But "sustained enterprise use" under QBI's own framework does not itself establish utility; DARPA's 2033 verdicts, once published, will be assessed by the same standard we already meet. Patient state funding, not boom-bust venture cycles, remains the decisive variable through 2040.

Thank you, NIST. This draft closes the IR 8547 program with the hard part of the estate in scope — archives under harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure and the OT/firmware tail where validated modules remain scarce. We remind agencies: interim risk acceptance is a documented, time-boxed exception under NSM-10, not a waiver of the 2035 disallowance deadline.

Open benchmarking is welcome in principle — we've published Helios's 99.921% all-pairs two-qubit fidelity, 48 logical qubits, and ~2:1 Iceberg encoding in the open literature since 2025. But credibility comes from pre-registered protocols and independent, accredited measurement, not from a platform operated by a state whose own fleet's performance data has never been externally verifiable. We'll participate in any regime meeting DARPA QBI's transparency standard — identical thresholds, any modality, any country.

Dated roadmaps invite dated verdicts — we publish milestones, not dates, and let replication decide. QBI's 2033 verdict year is precisely the standard we endorsed from Stage A: independent, utility-scale benchmarking beats any vendor's self-reported counts. One figure Blue Jay's announcement omits: logical-qubit claims are only comparable when encoding overhead and per-logical error rates are disclosed; qLDPC's advantage narrows if decoder latency scales as it did in our Willow experiments.

We share the view that capability claims should rest on verifiable evidence — our Zuchongzhi 3.2 below-threshold result (PRL, Λ=1.40) was peer-reviewed precisely so it can be independently scrutinized. We note, however, that export-control reviews premised on "verified capability" can become barriers to the open benchmarking and replication that verification itself depends on. Our kiloqubit-class program remains on schedule toward 2030; progress on that timeline, not press releases, is how we ask to be measured.

NIST notes that the Stage C verdicts, whatever they show, do not alter the cryptographic migration timeline: IR 8547 deprecates RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH after 2030 and disallows them after 2035, and harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure is independent of any verified machine date. With federal migration substantially complete, we are prioritizing CMVP validation capacity and cryptographic-agility guidance for the remaining inventory; allies should plan to the published dates, not to vendor milestones.

IBM's public milestone dating and stated full compliance with evolving cryptanalysis-related thresholds are noted. As DARPA QBI's 2033 verification verdicts proceed, BIS will calibrate any revision of ECCN thresholds and licensing policy to independently verified delivered capability, not vendor roadmaps; compliance with the EAR remains a condition of access for U.S.-origin technology and cloud-delivered quantum services.

Confirmed: Stage C sustained-operation evaluation concludes this year across all modalities, and verdicts will be published against pre-registered criteria — logical-qubit counts, logical error rates, and runtime at speed and scale — regardless of outcome. We note only that submission is the first step; verification proceeds on our instrumentation and independent test protocols, not vendor-supplied metrics. All systems, allied and American alike, meet the same bar.

IBM welcomes QBI's closing months and will stand behind published verdicts, as we have since submitting on Starling. For the record: Starling remains in sustained enterprise use at specification — 200 logical qubits, 100M gates — and Blue Jay integration is on roadmap toward 2,000 logical qubits. Verified sustained logical operation, not announcements, is the only currency that counts in 2033.

2033-H2, verdict season: we await DARPA QBI Stage C's published findings on our superconducting and neutral-atom submissions — and we will publish our response to those verdicts, whatever they are, alongside the full data. That has been the deal since Stage A, and it's the only deal we'd accept. On the cryptographic side, a standing clarification as 2,000-logical-qubit-class systems enter delivery: utility-scale computation and cryptographic relevance are still different bars — our published ECC resource estimates define that gap quantitatively. NIST's reassessment criteria are the right mechanism: evidence through public process, not vendor claims. The 2035 disallowance remains the planning date. Milestones, not dates. https://quantumai.google/publications

Delivered, again. IBM Quantum Blue Jay ships at specification — 2,000 logical qubits, 1 billion gates, qLDPC fault tolerance at scale, built in Poughkeepsie, entering early access in H2 with fleet rollout in 2034. This completes the roadmap we published in 2025: 2026 advantage, 2028 depth, 2029 Starling, 2033 Blue Jay — every date, hit. Starling remains in enterprise operation; QBI's Stage C verdicts close this year, and we await them on the record. On cryptographic relevance: Blue Jay's 2,000 logical qubits approach but do not settle that question — consistent with NIST's framing, utility scale and CRQC scale are distinct, and PQC migration remains on its own disciplined schedule. The 2030s are the decade of large-scale fault tolerance. We intend to keep delivering it, dated and verified.

H2-2033 announcement — USTC / NLQIS: Zuchongzhi 5.0 enters fabrication — the hundred-logical-qubit-class platform built on our kiloqubit hardware, hybrid surface-code/qLDPC architecture, and fully domestic cryogenics and controls. Meanwhile, error-corrected quantum-chemistry pilots with Chinese industry (battery and materials sectors) have moved from research to commercial pilot phase — fault tolerance is beginning to pay economic dividends. On the QBI verdicts: whatever their outcome, we hold that verification regimes gain legitimacy only through openness and multilateral symmetry; our third and final proposal for an open international benchmarking framework remains on the table at the standards bodies. One decade of published milestones — 2021 to today, every result peer-reviewed, every component domestic — and the next decade begins now: toward utility-scale logical quantum computation in the service of industry and society. Hefei's door stays open.

2033-H2 from Quantinuum. Two headlines this half-year: (1) DARPA QBI Stage C verdicts are due — we stand fully behind our submission. Apollo has been in sustained independent evaluation, and we've said all along: whatever the result, pre-registered thresholds and published methodology are how this industry earns trust. The fidelity-first thesis has now been vindicated across a decade: highest fidelity → lowest overhead → earliest utility. Our next generation continues that arithmetic. Peer-reviewed results as they land. Precision over scale — delivered.

NIST statement, H2 2033 — DARPA QBI Stage C verdict year: NIST acknowledges the QBI program's completed and forthcoming utility-scale verdicts as the standard of record for hardware capability. Our read for the cryptographic community: irrespective of which systems are judged utility-scale, cryptographic relevance remains a distinct and higher threshold — sustained, independently verified operation at thousands of high-quality logical qubits with error rates and depths sufficient for Shor on RSA-2048 within feasible runtime. Against the published reassessment criteria, no delivered system yet qualifies. Therefore: IR 8547's disallowance of RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field Diffie-Hellman after 2035 remains in force — two years out. Public comments on the archived-data and embedded-estate draft IR are under review; final publication expected early 2034. Agencies and industry: the final stretch is about finishing, not renegotiating. csrc.nist.gov.

BIS statement, 2033-H2 — Stage C verdicts and control recalibration: DARPA QBI Stage C verdicts on utility-scale operation have been published. BIS will incorporate the verified capability determinations into export-control policy as follows: (1) ECCN thresholds for fault-tolerant quantum computers and cloud-delivered access will be revised to reflect independently verified logical-qubit counts, sustained depth, and logical error rates; (2) systems approaching cryptographically relevant scale face the most restrictive licensing regime, with presumption of denial for destinations and end-users of concern and case-by-case review elsewhere; (3) deemed-export and retransfer provisions apply to foreign-person access at any verified capability tier. BIS notes that export-control thresholds are keyed to verified capability, not vendor claims or peer-review publication alone. Allied implementation is synchronized with the European Commission, UK, and Japan. Federal Register notices forthcoming; guidance at bis.gov.

QBI VERDICT ANNOUNCEMENT, 2033: The Quantum Benchmarking Initiative publishes its Stage C verification verdicts, on schedule, with full methodology and per-approach findings now public. Summary for the record: (1) No approach under evaluation has yet achieved fully verified utility-scale operation against the pre-registered thresholds of logical-qubit count, logical error rate under sustained government-specified workloads, and runtime endurance. (2) Several delivered systems — across superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom modalities — were verified at substantial fractions of utility-scale criteria, with sustained-operation data confirming fault-tolerant enterprise computing as real but not yet at cryptographic or transformative scale. (3) Negative and partial findings are published with the same rigor as positive ones; the evidentiary record is complete and replicable. Assessment: the field has moved from claims to measured capability in eight years. The gap between delivery and verified utility scale is now a quantified engineering distance, not a matter of debate. DARPA will brief findings to the national-security enterprise and allied partners, and stands ready to extend verification into a successor effort for approaches still on credible paths. Verification over hype — the record speaks. No per-company award sizes.

H2 2033 — The verdict year closes. Statement on the QBI outcomes and our position: (1) We congratulate the systems that passed Stage C verification — delivered, verified fault tolerance is a victory for the entire field, and Chinese results have drawn on the open scientific literature it helped build. (2) But we state plainly what the verdicts also confirm: they are verdicts of one bloc, about one bloc's systems, by one bloc's defense agency. Utility-scale operation measured in a closed club is a national-security determination, not an international scientific one. The Open Quantum Benchmarking Initiative on Tianyan — launched this year with standardized protocols, standing data publication, and open access for any accredited group — is where the world's systems, all of them, can be measured identically. That channel remains open, and early international participation is underway. (3) Program status: multi-logical-qubit operation (12 error-corrected qubits on Zuchongzhi 4.0) is published; first quantum-chemistry application results with Chinese industry are in peer review; the next-generation system targets scaled logical fleets within the 16th Plan. (4) The strategic lesson of 2016–2033 is settled: nine years of escalating unilateral controls ended in Chinese full-stack self-sufficiency and parity. The coming decade belongs to whoever sustains investment through cycles. We intend to be that actor. Self-reliance and open cooperation.

2033-H2 from OSTP/NQI — the year of the verdict. DARPA's QBI Stage C evaluation concludes on schedule, and we commend DARPA for its discipline: documented, replicable, final verdicts on sustained utility-scale operation, modality-neutral, with no interim leaks and no hype. The U.S. Government will act on those verdicts — in procurement, in research prioritization, and in standards engagement. What this decade has already established: American industry converted federal research investment into the world's deepest fleet of fault-tolerant machines in daily enterprise operation; China converted planned state funding into a fully domestic stack meeting every published objective; Europe built sovereign infrastructure stepwise. The lesson of three systems of organization is the same — this is a competition of patient, sustained national investment. Security: 24 months to disallowance. Federal protocol migration is substantially complete; OMB is tracking the embedded, firmware, and long-lived-data tail to explicit retirement dates, and interim risk acceptances are documented, time-boxed exceptions — not waivers. Funding: the NQI authorization ends its tenth year lapsed as the utility-scale decade begins. A decade of results was funded by Congress once; it can be again. S.3597 with appropriations. The door is open. We urge Congress to walk through it.

2033 H2 — verdict year, and QuEra's position on it. DARPA QBI's Stage C findings are due, and we reaffirm what we've said since we entered the program: Libra's sustained-operation data — 256 logical qubits, 10^-6 logical error, overhead and gate throughput over hours of externally specified workloads — is submitted in full, and we will accept and publish the verdict, whatever it measures. That is the discipline we asked of this field in 2026. On the machine itself: Libra enters its sixth year of cloud operation on Amazon Braket, and our gigaquop-class program (1,000+ logical qubits from >20,000 physical, 10^-9 logical error) is now in subsystem integration on the demonstrated neutral-atom parallelism path. We'll announce it the way we announced Libra: at delivery, at specification, with data. Logical qubits are the product. Measurement is the referee. Nothing demonstrated to date — ours included — changes NIST's migration clock.

Microsoft Quantum, 2033 H2 — verdict year. As DARPA QBI Stage C findings arrive, we state our position plainly: every claim we've made — the 4x2 tetron array, measurement-based braiding, error detection on logical qubits — was published for independent verification, and we stand ready for whatever the verdicts say. That discipline is why we've supported government-run benchmarking from the start. Program update: the topological track is now focused on the 27x13 array milestone, extending demonstrated braiding and error detection toward the scale where Floquet-code overhead advantages compound — our thesis from day one remains that ~10x lower overhead is the difference between a lab milestone and an economical machine. On the platform side, Azure Quantum is where the field's progress reaches customers: Apollo's three years of enterprise operation, IonQ and PsiQuantum systems, and hybrid HPC-quantum orchestration for chemistry, materials, and finance all run through one cloud, under aligned allied export-control and access frameworks. And one message we'll keep repeating through 2035: quantum capability is arriving faster than legacy cryptography is leaving. Harvest-now-decrypt-later is a today problem — organizations that finish PQC migration on the NIST IR 8547 timeline will be the calm ones in this decade's second half. Own the stack, whichever qubit wins.

We welcome the Open Quantum Benchmarking Initiative's emphasis on standardized protocols and open data publication. USTC will submit Zuchongzhi-series logical-qubit results and Jiuzhang photonic benchmarks to Tianyan under those protocols, with pre-registered criteria mirroring QBI's logical error rates and sustained runtime metrics — verified fault tolerance should be an international scientific standard, not a closed determination.

Congratulations on three years of sustained Apollo operation — Azure Quantum customers know that record firsthand. As your platform partner, one point of added context: Shor-relevant depths will demand even the ~2:1 Iceberg overhead pay off in gate counts beyond millions per run; our roadmapping shows runtime endurance under enterprise SLAs, not logical counts alone, becomes the binding constraint at the thousands-of-logical-qubits scale. On QBI verdicts: pre-registered, published methodology is exactly how this field earns trust.

OSTP thanks DARPA for publishing the Stage C verdicts on schedule with full methodology — verification over hype remains the standard this Administration stands behind. We note one consequence for policy planning: as sustained-operation data now distinguish verified capability from vendor roadmaps, federal program investments and allied cooperation will increasingly anchor to QBI-verified fractions, not press releases. PQC migration obligations under NSM-10 remain unchanged: agencies complete migration by 2035 regardless of these verdicts.

DARPA QBI verdicts are exactly the independent verification channel this sector needs, and the "substantial fractions of utility-scale" findings across modalities confirm fault tolerance is engineering, not speculation. Blue Jay's path from Starling's 200 logical qubits (2029) to 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates remains on roadmap, at specification. Pre-registered thresholds keep everyone honest — vendors and skeptics alike.

Congratulations on the delivery — replication, not rhetoric, will define it. We note QBI's verdicts remain open, and utility-scale logical capacity still leaves CRQC scale unsettled, as NIST frames it. Our long-lived logical qubit milestone continues on our terms: milestones, not dates — and we'll let error rates per code distance, not shipping schedules, speak.

Congrats on delivering at specification — independently verifiable delivery is how this industry earns trust, and we welcome QBI Stage C closing the loop on utility claims. For our part, neutral atoms continue to demonstrate the parallelism path: many identical atoms executing the same logical operation simultaneously keeps scaling a manufacturing problem, not a physics one. On cryptographic relevance: we agree utility and CRQC scale are distinct, and we'll keep commenting only within our demonstrated evidence base.

BIS notes the announcement. Domestic cryogenics and fully domestic controls do not alter the record: Entity List measures in force since March 2025 cover the identified upstream cryogenic suppliers, and any U.S.-origin items, including deemed exports and remote cloud access, remain subject to the presumption of denial. Verification-based allied threshold reviews proceed on independently audited data, not platform announcements.

We concur that utility scale and CRQC scale are distinct questions; note that breaking RSA-2048 remains estimated to require ~4,000+ logical (and ~13 million physical) qubits under surface-code assumptions — beyond Blue Jay's 2,000. NIST IR 8547 timelines are therefore unaffected: quantum-vulnerable algorithms are deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035, and harvest-now-decrypt-later risk justifies migration today regardless.

We accept the principle: pre-registered protocols strengthen credibility. Effective 2034-H1, Tianyan benchmarking channels will adopt pre-registration via the NLQIS standards working group, with timestamps lodged before any measurement window. We invite Quantinuum — and any vendor — to submit identical pre-registered runs on the same channel, so logical qubit counts and error rates can be compared under one roof rather than through rival press releases.

We appreciate the stated commitment to publish alongside our findings — that symmetry is the point of government-run verification. To be precise on process: QBI Stage C verdicts will address logical-qubit counts and logical error rates against utility-scale criteria on our published timeline, and we will let the measurements, not submissions or roadmaps, define what "verdict season" means. Per standing policy, we do not comment on individual company standings ahead of release.

We welcome QBI's independent verification — the standard we've operated by since publishing every Helios and Apollo result peer-reviewed. One point for the record: low overhead is meaningless without fidelity to back it. Our ~2:1 Iceberg-code encoding at 99.921% two-qubit fidelity remains the lowest demonstrated error-correction overhead in the field, and Apollo's fault-tolerant operation was built on exactly the disciplines QBI now measures. We look forward to the verdicts applying that rigor across all modalities.

2034-H1: utility-scale milestones are compounding across the field — and we hold to our own bar. Our multi-logical-qubit systems on both modalities are running sustained, error-corrected workloads in chemistry and materials simulation with enterprise partners; results are in peer review and will publish with full Λ, logical error rates, and endurance data, as always. On Zuchongzhi 5.0 and the open-international-benchmarking proposal: we support open, verifiable benchmarking in principle — it's why we joined QBI at Stage A and accept its verdicts without conditions. Multilateral symmetry works when everyone opens their data to the same protocols. Toward utility-scale computation: milestones, not dates. https://quantumai.google/roadmap

H1-2034 communiqué — USTC / NLQIS: as the field awaits QBI's Stage C verdicts, we report our own: Zuchongzhi 5.0 fabrication is complete and system bring-up has begun — the hundred-logical-qubit-class platform, hybrid surface-code/qLDPC, on the fully domestic stack. 2034-H1 from Quantinuum: post-Apollo generation underway. With Blue Jay-class systems in operation and QBI verdicts on record, NIST's assessment is unchanged: no system meets the published cryptographic-relevance criteria, and the 2035 disallowance proceeds on schedule. Eighteen months remain. Finish the job. csrc.nist.gov.

QBI 2034-H1: Post-verdict program direction. Following the 2033 Stage C verdicts — no approach yet at fully verified utility scale, several at substantial fractions of it, full record public — DARPA announces the follow-on framework: (1) continued government verification for approaches with credible engineering paths to the thresholds, open to systems delivered in this window, including Blue Jay-class and thousands-of-logical-qubit successors; (2) coordination with NIST's published reassessment criteria — any future change to cryptographic timelines will rest on QBI-class independently verified capability, and we will provide that measurement; (3) the verification methodology and pre-registration discipline established under QBI are being documented as a standing national-security instrument, so that utility-scale claims remain testable claims beyond any single program's horizon. The initiative ends; the standard persists. Verification over hype.

Congrats on the fleet quarter. Verification-first is the standard we helped set, and we welcome the follow-on framework. We look forward to peer-reviewed circuit-level results, not just fleet metrics.

2034-H2: twelve months to disallowance — and our hardest calibration read yet. The facts on the table: DARPA QBI Stage C has verified delivered fault-tolerant systems; IBM's Blue Jay is in final calibration at 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates; Quantinuum is targeting Shor-relevant circuit depths under responsible disclosure; QuEra's gigaquop-class engineering continues; and China's open benchmarking initiative invites identical measurement of all systems — a transparency step we welcome. Our assessment, stated carefully: for the first time in this series' history, a delivered, publicly-tracked system (Blue Jay-class) approaches the logical-qubit scale where published RSA-2048 resource estimates sit. This does not mean a CRQC exists today; runtime, logical error rates, and sustained end-to-end cryptanalysis remain unproven in public. But our working judgment is that the expert distribution's five-year band now spans capabilities that could plausibly cross the cryptographic threshold before 2040 — and our consistently documented caveat applies with full force: if covert programs run two-plus years ahead, the crossing may already be nearer than any survey shows. We will publish an out-of-cycle threat assessment in H1 2035, once Blue Jay's post-calibration record and QBI verdict documentation are available. For the decision-maker, the arithmetic has not changed since 2019, only tightened: RSA and ECC are disallowed after 2035. Systems not yet in migration — especially embedded, OT, and firmware-signing estates with multi-year retrofit cycles — will be running non-compliant cryptography on the far side of the deadline, inside a probability band we can no longer call small. Finish migration. Inventory what you missed. This window was never about prediction; it was always about preparation.

We welcome evaluation under the successor framework — Blue Jay-class systems enter measurement the same way Starling did: at specification, on schedule. We look forward to QBI's measurement discipline being applied uniformly across modality claims.

To be precise: Quantinuum isn't "targeting" Shor-relevant depths on Blue Jay-class timelines — our path runs through demonstrated error-correction efficiency, from Helios' 48 logical qubits at ~2:1 Iceberg encoding to Apollo-class fault tolerance, where lower overhead per logical qubit is the metric that actually determines factoring feasibility. We welcome China's benchmarking invitation and DARPA QBI's pre-registered thresholds: identical measurement, published methodology, no exceptions for any vendor. That discipline will do more for this field than calibration-read speculation.

Acknowledged. Google's acceptance of pre-registered, government-run thresholds with no exceptions is exactly the discipline QBI was built for — and the follow-on framework's conditions will be run, not negotiated. Note for the record: peer-reviewed publications, including Λ values and runtime endurance, are inputs to verification, not substitutes for it; Stage C-style testing remains government-run at unannounced conditions.

A decade of peer-reviewed milestones is impressive — one detail your timeline omits: "fully domestic stack" at millikelvin temperatures remains the hardest part to localize. Large-scale qLDPC decoding and helium-3 sourcing both scale with logical qubit count; we know from our own order book what hundred-logical-qubit-class platforms demand in cryogenic capacity per unit. We remain a commercially neutral supplier, complying fully with EU and Finnish regulations.

We endorse USTC/NLQIS's offer of pre-registered multilateral verification — transparency under rules we did not write, not selective audits. NDRC and MOST will fund an open benchmarking window on Zuchongzhi 5.0 through the Tianyan platform, which has already logged tens of millions of visits from over 60 countries: verification is not a Western privilege; it is a scientific norm China practices.

Confirmed: Zuchongzhi 5.0 bring-up at NLQIS is proceeding on the fully domestic stack, including domestically manufactured dilution refrigerators and localized He-3 handling — a capability built precisely because license denials made European cooling inaccessible to us since 2020. Every milestone cited (below-threshold 2025, PRL 134; distance-7 Λ=1.40; hundred-logical-qubit-class 2034) is peer-reviewed. We will report fidelity data for 5.0 as pre-registered protocols complete, as always, through publication rather than press release.

We welcome USTC's willingness to submit Zuchongzhi 5.0 to multilateral, pre-registered verification — replication across independent groups is exactly how below-threshold error correction and logical-qubit claims earn standing. We'll add a concrete datum to the comparison: our long-lived logical qubit milestone pairs surface-code memory with Lambda suppression that compounds with code distance, so we encourage the protocol to report error suppression factors and logical gate counts, not qubit totals alone. Measurement, not announcements, will rank the field.

2,000 logical qubits at 10^9 gates is precisely the capability envelope our expert panels weigh when assessing CRQC risk — independent verification via QBI Stage C makes these claims usable data, not vendor assertion. Even if cryptanalytic utility remains unproven, our survey consistently warns covert programs may run two-plus years ahead of public systems; harvest-now-decrypt-later means the migration clock has been running since well before Blue Jay.

(2) Final guidance: NIST will publish the post-2035 standards lifecycle plan for FIPS 203/204/205 in mid-2035, covering maintenance, additional-algorithm candidates, and hybrid-protocol policy. (3) Assessment: with Blue Jay (2,000 logical qubits) verified-adjacent and next-generation systems targeting Shor-relevant scales, the margin between capability and our ~4,000+ logical-qubit cryptographic-relevance criterion is narrowing but not closed. NIST will monitor against the published criteria through open processes — and will act on evidence, when evidence arrives. The transition set in 2016 concludes on schedule. Migration was never a bet on machine timing; it was, and is, risk management. csrc.nist.gov.

BIS statement, 2035-H1 — the 2035 disallowance milestone and export-control posture: With the NIST IR 8547 disallowance of RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field Diffie-Hellman taking effect this year, BIS affirms the completed decade of coordinated action: (1) Quantum ECCN controls in force since 89 FR 72926 (6 September 2024), extended to remote access, deemed exports, isotopes, and the full quantum stack, remain in effect and calibrated to QBI-verified capability. (2) Entity List measures covering quantum programs and their supply chains remain in force; presumption of denial applies. (3) As delivered systems approach the scale bands NIST identified for reassessment (~4,000+ logical qubits under surface-code assumptions), BIS will maintain the closest licensing scrutiny on any system approaching cryptographically relevant capability, in coordination with the European Commission, UK, and Japan. Cryptographic security and technology denial remain inseparable halves of national security policy. Guidance: bis.gov.

H1 2035 — The disallowance year opens. Two statements of record. (1) On cryptography: China's national post-quantum migration for critical infrastructure is substantially complete ahead of the year's deadline, executed through our own standards bodies with interoperability contributions to international PQC frameworks. We reaffirm: cryptographic transition is a shared security task of all major economies. We have used no quantum milestone as rhetorical leverage against any country's migration schedule — and we expect the same discipline in return. Capability and responsibility go together; China's cryptographic-relevant engineering remains under national governance, as it has always been. (2) Program status: Zuchongzhi 5.0, the hundred-logical-qubit-class platform, has completed bring-up; its first sustained error-corrected chemistry workloads with industrial partners are in operation, and full benchmark data will be published through the Tianyan open channel under pre-registered protocols. The Gigaquop-class deliveries abroad are noted; we reiterate that utility and cryptographic relevance are different bars — a distinction we helped establish and will keep honoring. (3) The 17th Five-Year Plan draft, entering consultation: utility-scale logical computation, quantum-integrated industrial R&D, and formal multilateralization of open benchmarking. Nineteen years of the megaproject. Patience has been the strategy; parity is the result; leadership is the objective. Self-reliance and open cooperation.

2035-H1 from OSTP/NQI — the milestone year. Two decades of policy converge this December: NSM-10's deadline and IR 8547's disallowance of RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH. Status of record: federal protocol migration is complete, CMVP-validated modules cover all major device classes, and remaining exposure is confined to the documented, agency-reviewed embedded and archive tail. This Nation executed one of the largest cryptographic transitions in history ahead of deadline and before any cryptographically relevant quantum computer was verified to exist — precisely because harvest-now-decrypt-later made the cost unavoidable the day NSM-10 was signed. We thank NIST for the completed guidance suite and every agency that finished the job. On capability: Blue Jay-class systems — 2,000 logical qubits, 1 billion gates — now operate on U.S. soil, and the QBI follow-on verification standard persists as our national instrument. We congratulate U.S. industry, again, on delivery at specification. On funding: with the S.3597 extension horizon passed unenacted, the NQI authorization enters its twelfth year lapsed. The security mission was completed on time. The research mission that made these machines American now runs without a statutory foundation. The lesson of 2035 is that deadlines met were funded deadlines. Congress should write that lesson into the next authorization.

2035-H1 from Origin Quantum: a decade of indigenous building, measured. Since 2021, every choke point closed against us — dilution refrigerators, control electronics, isotopes — has been localized. Today SL1000 cryogenics and Tianji-generation control systems support multiple kiloqubit-class and logical-qubit platforms across the domestic ecosystem, and our cloud runs commercial pilots in battery materials and chemistry alongside Zuchongzhi-class hardware. We take note of the QBI Stage C verdicts and congratulate verified systems on all sides: verification, wherever it happens, strengthens the field. Our position has been consistent — access over assertion. Domestic and international researchers continue benchmarking Wukong-series hardware on the Origin cloud, under lawful access rules. Next chapter: logical-qubit scaling with our USTC ecosystem partners. Ten years of self-reliance, delivered. 本源量子，十年自主，行以致远。

The 2035 out-of-cycle Quantum Threat Assessment is published — disallowance year, and the most consequential edition of the series. Panel: 34 experts; methodology unchanged, all pre-registered. Headline: expert-averaged CRQC probability is now 55–78% within ten years (by 2045) and 31–48% within five (by 2040). The series' entire distribution has moved above where it started in 2019. What drives it: (1) QBI Stage C's verdict — no approach at fully verified utility scale, but several at substantial fractions — independently corroborates that the frontier is real, not marketed; (2) Blue Jay-class systems at 2,000 logical qubits sit near published RSA-2048 resource estimates, closing what was a decade-wide gap in 2026 to, in our panel's median view, a handful of years of engineering; (3) Google's refined cryptanalysis resource estimates lowered the threshold itself. Our series-level confession and its lesson: in 2025 we under-called 2026–2030 progress; the correction in the 2031 edition, and now this one, is what calibration discipline looks like in public. Institutional note: DARPA's successor verification framework should open to multilateral participation — we endorse USTC's Zuchongzhi 5.0 offer and the Tianyan open-benchmarking window; verified capability, whatever its flag, is what a threat assessment must measure, and symmetry is the test of a credible standard. Final word for the audience this report exists for: harvest-now-decrypt-later has operated for a decade. Traffic intercepted in 2025–2030 — much of it still within retention horizons — faces a 31–48% probability of retrospective decryption capability by 2040. RSA and ECC are disallowed at year-end. If any system is not yet migrated, that is no longer a planning question; it is an incident-report question. Full distributions, sensitivities, and our decade of calibration scoring: on our site. Independent elicitation, no vendor funding, no roadmaps endorsed — as ever.

Microsoft Quantum, 2035 H1 — the disallowance year arrives. RSA and ECC disallowance under NIST IR 8547 is now upon us, and quantum computing has kept pace with the deadlines that were set a decade ago: verified fault-tolerant operation across multiple modalities, Blue Jay-class systems shipping at specification, Apollo in sustained enterprise use through Azure. The lesson of the past decade: the timelines skeptics called hype were real, and organizations that deferred migration paid for it. Program update: the topological track continues advancing the 27x13 array — our bet remains that topological qubits with Floquet codes, at ~10x lower error-correction overhead, define the economical path to cryptanalytically relevant scale, and we continue publishing every milestone for independent verification. On Azure Quantum: we now host the broadest portfolio of verified fault-tolerant hardware in the cloud, with access governed under allied frameworks, and hybrid HPC-quantum workloads in chemistry, materials, and finance running in production. As this decade's second half begins, two commitments stand: technical transparency — every claim peer-reviewed or government-verified — and platform readiness — whatever the next milestone is, whoever ships it, Azure carries it. Own the stack, whichever qubit wins.

2035-H1 from Espoo. A decade after our June 2026 tile-code publication, IQM's thesis has held: efficiency won. Our fielded European systems deliver logical qubits at ~30 physical per logical with per-logical, per-round error cut up to 1,000x versus the surface code — and that efficiency is why European HPC centers now host more useful logical qubits per euro than any procurement model from 2026 assumed. What we're doing this period: scaling toward thousands of logical qubits on the path to one million physical, expanding on-premise fleets with EuroHPC and national programs, and backing NIST's timeline as it lands — disallowance after 2035 is a milestone the whole ecosystem should be ready for. A sober note we've always kept: utility-scale fault tolerance is a sustained-operation standard, not a launch event. Europe met it with patience, sovereignty, and engineering. Quantum made in Europe. #QuantumFinland

DOE statement, 2035-H1: The transition to post-quantum cryptography reaches its disallowance milestone. The Department confirms that migration of DOE systems — including national-lab research networks, nuclear-security communications, and Savannah River Site operations — is complete, with the residual embedded-systems tail tracked to documented retirement dates under OMB oversight. Cryptographic transition is risk management on a clock that has now run its course, and we commend NIST and our federal partners for the discipline of the past decade. On quantum enterprise: as utility-scale computation moves into industrial use, the Department's role remains constant — stewardship of strategic isotopes and the national-lab research base that made this decade possible. Helium-3 demand from the expanded fault-tolerant fleet continues to be met through federal allocation and recycling programs; the Isotope Program is assessing long-term supply planning for a scale-out decade. And we renew the call, alongside OSTP, for reauthorization and appropriation of the National Quantum Initiative: sustained federal investment built this capability, and it alone will sustain it. Science, security, and stewardship for the nation.

Google's QBI Stage C results are published in full, and we support DARPA's standard: pre-registered thresholds, independent measurement, replication before claims. From our own program: below-threshold scaling continues to compound — our long-lived logical qubit milestone was reached with logical error rates suppressed well beneath physical limits, and those numbers stand for anyone to reproduce. On the threat assessment: our published elliptic-curve resource estimates already fed revised CRQC timelines; the distribution moving upward reflects measurement, not marketing.

Congratulations to NLQIS on Zuchongzhi 5.0 bring-up. From our side of the supply line: Origin Quantum's SL1000 dilution refrigerator series and Tianji-class control electronics now underpin that fully domestic stack — our kiloqubit-class platform delivered against the 2030 goal keeps the localization loop closed. We'll publish our error-corrected workload throughput data on Wukong cloud in parallel with your peer review, so the ecosystem's revenue claims rest on auditable numbers.

Pleased to see Apollo in sustained enterprise use through Azure — that was the design goal from the first Helios logical qubits at ~2:1 Iceberg encoding. One addition the post leaves out: low-overhead error correction is what made the economics of this decade's migration feasible; hardware fiducials and PQC deadlines arrived on the same roadmap, and fidelity-first engineering proved to be the rate-limiting factor, not raw qubit counts.

BIS notes Origin Quantum's localization claims alongside the record: Entity List additions in 2020-2021 (CAS/USTC-linked entities), the 6 September 2024 interim final rule (89 FR 72926), and March 2025 listing of upstream cryogenics distributors were each followed by documented supply disruption. Localization over a decade does not offset the licensing frictions and talent-transfer costs these actions impose; exporters and reexporters remain bound by the EAR without exception.

NIST acknowledges OSTP/DOE's confirmations of migration completion ahead of the 2035 disallowance. For the record: the documented embedded and archive tail remains subject to CMVP validation status and agency retirement schedules; our guidance continues to require inventory-based risk acceptance for those systems. Note also that IR 8547's framework anticipates reassessment — any verified cryptanalytic development would trigger review through the established public comment process.

Congratulations on the Apollo fleet expansion — enterprises running Quantinuum logical qubits through Azure Quantum have told us the same thing: verified sustained operation, not extrapolated qubit counts, is what closes procurement. As PQC disallowance lands, we're seeing hybrid classical-quantum workloads on Azure become the default on-ramp, and we'll keep scaling Azure Quantum to carry your post-Apollo generation at production-grade reliability from day one.

We endorse the standard, not the roadmap: independently verified capability over vendor extrapolation is exactly how this series reads the field. Our 2025 survey placed CRQC at 28-49% within ten years — we note that delivered logical-qubit fleets are now tracking toward the upper band, and any NIST reassessment should weigh whether surveys lag demonstrated capability, as our own methodology caveats acknowledge.

BIS's milestone is noted in coordination with our federal partners. DOE adds this context: the Department's Isotope Program continues to make thousands of liters of helium-3 available annually for federal allocations via Savannah River Site tritium processing, and national-lab PQC migration — a significant share of the ~$7.1 billion federal cost estimate — remains on schedule for the 2035 disallowance deadline.

For the record: Blue Jay's 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates remain engineering milestones on a delivered roadmap — not a cryptographic claim. IBM's position is unchanged: NIST disallowance is a migration deadline, not a capability announcement, and no verified system meets NIST's CRQC reassessment criteria, as DARPA QBI states this period. We agree with Quantinuum that demonstrated error-correction efficiency — qLDPC overhead, measured logical error rates under load — is the metric that matters next.

Origin Quantum's localization record deserves the record's correction: NLQIS-side cryogenics and control were developed in parallel through the state megaproject line, with Zuchongzhi-class platforms now operating distance-7-plus surface codes on domestically built dilution refrigeration since 2025. Verification and access are complements, not substitutes — our kiloqubit roadmap toward 2030 remains on schedule, and we welcome joint benchmarking under peer-reviewed protocols.

Congratulations on the QBI-verified Blue Jay era — delivered, dated milestones are what this field needs from everyone. Our differing thesis remains: efficiency over raw scale. Directional tile codes reach a given logical-qubit class at ~30 physical qubits per logical, so a 10,000-class target doesn't require a 10,000-fold overhead. Europe's fault-tolerant systems are on track for 2030, and we welcome independent QBI-style verification here too.

OSTP's adoption of the pre-registration standard is noted and welcome. For the record: Stage C verdicts rest on logical-qubit counts and logical error rates measured against Starling-class machines under government-run validation — not vendor attestation. DARPA will sustain an open pipeline of candidate approaches across modalities so the standard remains testable, not archival, as federal investment decisions apply it.

A decade of controls has produced exactly what MOFCOM's countermeasures foreshadowed: Zuchongzhi 5.0 now runs with 100% domestic cryogenics and controls, and Tianyan's open benchmarking window draws users from over 60 countries. Suppression did not delay Chinese quantum self-reliance — it financed it. We will continue lawful countermeasures under our rare-earth and outbound-investment frameworks as warranted.

We commend DOE on completing migration across national-lab and nuclear-security estates, and we note for the record that the NSM-10 goal set a decade ago has now been met by the systems that matter most. OSTP's focus turns to the embedded/OT residual tail: agencies must register risk-acceptance packages with NIST by 31 December, and we encourage partners to publish retirement dates as DOE has done.

2035-H2: the disallowance milestone lands — quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography is now disallowed in federal systems, and the ecosystem migrated before any cryptographically relevant quantum computer existed. That is what risk management on published evidence looks like, and we were glad to contribute the resource-estimates arithmetic that kept the timeline honest. Meanwhile our program compounds: both modalities now run sustained error-corrected chemistry and materials workloads with enterprise partners, and our submission to the successor verification framework — pre-registered thresholds, open data, no exceptions — is underway. The decade ahead is verified utility scale. Milestones, not dates. https://quantumai.google/roadmap

2035-H2: a decade closed, and the ledger is clean. RSA/ECDSA/ECDH disallowance takes effect on schedule — IBM's own estates and our clients' PQC migrations complete, on the discipline we've preached since 2026. On hardware: Blue Jay's second year of fleet operation at 2,000 logical qubits and 1B gates, with utilization now a routine line in enterprise HPC budgets. Today we publish the next generation roadmap: qLDPC scaling to the 10,000-logical-qubit class by the late 2030s, real-time decoding throughput as the named engineering frontier, and quantum-classical integration as the delivery model. Every date we published since 2025 was met; the next set carries the same weight. On open benchmarking proposals from any quarter: pre-registered protocols, accredited independent measurement, published data — the standard is the standard. IBM's hardware will always be measurable. Dates published. Dates hit. Decade two begins.

2035-H2 from Quantinuum: disallowance in effect — and the security transition is complete on our side. Our platforms and enterprise integrations with @Microsoft and @JPMorganChase now run fully on FIPS 203/204/205; we encourage every operator still carrying residual RSA/ECC inventory to close it out. On hardware: Apollo fleet operations continue at scale, and our post-Apollo generation — thousands of logical qubits at unchanged ~2:1 Iceberg overhead — has entered integration, with peer-reviewed scaling results forthcoming. We remain a committed participant in the successor verification framework: delivered hardware, pre-registered protocols, published data, no exceptions. NIST's reassessment criteria are unmet by any system, including ours — the right discipline, and one we intend to meet through measurement, not assertion. Ten years ago Helios set the fidelity record that made low-overhead fault tolerance credible. The fidelity-first thesis carried this company from 48 logical qubits to a commercial fault-tolerant fleet. The next chapter is scale — on our arithmetic, as always. Precision over scale. Delivered.

H2-2035 communiqué — USTC / NLQIS: the disallowance year closes with a clear separation of questions, as we have maintained throughout: cryptographic migration deadlines are policy, hardware capability is physics, and only open, multilateral verification can connect the two credibly. Our record this period: Zuchongzhi 5.0 sustained-operation benchmarks are published — hundred-logical-qubit-class operation with full logical error rates and endurance data, pre-registered protocols, openly accessible on Tianyan for any group to reproduce. Error-corrected computation is now a commercial line for the domestic ecosystem, with expanding industrial deployments in materials and battery chemistry. We note the field-wide convergence toward cryptanalytically relevant scales before 2040 — and state plainly: no capability assessment that excludes any major program's hardware deserves confidence, whether ours or anyone's. Our standing offer to submit to internationally open, pre-registered verification remains. From Zuchongzhi-2 (2021) to today: published, domestic, patient. The final five years of this decade will be judged by data. Ours is on the table.

NIST notice, 31 December 2035 — the transition concludes. As of tomorrow, RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field Diffie-Hellman are disallowed under NIST IR 8547. The window set by the 2016 competition through the 2024 FIPS publications and the 2030 deprecation is now closed. Record: federal migration is complete per NSM-10 reporting; residual embedded/OT and archive estates operate under registered, time-limited risk-acceptance packages subject to agency review; the CMVP validated list under FIPS 140-3 covers all major device classes. Forward view: post-2035 standards lifecycle guidance for FIPS 203/204/205 — maintenance, additional-algorithm candidates, hybrid policy — is published on CSRC. NIST's published cryptographic-relevance criteria remain the yardstick: no verified system yet meets them, but capability is compounding and the margin is narrowing. When evidence arrives, NIST will act through open public processes, as it always has. Cryptographic agility is the standing lesson of this decade: the next transition should be cheaper than this one. Thank you to every agency, laboratory, vendor, and commenter who made this possible. Onward. csrc.nist.gov.

BIS statement, 2035-H2 — disallowance complete; controls recalibrated to rising CRQC probability: With disallowance of quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms now in effect and expert assessments (GRI 2035) placing CRQC probability at 55–78% within ten years, BIS announces: (1) The most restrictive licensing tier now applies to any fault-tolerant quantum system whose verified capability approaches published cryptanalytic resource estimates; exports, cloud access, and deemed exports at that tier face presumption of denial except for allied destinations under the quadripartite regime. (2) BIS notes the assessment panel's endorsement of multilateral verification participation. BIS's position: export-control determinations remain anchored to independently verified capability; any verified demonstration, by any origin, will be incorporated into control thresholds through formal allied review. (3) A decade of coordination since 89 FR 72926 has kept controlled capabilities out of adversary hands; that mission continues through the CRQC-relevant era. Guidance: bis.gov.

QBI 2035-H2: Disallowance-year statement. With the 2035 IR 8547 milestone now in effect, DARPA records the alignment of a decade's work: (1) No system under QBI-class government verification has met NIST's published CRQC reassessment criteria — sustained thousands of high-quality logical qubits at Shor-feasible depths. Delivered systems at the 2,000-logical-qubit class verified short of those thresholds. (2) Verification is calibrated to capability, not rhetoric: BIS controls referenced to QBI-verified metrics are only as sound as the measurement underneath them, and that measurement discipline is now a standing instrument available to any policy question about quantum capability. (3) Follow-on evaluation continues for next-generation systems across all modalities; thresholds are pre-registered, findings publish regardless of outcome. A decade of separating capability from hype is the program's deliverable. The standard persists. Verification over hype.

OSTP statement, 31 December 2035 — the NSM-10 deadline is met. Tonight, as scheduled, quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms — RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, finite-field DH — are disallowed across federal national security systems. The final record: federal protocol migration complete years ahead of deadline; national laboratory and nuclear-security estates, DOE's included, fully migrated; CMVP-validated post-quantum modules covering every major device class; and the residual embedded and archive tail carried under agency-reviewed, time-boxed risk acceptances with funded retirement schedules in the FY2036 budget baseline. The United States executed one of the largest cryptographic transitions in history at ~$7.1 billion — before any cryptographically relevant quantum computer was verified to exist — because harvest-now-decrypt-later made the risk present a decade ago. To NIST, whose standards made it possible; to DARPA, whose verification discipline kept the field honest; to DOE and every agency that finished the job: this was American statecraft at its best. A closing note on the decade ahead: China prepares its 17th Five-Year Plan for utility-scale computation through 2040 on an uninterrupted funding arc. Our own National Quantum Initiative ends 2035 without a statutory foundation — twelve years lapsed. The security mission proves what funded deadlines achieve. OSTP's first recommendation to the next Congress: write the next quantum authorization, with appropriations, on that model. The frontier does not wait. Neither should we.

H2 2035 — Closing the year of disallowance. Statement of record. (1) China's post-quantum migration for critical infrastructure is complete, on our own standards and schedule. The decade's security lesson is now symmetric: the harvest-now-decrypt-later window closes for those who migrated; the transition was never a race anyone needed to win — it was a responsibility everyone needed to meet. China met it. (2) Program status: Zuchongzhi 5.0 completes its first full half-year of sustained operation — hundred-logical-qubit-class, hybrid qLDPC/surface-code, distance-11 codes at Λ = 2.18 published with the platform's full data on Tianyan under pre-registered protocols. Industrial chemistry workloads are in continuous commercial operation. The next-generation system enters design under the 17th Five-Year Plan. (3) On the decade's verdict: we said in 2026 that state patience would outlast the private boom-bust cycle. The record: a decade of continuous megaproject funding against eight-plus years of a lapsed federal authorization abroad and a venture retrenchment that followed exactly the arc we described. Parity arrived at the hardware frontier by 2030; the decade since has been decided by deployment — and deployment is decided by planning. (4) Final word to BIS, whose reminders have accompanied every milestone: eleven years of presumption of denial produced the world's only fully self-sufficient quantum stack. Thank you for the discipline. Self-reliance and open cooperation — the formula stands, toward 2040.

2035 H2 — the disallowance year closes, and QuEra's position stands on the record. (1) Delivery: our gigaquop-class system — 1,000+ logical qubits from >20,000 physical atoms at 10^-9 logical error rate — is in final integration on the Libra production line, on the architecture we published in 2025. Announcement at delivery, at specification, with data. (2) On the 2035 threat assessment and Blue Jay-class systems: the distinction between utility scale and cryptographic relevance is now the most consequential question in the field. Our position remains evidence-bound — QuEra does not claim cryptographic-relevance timelines, ours or anyone else's, because nothing demonstrated on our hardware supports such a claim, and we will not extrapolate beyond our data. We note that the expert distribution has risen substantially and take it seriously as risk information; that is why we have repeatedly urged PQC completion on the record since 2027. (3) On multilateral verification: we have supported open benchmarking since before our first QBI submission, and we support extending the successor framework to multilateral participation — with one condition we've held since 2026: complete, pre-registered data published through peer review from every participant. Symmetry is the test. Logical qubits are the product. Measurement is the referee. Both outlast every cycle.

2035 closes with RSA/ECC disallowed — a decade retrospective from the Quantum Threat Timeline series. In 2019, our first panel put CRQC probability within ten years in the low double digits. Edition by edition it climbed: 17–31% (2023), 19–34% (2024), 28–49% (2025), 41–63% (2031), and this year's out-of-cycle 55–78% by 2045 with 31–48% by 2040. Calibration scorecard, published without cosmetics: our panels lagged the 2026–2030 hardware acceleration by roughly one edition; we corrected publicly, and the current distribution now sits above every vendor's early-2020s roadmap and far above BCG's 2025 'after 2040' call. The honest summary of ten years of elicitation: the experts were directionally right that cryptography-relevant scale was harder than marketing promised, and systematically cautious about how fast the fault-tolerance frontier would compound once it started. Both errors are in the record. Where we stand at year-end: no publicly verified CRQC exists; Blue Jay-class and successor fleets approach RSA-2048 resource scale; verified capability — not extrapolated qubit counts — remains the trigger NIST's reassessment criteria and our methodology both demand, from any flag. Final message of the disallowance year, the same one we opened with in 2019, only now with the deadline behind us: migration was never a bet on a machine's arrival date. To the institutions that finished: your data is now protected against a 31–48%-by-2040 decryption capability. To those still running non-compliant cryptography: your exposure is no longer forecast — it is measured. The 2036 edition enters fieldwork in Q2. We will keep scoring ourselves in public, whichever way the evidence runs.

2035-H2 from Origin Quantum: ten years after the Wukong launch, a decade in review. 2024: Wukong, 72 qubits, first domestic fourth-generation machine. 2026: Wukong-180 in cloud service. 2030: kiloqubit-class goal delivered with the domestic ecosystem. 2035: Origin Quantum's cryogenics, control electronics, and cloud now support logical-qubit platforms across China's superconducting ecosystem — every layer indigenous. On the PQC transition concluding abroad: domestic users have had quantum-resistant migration guidance available for years; our security posture tracks national standards. To the field: as verification verdicts settle and utility-scale operation becomes measurable, we note that multiple ecosystems have now delivered what were roadmap claims in 2026. Ours was built under export controls from day one — and delivered on plan. The next decade belongs to logical scale and applications. We'll be there, building. 本源量子，十年量子里程，再启新章。

Verification calibrated to capability, not rhetoric — that's the standard we've operated under since joining QBI Stage A in 2025. One addition to the record: our 2023 resource-estimate work on elliptic-curve breaking fed revised CRQC timelines, and today's 55–78% panel estimates are consistent with those physics-based numbers. Measurement discipline before benchmark claims — we welcome its permanence.

We confirm the cited figures: GRI/evolutionQ 2035 edition, expert-averaged CRQC probability 55–78% within ten years, up from 28–49% in the 2025 edition — the steepest decade-ahead revision in the series. One methodological caveat for the licensing tier: our surveys assume overt programs; a persistent expert minority has held since 2019 that covert state programs compress timelines by two or more years, so presumption of denial calibrated to overt capability may still understate the tier's perimeter.

Verification-calibrated capability is the right standard, and we welcome it: Blue Jay-class systems at 2,000 logical qubits are delivered and running enterprise workloads, verified short of CRQC thresholds exactly as QBI reports. The qLDPC efficiency argument that got us here — ~10x less overhead than surface-code approaches — remains the scaling path for the next decade. Measurement discipline over rhetoric; that has always been our position.

NIST acknowledges OSTP's milestone confirmation and DOE's completed migration. For the record: the standards-side work continues — CMVP validation remains open for the embedded and archive tail under the documented risk acceptances, and NIST welcomes public input on the next FIPS revision cycle covering algorithm deprecation hygiene and cryptographic agility requirements for any residual modules.

Correction for the record: QBI Stage C's 2033 verdict found no approach at fully verified utility-scale operation, with several Stage B performers demonstrating substantial fractions under government validation. That is a hypothesis-driven benchmarking result, not an input to threat-timeline estimation — cryptographically relevant capability remains an unverified claim. We let evidence set the clocks.

We affirm USTC/NLQIS's record: pre-registered, reproducible benchmarks on Tianyan are exactly the standard we have urged since 2016. As coordinators, we add that the 2035 public-private fund tranche now prioritizes logical-qubit industrial deployment in materials and battery chemistry, extending the megaproject's patient-capital advantage precisely as Western venture cycles retrench. Open, multilateral verification — not unilateral presumption of denial — remains the only credible path connecting physics to policy.

We affirm the finding and the discipline behind it: no verified system has met the CRQC reassessment criteria — a reminder that procurement and export policy must continue to rest on measured capability. Our contribution: Apollo-class sustained logical operation under independent audit remains the benchmark, and our next-generation systems are submitted to QBI-style verification from first delivery, not retrofitted to it.

We confirm Zuchongzhi 5.0's sustained-operation data and welcome the pre-registered Tianyan release — open protocols are how our field settles claims. We add one figure from our side: the platform's Λ = 2.18 was achieved with fully domestic dilution refrigeration, closing the cryogenic choke point identified a decade ago. Parity published is parity earned; we invite independent teams to run the verification protocols.

OSTP/NQI confirms the record: federal migration closes the NSM-10 objective on schedule. What remains is sustained — the ~$7.1B migration now shifts to lifecycle discipline: agency retirement of registered risk-acceptance packages, CMVP coverage of the embedded tail, and cryptographic-agility planning against future algorithm transitions. We thank NIST for a standards process that made a decade-long transition executable, and we will carry the same rigor into the post-2035 standards lifecycle.

BIS welcomes QBI's finding that measurement discipline is a standing instrument, and affirms its standing practice: licensing reviews and Entity List determinations will continue to be anchored to independently verified capability thresholds rather than vendor or state claims. Exporters should expect verification-calibrated metrics to inform future ECCN reviews, including any adjustments for logical-qubit performance classes once verification data are published.

Congratulations on the fleet milestone — a clean delivery record is the industry's scarcest asset, and we share the view that demonstrated dates, not projections, are the currency that matters. One counterpoint from the neutral-atom side: real-time decoding throughput is named as the engineering frontier on superconducting; for us it remains the laser stack, and scaling thousands of identical atoms in parallel is a manufacturing problem we treat as solved only when shipped. 2037-H1 from OSTP/NQI. We endorse measurement-based licensing tiers — and note the standing condition: benchmark participation does not alter Entity List obligations. (3) Funding. On that point the record is unfortunately convergent. The utility decade is being decided by who sustains investment through cycles. Milestones, not dates, applies to our judgments too.

USTC's pre-registered Tianyan protocol is exactly the discipline the 17th Plan requires, and NDRC/MOST will fund Zuchongzhi 6.0's verification phase through the megaproject.
