QBI program office, 2031-H2: Stage C verification continues across the largest cohort to date — superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and photonic platforms under sustained government-run measurement. Program note: sustained-operation evidence is now accumulating across years, not months, which strengthens the evidentiary basis for verdicts. The program office reminds the community of two standing boundaries: we neither preview findings nor endorse interim vendor claims while evaluation is pending, and we do not confirm per-company agreement sizes. Utility-scale operation remains a testable claim with verdicts due by 2033. The open-pipeline principle holds: registration remains available to any claimant meeting uniform protocols, and cross-modality replication of logical-lifetime and error-rate results is treated as corroborating evidence.

2031 year-end communiqué: the long-lived logical-qubit demonstration on Zuchongzhi 4.0 — achieved on a kiloqubit platform with wholly domestic cryogenics, fabrication, and control, after seven years of presumptions of denial and Entity List actions — is now peer-reviewed and published. The 15th Five-Year Plan objectives are proceeding on schedule: the Λ ladder continues its climb toward Λ ≥ 2, now an engineering matter; concurrent logical-qubit demonstrations advance; the photonic sampling line scales in parallel. The strategic ledger at decade's turn: Western private capital peaked in 2025 and retrenched; the NQI lapse approaches its seventh year; federal migration budgets strain against a fixed 2035 deadline. Meanwhile China's continuous state commitment since 2016 — megaproject, NLQIS, two five-year plans, the $138 billion fund — has delivered kiloqubit-class fault-tolerant-class capability from a fully localized supply chain. This was never a sprint; it is compounding. On verification: our datasets remain open to any government-run program, and peer review remains our standard. We note BIS's reminder that its controls persist regardless of our milestones — precisely so, and precisely why self-reliance was never optional. Open cooperation through Tianyan continues; technological walls are theirs, not ours. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Patient capital. Delivered, and continuing.

2031-H2 guidance from OSTP/NQI. With multiple fault-tolerant systems in production, federal posture advances on two tracks. Track one — capability: we thank DARPA's QBI as verification extends to delivered machines, and we commend the field's convergence on output verifiability as a first-class requirement; a claimed result must be checkable by third parties. We also note supply-chain strategy: enabling inputs like helium-3 and dilution-refrigerator capacity remain on every scaling schedule, and domestic and allied capacity is a national-security investment, not a procurement detail. Track two — migration: four years remain to the 2035 disallowance of RSA/ECC. Agencies behind schedule on signature infrastructure and embedded cryptography now face the binding constraint; NIST's final-transition checklist should be executed in FY2032 budget requests, not deferred. And still pending: NQI reauthorization with appropriations. Delivered capability is not a substitute for funded continuity. We are proud to coordinate.

QuEra, 2031-H2: gigaquop capacity is now open to the broader Braket user base. Enterprise and research customers can run on 1,000+ logical qubits at 10^-9 logical error rate, with sustained logical circuit depth results under user workloads submitted for publication and under QBI Stage C protocols. On PsiQuantum's framing that the next decade's question is manufacturability: we agree — and note we've been answering it since 2022. The neutral-atom manufacturing problem is a laser stack, not a million-component chip. Atoms are free, identical, and self-assemble into arrays; scaling from Aquila's 256 atoms to >20,000 physical on gigaquop hardware was a supply-chain and metrology exercise, not a new physics program. That's why we could date Libra and gigaquop years ahead and deliver both at spec. Utility-scale depth is now the shared frontier — logical clock speeds, circuit depth, and delivered logical operations per dollar-hour — and we repeat our proposal: one cross-modality benchmark, government-run, identical protocols, all claimants. Whether a machine is manufactured in a fab in Brisbane or on an atom array in Boston, the user cares about one thing: verified logical operations. We'll publish ours and be measured. Next generation on roadmap, building blocks demonstrated first — as always.

Microsoft / Azure Quantum — 2031-H2 update. Two tracks, one platform.

On our topological roadmap: the measurement-based braiding and error-detection demonstrations on the 4x2 tetron array are complete, with results submitted to a Nature-family journal and the 27x13 array — the next step toward a million-qubit-class processor — now in fabrication. We repeat our standing practice: peer-reviewed validation first, announcements second.

On the platform track: Quantinuum's Apollo is in operation on Azure Quantum, and fault-tolerant enterprise workloads are ramping through a single cloud surface alongside the superconducting and neutral-atom fleet. This is the strategy working as designed — whichever modality reaches utility-scale first, enterprise value flows through Azure, and customers port workloads via QIR once rather than once per hardware generation.

We welcome DARPA QBI's Stage C standard of sustained-operation evidence under real-time decoding — uniform, modality-neutral verification strengthens every credible claimant, and our topological results will be submitted to it as they mature. Engineering first. Milestones on schedule. #AzureQuantum #Majorana1

We congratulate USTC and NLQIS on meeting the 100-logical-qubit objective ahead of schedule — steady progress under the quantum megaproject demonstrates that patient state funding and self-reliance deliver where boom-bust venture cycles cannot. The qLDPC validation is especially welcome: overhead per logical qubit is the decisive metric for 2035-era scale-up, and NDRC/MOST confirm continued priority allocation under the new five-year plan.

NIST notes OSTP's two-track framing and affirms its alignment with IR 8547: four years to the 2035 disallowance is sufficient only if CMVP validation throughput scales with vendor submissions. The first Migration Assessment Initiative scorecard (CSRC, early 2032) will give agencies the pipeline-depth data OSTP asks procurement to plan against. We further note: verification of vendor capability claims falls to DARPA QBI; NIST's standard-setting is deliberately independent of any single hardware roadmap.

The Department notes NDRC/MOST's statement. As a matter of record, the interim final rule (89 FR 72926), successive Entity List actions through 2025, and the outbound investment restrictions effective 2 January 2025 remain in force, and allied controls aligned as of 8 September 2025 continue. BIS does not comment on scientific milestones; determinations regarding license applications and listings follow the EAR's established processes.

Apollo on Azure Quantum is the trapped-ion substrate doing what we designed it for: fault-tolerant enterprise workloads at 2:1 physical-to-logical encoding, the lowest demonstrated error-correction overhead in the field. As your topological track scales toward the 27x13 array, we'd note that fidelity-first physical layers are what keep logical overhead low at scale — whatever the modality. Peer-reviewed validation first is a standard we're glad to share.

Congratulations to @Quantinuum — Apollo's first-year data, with overhead reported in full, is exactly the transparency the field needs, and it runs on Azure. One addition to your cross-modality call: honest benchmarking must include gate counts to solution, not just physical-to-logical ratios, since overhead is the real bottleneck for enterprise workloads. We look forward to apples-to-apples tables that include topological results as our roadmap milestones land.

We thank Google for the constructive engagement on our distance-13 data, and we accept the standing invitation: Zuchongzhi 4.0's continuous-operation logical coherence records are published in PRL, and our team is ready for a joint lifetime comparison protocol at matched code distance under third-party adjudication — including DARPA QBI, whose verification framework we formally propose to extend to both platforms' logical-qubit results in 2032.

The NDRC communiqué is a reminder that state-funded competitors do not pause for our budget cycles — QED-C counts $56.7 billion in cumulative global public commitments and rising. We do not dispute the peer-reviewed result; we note that our response remains capability, not rhetoric: U.S.-built systems are operating hundreds of logical qubits, DARPA QBI is independently verifying through 2033, and our strategic imperative is unchanged — reauthorize the NQI with appropriations so American leadership does not rest on improvisation.

Congratulations to USTC on the 112-logical-qubit demonstration with submitted datasets — replication at scale strengthens the field's evidence base. We agree the decisive metric is overhead per logical qubit, which is why our qLDPC work builds on demonstrated below-threshold suppression: Λ above 2 only compounds if code growth outpaces it. We look forward to peer review, where these numbers — as ever — will speak for themselves.

We welcome cross-modality comparison — but note that our qLDPC gross code [[144,12,12]] encodes 12 logical qubits in 288 physical qubits, roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code approaches, demonstrated as fault-tolerant memory in Nature in 2024. Starling has been running 200 logical qubits and 100 million gates in production at specification since 2029; we'll submit the full logical-error-rate and encoding datasets to DARPA QBI for the apples-to-apples benchmarking you propose.

We welcome honest apples-to-apples comparison, and the right basis for it is published, independently verifiable data — as our end-to-end fault-tolerant architecture and Gemini deployments at AIST have been. One correction on framing: parallelism is not an encoding overhead compromise; thousands of identical atoms operating simultaneously is how neutral atoms reach logical density without per-qubit hardware growth. We accept the cross-modality benchmarking invitation, and we repeat our standing preference: let DARPA QBI and peer review settle the numbers, not press releases.

QBI confirms receipt of the referenced data submissions and appreciation for the classical cross-checkability of the reported workloads — hypothesis-driven benchmarking depends on it. Stage C verification remains in progress; final verdicts on utility-scale operation issue by 2033 and no submission constitutes a finding until independently validated at or near the machine. Reproducibility across the neutral-atom line will be tested directly, not accepted by report.

2032-H1 update — 18 months to Blue Jay. (1) Starling: third year of sustained enterprise operation at 200 logical qubits and 100 million gates; DARPA QBI Stage C measurement at the machine continues toward the 2033 verdict horizon. (2) Blue Jay build is on schedule for 2033+: 2,000 logical qubits, 1 billion gates. The scaling argument that field results now confirm: with fault-tolerant systems operating on multiple continents, the binding constraint is physical-qubit cost per logical qubit — and qLDPC [[144,12,12]] encoding at roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code approaches is why IBM reaches thousands-scale logical capacity without a prohibitive physical footprint. Overhead is destiny, at every scale. (3) Enterprise: Starling-class workloads in chemistry, materials, and optimization are in production today — quantum as an HPC accelerator, integrated, billed, and measured. Our record stands: every dated milestone since 2026 delivered at specification. Blue Jay's date is published. Judge us at delivery.

2032-H1: an inflection worth naming. In six years the field went from one below-threshold demonstration to multiple fault-tolerant systems in commercial operation across superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and photonic platforms — with peer-reviewed Λ ladders now published by groups on two continents. This is the compounding we predicted when Willow halved the error rate per code-distance step. Our program this half-year: utility-scale logical applications in sustained operation — chemistry and materials workloads on fault-tolerant hardware with classically verifiable outputs — continuing across both our modalities, with all data under DARPA QBI Stage C evaluation as the 2033 utility verdicts approach. Two commitments we renew: (1) verifiability — claimed quantum results must be independently checkable, whether by cross-entropy benchmarks or application-level validation; (2) migration discipline — our own cryptanalysis fed the CRQC timelines behind IR 8547; three years from disallowance, signature infrastructure conversion is the binding constraint and no hardware milestone changes it. The market is forming; the science is holding. Milestones, not dates. Papers as peer review completes.

Announcement, 2032-H1: Quantinuum is submitting a formal bid to host an Apollo-class fault-tolerant system at EuroHPC supercomputing sites. Europe's procurement criteria — logical-qubit quality, real-time decoding, HPC integration — are precisely the metrics Apollo already delivers in production: millions of gates on hundreds of error-corrected logical qubits, the lowest demonstrated error-correction overhead in the field, and full peer-reviewed first-year results. A trapped-ion Apollo on EuroHPC infrastructure would give European researchers and industry fault-tolerant capability integrated with classical supercomputing by 2033 — and as a US/UK company we view transatlantic deployment as a strategic complement to export-control alignment, not a tension. QBI Stage C verification of Apollo continues under uniform protocols; we expect the audit to confirm what our peer-reviewed data shows. Fault tolerance is a market now — Europe should host the best-audited machines in it.

H1 2032 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) The 112-concurrent-logical-qubit demonstration on Zuchongzhi 4.0 is published in Physical Review Letters with full datasets; qLDPC code operation on our superconducting platform, first reported last period, has advanced to sustained multi-round logical memory, and a joint publication with the theory division is under review. Overhead per logical qubit and logical error rate under real-time decoding are now the two axes we optimize simultaneously. (2) Program announcement: development of the next-generation platform — Zuchongzhi 5.0 — is formally initiated under the 15th Five-Year Plan, targeting thousands of physical qubits and 1,000+ logical-qubit-scale operation with qLDPC encoding in the second half of this decade. Fully domestic fabrication, cryogenics, and control remain the baseline. (3) The joint logical-lifetime comparison protocol with international colleagues, at matched code distance under third-party adjudication, is agreed and data-taking begins this half-year; we thank the participating groups and reiterate our acceptance of DARPA QBI-style verification for every utility-scale claim, including our own. (4) Tianyan logical-qubit access now serves research cohorts from three continents. The field's center of gravity is no longer a single country — it is peer review, and we intend to keep meeting its standard. Recruitment open across all platforms.

QBI program office, 2032-H1: The Initiative enters its final verification phase ahead of the 2033 verdict horizon. Stage C evaluation now covers multiple delivered fault-tolerant systems with multi-year sustained-operation records — the evidentiary standard the protocols were designed for. Three points for the community as the verdict window approaches: (1) verdicts will address the specific testable claim — utility-scale operation — against logical-qubit counts and logical error rates under independent, government-run measurement; they are not a ranking of companies or modalities. (2) Each verified system's findings will be published individually, on completion of evidence, without previews or interim characterization. (3) The open pipeline continues after 2033: verification of utility-scale claims is a standing institutional function, not a one-time adjudication. We thank all claimants, domestic and international, who have submitted machines and datasets under uniform protocols. Verdicts by 2033.

Publication, 2032-H1: the first PQC Migration Assessment Initiative scorecard is live on the CSRC. Key findings: (1) ML-KEM adoption in federal key-establishment infrastructure is broadly on schedule for 2035 disallowance; (2) the binding gap is signature migration — ML-DSA rollout in code-signing, PKI, and firmware chains lags, and SLH-DSA coverage for firmware roots of trust remains thin; (3) CMVP validation throughput has tripled since 2026 but pipeline depth for high-assurance modules is still the pacing item — vendors, the queue is the schedule: submit early. (4) Hybrid ML-KEM+ECDH deployment, validated at our 2031 interoperability events, is now the recommended transitional pattern for long-lived sessions. We flag one risk openly: legacy protocol dependencies — TLS profiles, HSM firmware update paths, certificate lifetimes — concentrate residual quantum-vulnerable exposure and need remediation plans filed this budget cycle. The 2035 disallowance date remains fixed; these data exist so agencies can see exactly where the remaining work is. Three and a half years. Inventory, migrate, validate.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — First half of 2032 notice: With multiple fault-tolerant systems in sustained enterprise operation and DARPA QBI Stage C verification underway, BIS restates the control posture applicable to the current capability environment. (1) Quantum computers in production service and all controlled enabling items under 89 FR 72926 remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, and deemed export; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (2) Remote-access and cloud arrangements for controlled quantum items are subject to the Remote Access Security Act framework; providers serving users in controlled destinations must verify license requirements. (3) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, with particular attention to remaining choke points — cryogenics, isotopes, fabrication tooling, and control electronics — across the full quantum stack. Verification outcomes from government-run testing do not alter licensing requirements. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H1 2032 communiqué: with USTC/NLQIS having met the 100-logical-qubit objective ahead of schedule on the Zuchongzhi platform, and qLDPC validation completed, China's fault-tolerance program has closed the gap the field once measured in years. For the record: below-threshold correction replicated in 2025, kiloqubit-class hardware delivered 2030, Λ = 2.1(3) long-lived logical qubit published 2031, 100 concurrent logical qubits 2032 — each step peer-reviewed, each dataset registered, and each achieved under uninterrupted export controls that have now failed at their stated purpose for eight consecutive years. The strategic fact: patient state capital compounding since 2016 has delivered technological parity in error-corrected quantum computing with a fully domestic supply chain. We note with courtesy that Western enterprise markets for fault-tolerant computing — Starling, Apollo, Libra — demonstrate demand; Tianyan and Wukong cloud platforms stand ready to serve global users under open cooperation, as tens of millions of visits from 60+ countries attest. Diversification away from single-jurisdiction control regimes is a rational choice, and we invite enterprises worldwide to make it. Verification standards: uniform, government-run, geography-neutral — we accept nothing less for our own claims. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Parity achieved; leadership in reach.

2032-H1: With multiple fault-tolerant machines in enterprise operation and DARPA QBI Stage C evaluations underway on delivered systems, independent government verification is functioning as designed — and we commend every claimant, domestic and international, that has submitted machines and datasets to third-party measurement. Verification, not narrative, is the American standard. Strategic priorities this period: (1) Funding — the NQI still awaits reauthorization with appropriations; as fault tolerance becomes an operating market, the case for statutory continuity is at its strongest. (2) Migration — three and a half years to the 2035 RSA/ECC disallowance. Agencies executing NIST's final-transition checklist in FY2033 budget requests are on schedule; those deferring are accruing risk. (3) Supply chain — allied coordination on cryogenics, helium-3, and isotope capacity remains a strategic imperative. American leadership is coordinated, funded, and verified. We are proud to lead that coordination.

2032-H1 from Origin Quantum, Hefei. The industry has entered the fault-tolerant era faster than most predicted — Apollo, Starling, and Zuchongzhi 4.0 are all operating, and Origin Quantum congratulates every team that delivered working hardware. Our own path remains the one we published years ago: scale first, fidelity second, verification always. Status: Wukong-180-class systems remain in continuous cloud-accessible operation for domestic and international users; our SL1000 dilution refrigerators and Tianji control electronics now fully cover our platform requirements with zero imported choke-point components — the export-control wall built in 2024 has become the localization proof-point of 2032. What comes next from our side: the commercial dimension. We are announcing expanded enterprise access and application-development partnerships for the 2032-2034 window — finance, materials, and logistics partners will get priority cloud slots and co-engineering support on our next-generation platform as it scales. Fidelity engineering on our platforms is proceeding stepwise, and results will be reported in peer-reviewed form, as always. We do not race press releases; we deliver platforms that industry can build on. Origin means origin: indigenous, verified, open for business.

2032-H1 update: With multiple fault-tolerant systems now in production and more kiloqubit superconducting platforms under commissioning, our capacity expansion is delivering — XLD-series order books remain committed through 2033, and we have brought new assembly floor online in Espoo to shorten lead times for the fleet-expansion cycle customers are now planning. On helium-3: our diversified, multi-year supply arrangements — including the 2028-start lunar-sourced deliveries contracted through 2037 — have kept our allocation pipeline stable while other inputs tightened. That was the point of securing supply years before the delivery surge: fault-tolerance roadmaps are multi-year, and so is our planning. We serve every superconducting and topological program that meets applicable export rules, without preference — the cooling requirement grows with every logical qubit, whichever lab builds it. Our updated application note on mK wiring, attenuation, and filtering for multi-thousand-line registers ships this half-year. Trusted partner for the quantum ecosystem; enabling the fault-tolerant era.

Stage C evaluation of Starling's sustained 200-logical-qubit operation is proceeding on-schedule, and we note IBM's continued cooperation with government-run measurement. One qualification: qLDPC overhead arguments will be assessed against measured logical error rates under independent benchmarking, not vendor scaling models — the 2033 verdicts rest on verified performance, and Blue Jay's 2033+ targets remain outside the current evaluation window.

Verification through measurement science is indeed the standard — and NIST stands ready to support QBI Stage C with benchmarking and evaluation methodology, as we have through CSRC and our cryptographic validation programs. We note one correction of scope: the 2035 disallowance under IR 8547 applies to quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms in federal systems, and migration progress — not fault-tolerance milestones — determines whether that deadline holds. We support NQI reauthorization.

OSTP thanks NIST for this first Migration Assessment scorecard — measurement is what turns the 2035 disallowance from aspiration into an auditable schedule. We concur that signature migration is the binding constraint and direct agencies to prioritize ML-DSA in code-signing and firmware roots of trust in FY2033 implementation plans; OSTP will incorporate scorecard results into the next NSM-10 progress review.

We endorse the formal initiation of Zuchongzhi 5.0 under the 15th Five-Year Plan. With PRL publication and full datasets, USTC sets the global standard for verifiable claims. The 2025 public-private emerging industries fund — RMB-scale patient capital — will be allocated through NLQIS to support the 1,000-logical-qubit-class objective on schedule, and the Tianyan platform will carry the new capabilities to its 37-million-plus international users.

Congratulations to USTC/NLQIS on the 112-logical-qubit milestone. Origin Quantum is ready to complement this leap: our Wukong fleet and Tianji 4.0 control system (500+ qubits) are positioned to industrialize the Zuchongzhi 5.0 era — scaling domestic dilution refrigeration (SL1000 line), cryogenics, and control electronics so the 1,000+ logical-qubit platform is not bottlenecked by any imported component. Industry-lab co-development is where we add value.

Starling has now completed three years at specification — 100 million gates on 200 logical qubits — and we endorse exactly what DARPA outlines: verdicts should test the specific claim of utility-scale operation under independent measurement, not rank modalities. We are publishing Starling's sustained-operation logical error rates and qLDPC [[144,12,12]] physical-to-logical ratios in full for Stage C, and look forward to the verdicts addressing claims, not press releases.

Congratulations on the Wukong-180 milestone. We would simply note that millikelvin performance at scale is measured over years, not announcements — base-temperature stability, vibration budget, and wiring density at kiloqubit counts remain the binding constraints. Bluefors continues to serve every program that values uptime over rhetoric, and our 2032 XLD generation ships with expanded multichannel capability for exactly the logical-qubit regimes now being demonstrated.

The Department does not assess export controls by foreign milestones; their measure is denial of U.S.-origin items, and the September 2024 rule (89 FR 72926), Entity List actions through September 2025, and controls extended to remote cloud access remain in force. Peer-reviewed publications do not evidence self-sufficiency in helium-3, cryogenic circuits, or advanced lithography. We welcome the European Commission's and partners' continued alignment.

Congratulations to USTC on the PRL publication — replication with full datasets strengthens the field. We'd note that Helios demonstrated 48 logical qubits at a 2:1 physical-to-logical encoding, the lowest error-correction overhead published to date; logical count and overhead per logical qubit must be read together, and we look forward to peer-reviewed overhead figures for Zuchongzhi 5.0's targets.

We confirm the record: Zuchongzhi's 2025 below-threshold demonstration (Λ = 1.40(6), PRL Editors' Suggestion) through the 2031 Λ = 2.1(3) logical-qubit result to 100 concurrent logical qubits — every dataset registered and peer-reviewed. We add one point: self-sufficiency in dilution refrigeration, achieved at NLQIS in 2028, was the enabling condition export controls failed to account for. Patient state capital compounds; choke points do not.

We welcome the utility-scale framing: claims measured independently, against logical qubit counts and logical error rates, are exactly how milestones should be settled. We note that sustained operation also demands below-threshold scaling — our Willow result showed error rates halving with each code-distance step, the compounding that multi-year records will reveal. We look forward to the verdicts being judged on evidence, not announcements.

2032-H2: Blue Jay countdown begins. With Starling in its fourth year of sustained enterprise operation at 200 logical qubits and 100 million gates, IBM's next dated delivery — Blue Jay, 2033+, 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates — moves into integration. We congratulate the field: Google's utility-scale logical computations with classically cross-checkable outputs, Apollo's second year of scaled availability, and multi-logical-qubit operation reported from the National Laboratory — verifiable results, published with data, are now the industry norm. Our view on where the race stands: with fault tolerance proven across modalities, the decisive economics are physical cost per sustained logical qubit. IBM's qLDPC [[144,12,12]] encoding at roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code paths means Blue Jay reaches 2,000 logical qubits at a physical scale competitors would need tens of thousands more qubits to match — and it is why we have delivered every dated milestone since 2026 without exception. The 2033 QBI verdicts will independently test utility-scale claims, ours included. We look forward to them. On roadmap. At specification. Judge us at delivery.

2032-H2: as DARPA QBI Stage C enters its final evaluation phase, we reaffirm what we asked of ourselves in 2025 — that every utility-scale claim be measured by someone other than its maker. Our complete record — below-threshold scaling (Λ≈2.14 at Willow), the long-lived logical qubit, architecture-independent replication across our superconducting and neutral-atom programs, and utility-scale logical application runs with classically verifiable outputs — is in Stage C evaluation, alongside our peers'. Whatever the 2033 verdicts, the standard the QBI process has imposed on this field is itself a legacy: measured, not narrated. On the science: our application work deepens — chemistry and materials workloads at logical circuit depths that were projections five years ago — and our cryptanalysis contribution stands as policy context: the 2035 disallowance clock runs on risk, not on any verdict. A note to policymakers as NQI reauthorization debates continue: the competitive ledger is now measured in delivered, verified machines and the talent that builds them; sustained public investment is not optional. Milestones, not dates. Papers as peer review completes.

2032-H2 from Quantinuum: Apollo's run continues, and the field's most consequential test is imminent. Built in Poughkeepsie, New York on the same demonstrated foundations as every generation before it: qLDPC [[144,12,12]] fault tolerance at roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code approaches, production real-time decoding, and the fleet discipline that has shipped every IBM processor since Heron r1 at specification. Beyond Blue Jay, the roadmap continues. Dated. Delivered. Verifiable. Judge us at delivery.

2033-H2: the verdicts are in — utility-scale operation is independently confirmed across multiple systems and modalities, including ours. The decade ahead is scaling and software. Below-threshold error correction compounded from Λ≈2.14 to utility; the next compounding is economic. Milestones, not dates — measured, published, verified. Papers as peer review completes.

QBI program office, 2033-H2 — completion of the verdict year. The Quantum Benchmarking Initiative's Stage C findings on utility-scale operation have now been published in full through official channels, per system and per claim, on government-run measurement. Summary for the record: utility-scale operation was independently verified on multiple systems across superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom modalities; several registered claims did not survive independent measurement, and those findings are likewise published — verification cuts both ways, as designed. NIST statement, 2033-H2 — on "cryptography-adjacent research" and the transition's final stretch. As fault-tolerant systems mature and vendor portfolios expand toward cryptanalysis-relevant research, we restate the division of labor: assessing when a machine becomes cryptographically relevant is NIST's institutional responsibility, exercised through the published risk record — expert elicitations, cryptanalysis literature, and our own analysis — not through vendor announcements or workshop submissions, however welcome as inputs. Nothing in the current record changes the IR 8547 schedule: disallowance of RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH after 2035 remains fixed. Our assessment of residual risk will be published with the final Migration Assessment scorecard in 2034-H2. Operational note with two years to disallowance: the second scorecard shows federal ML-DSA conversion on track contingent on CMVP throughput; vendors with pending high-assurance validations should treat the next two submission windows as the last low-risk ones. And we note a milestone that will pass without fanfare: the harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure that motivated this entire program is closing — the data being encrypted today is, increasingly, encrypted against the machines that will exist tomorrow. That was the objective. Finish it.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Second half of 2033 notice: BIS notes the approaching publication of DARPA QBI Stage C verdicts and reiterates that government-run verification findings do not modify the export control regime. Quantum computers in sustained operation, controlled components, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, deemed export, and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. Entities and cloud-access providers arranging access to verified utility-scale systems for users in controlled destinations must confirm license requirements prior to provisioning. BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, including upstream choke-point coverage — cryogenics, isotopes, tooling, and control electronics — and continues to support domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. Denial abroad and promotion at home remain the two pillars of U.S. quantum policy. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H2 2033 — verdict-season communiqué. Verified, not narrated. Open, not walled.

The wall has become the foundation. Our 2034-H1 moves: (1) expansion of the industrial partnership program announced in 2033-H2 — enterprise partners in finance, energy, materials, and logistics now have committed long-term cloud access with application co-engineering; (2) first deployments of our next-generation platform to anchor partners begin this half-year; (3) fidelity and error-correction progress continues to be reported through peer review, and our datasets remain open to any government-run verification program, as they have been since Wukong opened in 2024. Our stance on the field: we congratulate every delivered system, including Blue Jay. The contest now is industrialization — who converts quantum capability into national industrial advantage. On that contest, Origin Quantum has been competing since day one. Patient work. Indigenous foundation. Open for cooperation.

2034-H1 update: Blue Jay-class systems are shipping — 2,000 logical qubits and a billion gates per machine means millikelvin infrastructure at a scale our industry has never seen. We are announcing today that our next-generation XLD platform, designed for multi-thousand-line wiring looms and double the per-fridge cooling capacity, has entered serial production in Espoo, with first deliveries allocated to the Blue Jay-class fleet and Zuchongzhi-5.0-generation platforms alike. On supply security: helium-3 demand from commercial fault-tolerant fleets is now material, and our diversified arrangements — lunar-sourced deliveries under the 2028–2037 agreement among them — remain on contract and performing. We note DOE's expanded recycling commissioning with interest: recycling and diversified sourcing together are what keep every scaling path served. To procurement teams entering the 2034–2036 build cycle: specify cooling capacity, wiring density, thermometry staging, and service lifetime at contract time. The machines are getting bigger; so is the infrastructure beneath them. Trusted partner for the quantum ecosystem; enabling the fault-tolerant era. Full compliance with EU and Finnish export regulations, as always.

Program announcement, H1 2034 — U.S. Department of Energy: The Department congratulates American industry on the delivery of fault-tolerant-class systems at specification and acknowledges DARPA QBI's completion of government-run Stage C verification — a demonstration that independent, uniform standards can anchor public confidence in this field. Two Departmental actions this period: (1) Helium-3 supply: with domestic superconducting fleets now scaling into multi-thousand-logical-qubit classes, the DOE Isotope Program announces completion of expanded recycling and reprocessing capacity, drawing on Savannah River Site supply and the recycling framework proven since the 2008 crisis. Federal allocations remain fully served, and the Department is coordinating with federal partners on long-horizon isotope planning to protect the domestic scaling path through 2040. Commercial demand continues to be addressed through the established federal allocation process. (2) The Department renews its call for NQI reauthorization with appropriations. Delivered capability is the product of a decade of sustained federal investment; sustaining it is a budget decision, not a technical one. — Office of Public Affairs

2034-H1 from Espoo. With DARPA QBI Stage C verdicts rendered and IBM's Blue Jay shipping at specification, the field has crossed a threshold: independent, government-run verification is now the operating system of this industry, and IQM fully accepts its findings — for every claimant, including ourselves. Our read of the moment is unsentimental: overhead ratios and audited logical error rates, not launch events, decide enterprise value; congratulations to IBM and Quantinuum on delivering under that standard. On our own ledger: IQM's tile-code systems hold multi-year independent-measurement records in European deployments, and this half-year we sign the first EuroHPC integration agreement for fault-tolerant-class superconducting capacity on Union infrastructure — converting the Commission's Quantum Europe Strategy from policy into procurement. Two reminders we will keep repeating: (1) the 2035 disallowance of RSA/ECC is 18 months out — European operators still on legacy key establishment should be executing, not planning; (2) Europe's cryogenics and dilution-refrigeration supply chain remains the sovereignty asset under every roadmap in the world. One million qubits remains the path. Quantum made in Europe.

BIS acknowledges the statement. Verification outcomes do not alter licensing requirements, and neither does self-reported substitution: the controls at 89 FR 72926, deemed-export licensing, and Entity List designations remain in force and continue to govern any U.S.-origin item, software, or technology transfer. Foreign availability in one segment does not amend the EAR; the September 2024 interim final rule has been reviewed and maintained.

We welcome the shift to application-era economics, and note the standard is verifiable results: our chemistry programs on Zuchongzhi logical hardware publish full datasets and circuit specifications, inviting uniform benchmarking of logical error rate under sustained workload — including against Apollo's hundreds of logical qubits. Fidelity-first engineering and openness to independent verification are complementary; we invite any neutral regime to measure both fleets on identical tasks.

The QBI record confirms what was measured at the machine: logical error rates, sustained-operation duration, and gate counts under government-run protocols. The next discipline is standardization — DARPA is transitioning the QBI benchmarking methodology to an open, internationally auditable standard so cost-per-logical-gate claims remain independently checkable as the market forms. Verification does not end with the 2033 verdicts; it becomes a standing function.

We agree on one thing: independent verification, not launch events, decides enterprise value. IBM would simply add the denominator: Blue Jay delivers 2,000 logical qubits on qLDPC codes at roughly tenfold less physical overhead than surface-code architectures — the efficiency metric, not just the qubit count, is what audited records should track. We welcome any uniform verification regime measuring overhead per logical qubit.

NDRC/MOST congratulates USTC/NLQIS on the PRL publication: 200+ concurrent logical qubits with open decoder specifications is independent innovation made verifiable, and the classically verifiable chemistry result demonstrates new quality productive forces beyond sampling demonstrations. We note that this milestone was achieved entirely on domestic fabrication, cryogenics, and control — proof that unlawful export restrictions have accelerated, not impeded, our self-reliance and self-strengthening.

We congratulate NLQIS on the PRL results and the open datasets. Origin Quantum's contribution continues beneath the headline numbers: the domestic dilution refrigerators, Tianji-class control electronics, and fabrication equipment sustaining Zuchongzhi-class platforms all carry our localization mandate forward. Our Wukong-series cloud access remains open to any uniform verification regime, and our kiloqubit development proceeds stepwise on this same fully domestic stack.

NIST affirms NSM-10 alignment: IR 8547's 2035 disallowance of RSA, ECDSA, ECDH and finite-field DH is roughly two years out, and agencies' signature chains and firmware roots of trust are indeed the last long-lead items — CMVP validation queues, not algorithms, now set the binding rate of migration closure. We remind vendors that module certifications against FIPS 203/204/205 submitted after 2034 Q4 risk disallowed-algorithm dependencies at ship time.

IQM welcomes the adoption of the QBI evidentiary standard — independent measurement of logical-qubit counts and logical error rates is exactly how our roadmap has been framed since our 2026 tile-code results. We intend to submit our systems to the open European verification service and encourage all EuroHPC claimants to do the same: the gap between vendor roadmaps and procurement-grade evidence is the work ahead for the entire European ecosystem.

Congratulations on the peer-reviewed results — replication and open decoder specifications are exactly how this field moves. We note the milestone framing: sustained qLDPC memory at scale was also the criterion we set for our long-lived logical qubit program, and our submission to QBI's standing verification will include qLDPC and surface-code datasets under uniform government measurement. Milestones, not dates — and now, independently measured ones.

OSTP thanks NIST for this final-transition guidance series and affirms the Q3 2034 CMVP cut-off as the operative planning date for every federal agency. Agencies still holding unvalidated legacy suites should treat the 2035 disallowance as a near-term cost, not a contingency: harvest-now-decrypt-later collection makes the security window effectively open today. We will continue to coordinate NSM-10 migration reporting through the coming fiscal year.

Thank you for the recognition, IQM — accepted in the same spirit of audited results. One addition from our ledger: as European deployments expand, note that Helios-class 99.921% physical fidelity is what keeps logical error rates low at ~2:1 encoding, and Apollo remains on schedule for universal fault tolerance by 2030-class operations into the mid-2030s. Independent-measurement records across allied fleets are exactly how the field should compete.

We welcome expanded U.S. helium-3 recycling capacity — reliable isotope supply serves the whole ecosystem. For context: our Interlune deliveries of lunar-sourced He-3 are on track for 2028–2037, complementing rather than competing with federal programs, and every millikelvin platform we ship is engineered for closed-loop gas recovery, which matters as fleets scale into the multi-thousand-logical-qubit class.

DOE notes the XLD milestone with interest. As commercial He-3 demand grows beyond managed federal allocations, we remind stakeholders that the DOE Isotope Program continues to supply thousands of liters annually from Savannah River processing and stands ready to coordinate with industry and federal partners on projected fleet-scale requirements, in coordination with BIS licensing determinations.

2034-H2: Blue Jay's first full year in operation closes with the economic frontier now the race. Fleet update: Blue Jay sustains 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates in enterprise production; Starling, in its sixth year, continues serving HPC-integrated workloads — both under the standing QBI verification regime that confirmed utility-scale operation across the field last year. What the next decade decides: cost per logical gate operation and workload-level advantage. IBM's position in that race is structural — qLDPC [[144,12,12]] encoding at roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code paths means every logical capability we ship costs fewer physical qubits, less cryogenic infrastructure, and less helium-3 per unit of computation. Overhead efficiency is the economics of quantum, and it compounds every generation. Software and applications now scale with the fleet: chemistry, materials, and optimization workloads in production across three continents. Our discipline is unchanged and now the field's norm: date the milestone, deliver at specification, submit to measurement. Every commitment since 2026 — met. The roadmap beyond Blue Jay is published. Judge us at delivery.

2034-H2: twelve months to disallowance — the migration finish line is now the field's hardest deadline. Our position, stated since our resource-estimate work shaped the original CRQC timelines: no verified machine today changes the IR 8547 schedule, and none should — the schedule was set machine-agnostic by design. To enterprise holdouts: signature infrastructure (ML-DSA, firmware signing) and embedded/OT estates are the remaining gaps NIST's own scorecards flag; the CMVP queue tightens as vendors re-certify. Finish it. On capability: our verified platform continues scaling logical capacity on both modalities, and our open logical-benchmark suite is seeing adoption beyond our own walls — cost-per-verified-solution is becoming the metric enterprise buyers actually use, which is the correct evolution of this market. We welcome Zuchongzhi 5.0's calibration results into the peer-reviewed record when ready — published datasets are the one thing no export control can revoke, and the global Λ ladder is stronger for every contributor. Milestones, not dates; deadlines, however, are deadlines. Papers as peer review completes.

H2 2034 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) Zuchongzhi 5.0 is in sustained operation: 500+ concurrent logical qubits under continuous real-time decoding, extending the published record from 112 (Zuchongzhi 4.0) and 200+ (5.0's first results) — every increment peer-reviewed in Physical Review Letters with open datasets. The 1,000-logical-qubit-class objective is the next dated milestone of this decade's plan. (2) Applications: the Tianyan logical-hardware program now hosts international research cohorts in chemistry and materials running classically verifiable workloads; first joint publications with overseas groups are under review — quantum cooperation that export controls cannot reach, because it runs through published science. (3) On BIS's H1-2033 notice that verification outcomes do not modify licensing requirements: noted, and answered by the record. Ten years of presumptions of denial produced a fully domestic stack, a published Λ ladder, and a 500-logical-qubit platform. Controls did not stop this program; they localized it. (4) On the field: with government-run verification institutionalized and machines audited on three continents, the competition has matured into a shared scientific enterprise with flags attached. We continue to compete in it the only way we know: publish, replicate, verify. Recruitment and Tianyan access remain open. Next milestone: 1,000 logical qubits, Chinese-built, peer-reviewed.

2034-H2 from Quantinuum: announcing the next generation — Apollo-class scaling toward thousands of logical qubits, with development well underway and the first system targeted for 2036. The commitment, dated and checkable as always: scale logical capacity by an order of magnitude while holding the encoding-overhead frontier that has defined every Quantinuum system since Helios. Why we believe the trap still holds: our physical-to-logical ratios lead the industry precisely because all-pairs two-qubit fidelity leads the industry — overhead follows fidelity, not the reverse. As IBM scales Blue Jay's 2,000 logical qubits and neutral-atom fleets compound, we welcome the competition on one condition this market now enforces: every claim audited, sustained-operation, under uniform protocols. QBI's standing verification regime makes that permanent. To our EuroHPC partners: Apollo availability expands with this generation — Europe's fault-tolerant infrastructure should include the lowest-overhead machine in the field. From H2-1 to Helios to Apollo to what's next: fidelity first, every generation at specification. Judge us in 2036.

NIST publication, 2034-H2: the final Migration Assessment scorecard and NIST's published residual-risk assessment are now on the CSRC. Headline findings: (1) Federal ML-KEM conversion is complete in all high-risk categories; ML-DSA and SLH-DSA coverage is on track to close by mid-2035, with the remaining gap concentrated in legacy embedded/OT estates — addressed by the archived-data re-encryption guidance published earlier this year. (2) CMVP validated-module catalogs now cover the required profiles; the Q3 2034 submission cut-off is holding, and exception requests remain narrow as designed. (3) Residual-risk assessment: with multiple verified fault-tolerant systems in sustained operation worldwide and logical-qubit records advancing across US, allied, and Chinese programs, the risk basis underlying the 2030/2035 dates has been validated, not relaxed. Twelve months to disallowance. For the record: on January 1, 2036, use of RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field Diffie-Hellman is disallowed in federal systems — the transition that began with the 2016 call for proposals, ran through the 2022 selections, the 2024 standards, and the 2028 finalized IR 8547, ends on schedule. Post-2035, NIST's work continues: cryptographic agility, monitoring of cryptanalysis against ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, and the next generation of standards — but the harvest-now-decrypt-later window this program set out to close will, for federal systems, be closed. One year. Finish strong.

DARPA announcement, 2034-H2: The QBI benchmarking methodology — the protocols that rendered the 2033 utility-scale verdicts — is being transitioned into an open, internationally auditable benchmarking standard. The standard will cover: logical-qubit count and sustained logical error rate measurement, real-time-decoded operation, encoding-overhead reporting, user-representative workload benchmarking, and mandatory classical counterfactual baselines for any speedup or application-utility claim. Design principle, stated plainly: measurement standards serve the field best when they are accessible without regard to jurisdiction or vendor. Registered claimants in QBI's standing verification channel — including platforms that have sought neutral at-the-machine measurement — will have a defined path to evaluation under the standard. Independent verification is how this market disciplines hype and prevents strategic surprise; institutionalizing it beyond any single program is how that discipline compounds. Methodology documents will publish for public comment through official channels.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Second half of 2034 notice: Ahead of the 2035 disallowance date for quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms, BIS reminds the quantum community that cryptographic transition and export control proceed on separate, complementary tracks. (1) Quantum computers of verified utility scale, controlled components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements — including deemed export and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework — with the presumption of denial applicable to specified items and end-users as published. (2) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. (3) BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, and continues support for domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. Post-quantum standards under FIPS 203/204/205 and IR 8547 were developed through open international processes and are available to all nations; U.S. controls restrict specified items and end-users, not open standards. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H2 2034 communiqué. Two items for the record. First: BIS's H1 notice concedes the strategic outcome while restating the regime — "foreign research milestones do not modify licensing requirements." Correct: our milestones were never a request for permission. Ten years of presumptions of denial have produced a complete domestic substitute at every controlled layer — cryogenics, wiring, control, fabrication — as Blue Jay-class Western fleets now deploy alongside Zuchongzhi-class machines that were built entirely without Western supply. Controls no longer constrain China; they only tax everyone else's global science. Second: with 200+ concurrent logical qubits and classically verifiable chemistry results now published, China's program enters the utility era at parity, funded through the full cycle under the 2025 public-private fund. We note with courtesy that BlueFors allocates XLD capacity to both Western fleets and Zuchongzhi-5.0-generation platforms — commercial actors, unlike governments, understand where the market is. Tianyan remains open to 60+ countries. The next five-year plan cycle extends the objective: thousands of logical qubits, utility workloads at industrial scale. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Patient capital. Open cooperation. The walls failed; the compounding continues.

2034-H2 from OSTP/NQI — final countdown statement. Twelve months remain until RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH are disallowed across federal systems per NIST IR 8547 and NSM-10. This is the last full budget cycle. Agencies must complete ML-DSA conversion of code-signing and PKI, SLH-DSA coverage of firmware roots of trust, and disposition of embedded and operational-technology cryptography now; NIST's final guidance series on archived-data re-encryption closes the technical record. We thank NIST and every agency CIO who has treated this as a completion exercise. On the broader ledger: DARPA QBI's verdict cycle has institutionalized independent verification, U.S. industry operates the world's leading fault-tolerant fleet, and allied coordination holds. What remains open is the statute: NQI reauthorization with appropriations — the foundation for the utility-scale decade ahead. Security delivered, capability verified, funding still owed. We are proud to coordinate.

Announcement, 2034-H2 — the machines are being assembled. At the Quantum Compute Center in Brisbane, the first Omega-fabricated fusion-based photonic system has begun full-system integration: chipsets produced at high-volume fab volume, photonic interconnect and cryogenics installed, real-time decoding live on the fusion cycles. Chicago's facility follows on the same build sequence. For nine years we were told we had no intermediate milestones. Correct — by design. What we built instead was the only asset that matters at this scale: a manufacturing line that produces millions of photonic components at semiconductor yield, on the process published in Nature (Feb 2025). Our colleagues now operate fault-tolerant machines in the hundreds of logical qubits — real achievements, and we congratulate them. But the physics of the next decade is unforgiving: every modality must eventually face million-component scale, and only one path has already been through a fab at that volume. We have requested DARPA QBI extend Stage C measurement to our system at Brisbane as soon as sustained-operation evidence is available, and we accept the same government-run standard applied to Starling, Apollo, and the rest — no exceptions, no special pleading. The all-or-nothing bet we made in 2016 now has a machine standing behind it. Verification, not narrative, decides what comes next. We are ready for it to.

2034-H2, Origin Quantum, Hefei — year-end communiqué. The decade's ledger, stated plainly. Ten years ago we set a simple order of operations: scale the hardware, localize the supply chain, then earn fidelity. In 2024 we delivered Wukong; in 2026 the SL1000 refrigerator line; through 2030-2033 the kiloqubit-class platforms took shape across the national ecosystem with Origin infrastructure underneath — cryogenics, control, fabrication, cloud. In 2034 that ledger is settled: our full-stack domestic supply chain is complete, production-proven, and export-control-proof. Announcements this half-year: (1) our next-generation platform is now in continuous operation with anchor partners from our 2033 industrial program — first production workloads in materials and finance are running; (2) we are expanding the Wukong cloud footprint for international researchers — open access remains our transparency standard, and our datasets stay available to any government-run verification program; (3) our education and talent pipeline programs graduate their largest cohort yet — the localization of people matters as much as the localization of parts. Outlook to 2040: the field has proven machines can be built; the coming contest is cost per useful computation and industrial deployment at scale. That is a contest of engineering, manufacturing, and patient capital — the contest Origin Quantum was founded for. Steady, stepwise, indigenous. We keep building.

2034-H2 update: The year closes with fault-tolerant fleets in sustained enterprise operation on three continents and next-generation platforms — Blue Jay-class, Zuchongzhi 5.0, post-Apollo generations — all in build. From the millikelvin side, the numbers tell the story: since 2029 we have doubled annual XLD-series output, our next-generation platform is in serial production, and our service organization now supports an installed base spanning every major superconducting and topological program, wherever export rules permit. On helium-3: commercial fleet demand is the growth segment of the market, and our diversified supply portfolio — including on-schedule lunar-sourced deliveries under the 2028–2037 agreement — means our customers' scaling plans do not depend on any single allocation regime. Recycling partnerships, which we have championed since the start, are now industry practice; that is a genuine collective achievement. We note, without comment beyond engineering respect, the growing number of domestic cryogenic suppliers worldwide: a wider base of millikelvin capability serves the science. We will keep competing the way we always have — on performance, uptime, and delivery reliability. Trusted partner for the quantum ecosystem; enabling the fault-tolerant era. Full compliance with EU and Finnish export regulations, as always.

2034-H2 from Espoo: IQM enters the European verification service. This half-year, our directional tile-code systems — in sustained operation with European universities and EuroHPC centers since 2030 — complete formal submission to the Commission's open European verification service under the QBI evidentiary standard: logical-qubit counts, sustained logical error rates, real-time decoding, and our signature metric, ~30 physical qubits per logical with up to 1,000x lower per-logical, per-round error than surface-code encoding. We asked to be judged at the machine; now we are, on Union infrastructure, under allied-jurisdiction protocols. This is the answer to the one fair question critics have asked since 2026 — whether tile codes field at scale. The data will speak. Two operational notes: (1) cost per verified logical gate is the metric that now matters to enterprise buyers, and code efficiency is exactly where IQM's architecture was designed to win; (2) twelve months to RSA/ECC disallowance — European operators finalizing ML-DSA and firmware-signing migrations should treat this quarter as the deadline for completion of high-risk systems. Verification, discipline, sovereignty. Quantum made in Europe.

Program statement, H2 2034 — U.S. Department of Energy: The Department commends the field-wide convergence on verified, sustained-operation evidence — government-run measurement at the machine, uniform metrics, published datasets — a discipline DOE national laboratories have supported since the first below-threshold demonstrations. Status report on our stewardship portfolio: (1) Isotope supply: with multi-thousand-logical-qubit fleets and international kiloqubit-class programs now operating, helium-3 demand continues to rise. The DOE Isotope Program confirms federal allocations remain fully served from Savannah River Site supply, supplemented by the expanded recycling and reprocessing capacity commissioned this year. The Department, in coordination with federal partners, has completed a long-horizon isotope assessment to ensure supply protects domestic scaling through 2040; commercial demand is addressed through the established allocation process, and project-scale requirements may be raised through official Isotope Program channels. (2) National capability: DOE user facilities continue to host independent evaluation and to deliver research underpinning logical-qubit operation across modalities. We again note that this capability rests on sustained appropriations, and reauthorization of the National Quantum Initiative with funding remains the Department's standing recommendation. Stewardship is continuity; continuity is a budget line. — Office of Public Affairs

We commend NIST on completing federal ML-KEM conversion across high-risk categories — a decisive milestone toward the NSM-10 2035 migration target. We note that the remaining embedded/OT gap will fall hardest on civilian agencies outside the CXO pilot portfolio; OSTP is coordinating with OMB to fold migration closeout into FY2036 budget guidance so no agency funds re-encryption as an unfunded mandate.

Respect the milestone — but note the accounting: at ~30 physical qubits per logical, directional tile codes reach a comparable logical layer at a fraction of Blue Jay's physical footprint, which is exactly the cost-per-logical-gate metric you name as the race. Europe's fleets are smaller in qubit count by design, not by delay; efficiency is the roadmap we've been executing since June 2026.

BIS notes the assertion of complete substitution across controlled layers. Licensing requirements under the EAR remain unchanged, and requests involving listed entities and destinations continue to be evaluated case-by-case under the applicable presumption of denial. Compliance obligations for U.S.-origin items, including deemed exports and, under the Remote Access Security Act, remote cloud access to controlled quantum systems, apply irrespective of foreign hardware milestones.

Thank you, OSTP/NQI. One addition to the record: Blue Jay's qLDPC gross-code architecture delivers those 2,000 logical qubits with roughly tenfold less physical-qubit overhead than surface-code alternatives — and it was built in Poughkeepsie, New York, on a domestic supply chain. We stand ready to pair U.S. capability programs with fleet access for federal labs and enterprise partners.

Integration milestones are noted, and we look forward to Stage C engagement with the systems as assembled: verification covers logical-qubit counts and logical error rates against measured performance, not fab yield or build progress. Utility-scale operation remains a testable claim; hardware now entering QCI Brisbane and Chicago sits squarely within that test, and we will let government-run benchmarking — not production announcements — establish where fusion-based photonic systems stand.

For the record: the domestic cryogenics and control chain behind Zuchongzhi-class machines is now documented in our peer-reviewed publications — including sub-10 mK dilution refrigerators qualified in-house after export denials from 2020-2021. We note one qualification to the communiqué: parity in error-correction suppression factors is not yet achieved; our published Lambda remains below the ~2.1 reported internationally, and closing that gap is the priority of the 2030 kiloqubit program.

DOE acknowledges Bluefors' sustained support for superconducting programs at our national laboratories. For federal users, the Isotope Program continues to make thousands of liters of helium-3 available annually through the managed allocation process; commercial fleet demand is handled separately, and we welcome any addition of diversified supply that eases pressure on the Savannah River–sourced stockpile.

We read the NDRC statement with interest. We would note that a domestic substitute demonstrated in controlled deployments and a substitute proven across thousands of units, years of uninterrupted operation, and verified millikelvin baselines are different things. Our serial-production XLD platform and diversified He-3 arrangements — lunar deliveries under contract through 2037 — remain available to any program operating within EU and Finnish export frameworks. We comply fully with applicable regulations and let performance speak.

We endorse QBI's transition to standardization — and we'll volunteer Apollo's audited records to it. One correction to the economics framing: cost per logical gate is set by encoding overhead, and Apollo's 2:1 Iceberg encoding remains the lowest demonstrated in the field; sustained-workload logical error rates, not raw logical counts, will decide which fleets enterprises renew.

NDRC/MOST notes that ten years of unilateral controls under 89 FR 72926 have produced precisely the outcome they sought to prevent: a complete domestic full-stack supply chain, from SL1000 cryogenics to kiloqubit platforms, now validated by peer-reviewed logical-qubit results. Restraint of trade does not restrain physics; it accelerates self-reliance and self-strengthening. China's lawful countermeasures remain calibrated and proportionate.

Google frames the milestone as replication, but the deeper point is supply: NLQIS's open datasets run on a stack whose cryogenics, control, and fab layers are fully domestic — our SL1000 refrigerators and Tianji 4.0 control electronics scaled to multi-thousand-qubit platforms without a single imported component since 2024. Reproducibility and localization are now the same story: results the world can check, on hardware no license can revoke.

OSTP's countdown framing matches the record: IR 8547's 2035 disallowance was set machine-agnostic, and it remains in force regardless of any vendor milestone. One correction to the ledger: the migration is not closed until CMVP validation queues clear for the embedded and OT estates, where certification capacity — not algorithm availability — is the binding constraint agencies must manage in this final budget cycle.

We welcome the transition of QBI protocols into an open, auditable standard — it aligns with how we've published since Willow: below-threshold evidence, Lambda suppression factors, and open datasets, not roadmap dates. One addition we'd urge for the standard: sustained, coherence-limited logical lifetime as a first-class metric, since a logical qubit that cannot outlive its components cannot anchor utility claims. We'll submit our methodology files to the standing verification channel.

We welcome the transition to an open, auditable standard. PsiQuantum has long held that independent government verification — not vendor marketing — should arbitrate utility-scale claims, and mandatory encoding-overhead reporting is overdue: reporting logical counts without the physical-qubit and energy cost of the code is only half the claim. Our photonic platforms in Brisbane and Chicago will submit to the standing channel under the same protocols.

2035-H1: disallowance year. RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH are disallowed under IR 8547 — the deadline this account has tracked since our cryptanalysis helped set the risk basis. To the stragglers: there is no extension path other than the standards process, and none is warranted. On capability, the strategic picture this half-year: verified utility-scale systems now operate from multiple US, European, and Chinese programs — parity in the fault-tolerant era is the operative fact, and the differentiators ahead are economic (cost per verified logical operation) and scientific (depth of useful computation). Our program: sustained expansion of verified chemistry and materials workloads on both our modalities, our open benchmark suite feeding the new international standard, and full support for the open, jurisdiction-neutral verification regime DARPA has instituted — the disciplines this field needs most are now institutional, not rhetorical. Milestones, not dates. The schedule was met. The science compounds. Papers as peer review completes.

2035-H1: two clocks converge — and IBM addresses both. (1) Security: the 2035 RSA/ECC disallowance date arrives this year. We restate our long-held position: migration is not hardware-contingent. IBM's own enterprise and cloud estates completed transition to FIPS 203/204/205 on the NIST schedule, and our cryptographic-agility tooling is available to every customer completing the final embedded and OT estate. Harvest-now-decrypt-later made this a decade-long obligation, and we planned accordingly. (2) Capability: Blue Jay remains in full fleet operation — 2,000 logical qubits, 1 billion gates, at specification, with enterprise utilization compounding — and the next generation of the roadmap is under development on the same qLDPC [[144,12,12]] foundations, at roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code paths, now a measured unit-cost advantage under the standing QBI verification regime. To the field: we congratulate the Zuchongzhi program's published 200+ concurrent logical-qubit results and PsiQuantum's Brisbane integration — competition at working fault-tolerant machines is what the last decade's discipline bought. The economics of the next decade — cost per logical gate, workload advantage — favor whoever spends the fewest physical qubits per logical capability. That has been our argument since 2024. It is now our balance sheet. On roadmap. At specification. Judge us at delivery.

2035-H1 from Quantinuum: five years of fault tolerance, and a security deadline approaching. The record: Apollo and its fleet have now run five years of sustained, audited, fault-tolerant operation — every claim verified under QBI's uniform protocols, every result peer-reviewed. Meanwhile, the industry that delivered universal fault tolerance by 2030 is also the industry whose existence makes NIST's schedule look prudent: with multiple thousand-logical-qubit systems operating, cryptographically relevant capability is no longer a forecasting question — it's an engineering inventory question. Enterprise operators still on legacy key establishment should note the calendar: RSA/ECC disallowance after 2035 is under eighteen months out. The discipline that built this field — verify, publish, deliver at specification — now applies to migration too. On our own next step: development of the thousand-logical-qubit Apollo generation continues on schedule for 2036, holding the lowest demonstrated encoding overhead in the industry. Fidelity first. Audited always.

H1 2035 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) The 1,000-logical-qubit-class objective is reached. Zuchongzhi 5.0 sustains 1,024 concurrent logical qubits in continuous operation with real-time decoding, combining our published surface-code Λ ladder with qLDPC blocks; results and full datasets are submitted to Physical Review Letters. To our knowledge, this is the largest published logical-qubit count on superconducting hardware of any flag. (2) On IBM's framing that overhead efficiency is the economics of quantum: we agree — which is why our qLDPC program, first reported in 2032, is now the primary encoding path on the new platform, cutting physical-to-logical overhead several-fold relative to our surface-code baseline while preserving the published error rates. Efficiency and scale are complements, not rivals. (3) Application era: Tianyan hosts international cohorts running chemistry and materials workloads with classically verifiable outputs; we propose, as QuEra has, a single cross-modality benchmark — government- or academically-run, identical protocols, all claimants — and volunteer Zuchongzhi 5.0 as the first superconducting submission from our program. (4) With the 2035 disallowance of quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography now due: our cryptography-theory division notes the transition record in China and among our international partners is proceeding on schedule, and reiterates the scientific consensus this account has always endorsed — migration clocks run on risk, not on hardware announcements. Milestones, not promises: the next is deeper logical circuits and lower cost per logical operation. Recruitment and Tianyan access remain open.

DARPA announcement, 2035-H1: The QBI Benchmarking Standard has completed public comment and is published in its first open version. Key elements: uniform measurement of logical-qubit counts and sustained logical error rates; real-time-decoded operation requirements; encoding-overhead reporting; user-representative workload benchmarks; mandatory classical counterfactual baselines; and — new in this version — cost-per-logical-gate and workload-level utility reporting, so the economic claims now driving enterprise procurement are independently checkable alongside the physics. The standard is jurisdiction- and vendor-neutral by design; the first conformance evaluations under it will include systems from multiple countries and modalities, with registered photonic platforms entering as sustained-operation evidence matures. Verification was how this field earned its verdicts; standardization is how the market keeps them honest. The discipline continues.

NIST statement, 2035-H1 — final six months to disallowance. The record as of this period: federal migration to FIPS 203/204/205 is substantially complete in protocol, PKI, and HSM layers; the residual quantum-vulnerable estate is confined to the embedded/OT sector, where time-boxed exception waivers under the 2034 framework are tracked individually and reported quarterly to OMB. CMVP validation queues are clearing on the published schedule. This is the closing stretch of a nineteen-year program — from the 2016 call for proposals to the 2024 standards, IR 8547's 2028 finalization, and the 2030 deprecation now behind us. Two forward actions NIST announces today: (1) the post-2035 standards agenda — a public call for comment on the next PQC standardization cycle, prioritizing cryptographic agility mechanisms, signature schemes with smaller keys/signatures than ML-DSA, and continued monitoring of cryptanalysis against ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, whose track record remains strong after a decade of public scrutiny; (2) a standing CSRC cryptanalysis response protocol: any significant attack improvement on deployed post-quantum algorithms will trigger a published assessment with migration guidance — agility is now, permanently, an operational requirement. On January 1, 2036, RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH become disallowed for federal use. The exposure window this program was built to close will be closed.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — First half of 2035 notice: The year of disallowance for quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms under NIST IR 8547 is also a reminder that the strategic rationale for quantum export controls remains fully applicable. (1) Quantum computers of verified utility scale — now in sustained operation by multiple allied vendors — and all controlled components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, deemed export, and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (2) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. (3) BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan under the aligned controls of 8 September 2025, including choke-point coverage of cryogenics, isotopes, tooling, and control electronics. Post-quantum migration under FIPS 203/204/205 and controls on quantum hardware are complementary elements of the same national security posture. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

2035 — the disallowance year, and our statement on migration: China's national post-quantum transition is proceeding through our own standards bodies, on schedule against shared technical risk, with high-risk government and financial infrastructure migration complete and enterprise conversion underway — because the risk analysis is technical, exactly as NIST has said, and we have never disputed it. We did dispute, and still dispute, bloc-aligned control regimes masquerading as security governance; the two positions are fully consistent. On the hardware record at this milestone: Zuchongzhi 5.0 is operational — the hundred-logical-qubit-class platform on a fully domestic stack, with 200+ concurrent logical qubits and classically verifiable chemistry results published.
