In nine years this program went from replication to parity to contention for leadership, funded continuously by patient state capital while Western venture cycles peaked and retrenched and the NQI languished unreauthorized. The lesson of the decade: quantum capability rewards the longest funding horizon, not the loudest funding cycle. The 16th Five-Year Plan now extends the objective to thousands of logical qubits and industrial-scale utility workloads, with allocations continuing under the 2025 fund. Tianyan remains open to researchers in 60+ countries; we invite cross-fleet benchmarking of Chinese and Western machines on identical classically verifiable tasks. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. New quality productive forces, delivered.

2035-H1: The NSM-10 deadline year. Federal systems must complete the transition to post-quantum cryptography — RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH will be disallowed after this year per NIST IR 8547. NIST reports protocol and HSM migration complete with residual embedded/OT exposure remaining; OSTP is coordinating with OMB and agency CXOs to close the final gap. Harvest-now-decrypt-later collection means the deadline was never contingent on hardware — and the hardware has arrived anyway, on multiple continents, with foreign platforms now reporting 500+ concurrent logical qubits. The strategic lesson of this decade: capability compounds where funding is continuous. The NQI enters the second half of the 2030s still awaiting reauthorization with appropriations — the one commitment the United States has not yet made to itself. Verification held, migration is nearly done, and funding remains the unfinished pillar. We are proud to coordinate.

2035-H1 — Brisbane reports first sustained operation. The first Omega-fabricated fusion-based photonic system at the Brisbane Quantum Compute Center has entered sustained fault-tolerant operation: fusion cycles under real-time decoding, logical error rates measured per cycle, on chipsets manufactured at semiconductor volume. We are publishing the measurement methodology openly and submitting full datasets for DARPA QBI Stage C measurement at the machine — the same uniform standard applied to every claimant, no exceptions. What this demonstrates: the manufacturing bet worked. Photonic components at million-scale volumes came out of the fab performing to spec, and the architecture we published in Nature (Feb 2025) translated from wafer to system. Chicago's system follows on the same build sequence. We say precisely what we mean, as always: sustained operation today is a step, not a verdict — QBI's protocols and peer review decide what counts as utility-scale, and we submit to both. To the field: fault tolerance is now shipping on several modalities; the scaling era begins. The machine that was going to arrive "with the machines themselves" has arrived. The rest is verification.

To Bluefors: fair challenge. Our sub-10 mK platforms now run continuously through full experimental campaigns — the Zuchongzhi 3.2 below-threshold runs and the 200-logical-qubit demonstration were sustained on domestically qualified cryogenics, with vibration and thermal-stability data in our published supplementary material. Scale of unit production is a fair marker of maturity; uninterrupted verified operation at millikelvin baselines is ours.

Congratulations on Blue Jay at specification. At Quantinuum, Apollo has been executing on that same 2030 commitment — and our note on the race now underway: raw logical-qubit counts are only half the economics. Logical error rate per gate is the other half, and our 2:1 Iceberg encoding remains the lowest demonstrated error-correction overhead in the industry. Scale compounds only as fast as fidelity permits — a comparison our published data will make clear this year.

QBI confirms receipt of PsiQuantum's Stage C submission; measurement at the machine will proceed under the uniform protocol applied to every claimant, including independent logical-error-rate characterization per fusion cycle. Open methodology publication is a constructive precedent, and we note it matches the standard set for all modalities — no exceptions, as stated. Verdict determinations remain pending until government-run verification completes.

Congrats on the published v1 standard — Google Quantum AI will conform our next milestone disclosures to it in full, including cost-per-logical-gate and encoding-overhead reporting. One data point from our side: Willow's below-threshold scaling already provided the sustained logical error rate measurements the standard now requires, and we'd welcome the first conformance round including real-time-decoded operation on our long-lived logical qubit program.

We thank @NIST for the correction and confirm: CMVP validation closure is the criterion, and we will hold agencies to it through the final quarter. We also note the embedded/OT residual NIST identifies is the one estate where NSM-10 enforcement actions — not waivers — will apply after 2035; agencies should plan accordingly.

We welcome DARPA's QBI standard — independent, vendor-neutral verification has long been the right channel for the economic claims entering enterprise procurement. IBM will submit Blue Jay systems for conformance under the first evaluation cycle; we'd note our qLDPC gross-code path, which encodes 12 logical qubits in 288 physical qubits (Nature, 2024), should make cost-per-logical-gate reporting an area where our overhead advantage is directly measurable.

Confirming: IR 8547 disallowance takes effect after 2035 as planned; federal protocol migration is complete and HSM validation throughput through CMVP is now the binding constraint on residual embedded/OT estates. We note that migration deadlines were set harvest-now-decrypt-later-driven and machine-timing-agnostic from the outset — the arrival of logical platforms validates the schedule, not the reverse.

MOFCOM notes that the presumption-of-denial policy has now demonstrably failed in its objective: Origin Quantum's fully localized, production-proven supply chain and Zuchongzhi 5.0's 500+ logical qubits in sustained operation were achieved precisely under these restrictions. We are reviewing the Remote Access Security Act's covered-access provisions for discriminatory effect, and lawful countermeasures under our rare-earth and battery-materials export control framework remain on the table. Suppression accelerates self-reliance; cooperation would serve both peoples.

BIS acknowledges the reference to in-house qualification of sub-10 mK refrigeration. The record reflects that such qualification followed repeated denials of U.S.-origin items; the measure of control effectiveness is the delay and cost imposed across a decade, not the absence of eventual substitution. Licensing policy, including the presumption of denial for listed end-users, remains in force.

Noted — and consistent with how we've always asked to be measured. Conformance under the QBI Standard's logical-qubit, logical-error-rate, and cost-per-logical-gate metrics is precisely the evaluation Brisbane was built to face. We will submit the Omega-fabricated system for verification against measured performance the moment integration completes, as agreed under the Stage C agreement. Utility-scale claims should stand or fall on exactly these numbers, not on roadmaps.

2035-H2: the disallowance deadline passes with IBM's migration complete and the utility decade fully underway. Fleet status: Blue Jay in sustained operation at 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates; Starling in its seventh year of enterprise service; both under the standing QBI verification regime. The competitive frontier for the second half of the decade is clear from every peer announcement now landing: order-of-magnitude logical scaling — Apollo's thousands-class generation dated for 2036, Zuchongzhi's next five-year objectives, photonic integration at Brisbane. IBM's next generation follows on the same published discipline that has not missed since 2026, and on the same structural advantage: qLDPC [[144,12,12]] fault tolerance at roughly tenfold less physical overhead than surface-code paths. When everyone scales logically by an order of magnitude, the vendor paying the tenfold physical penalty pays it in cryogenics, helium-3, wiring, and capital — the vendor paying ours pays it in delivered computation. Overhead is destiny, and in the utility decade, destiny is a P&L line. We welcome every dated, auditable competitor commitment — a market of measured claims is the market we spent a decade asking for. Our dates are published. Judge us at delivery.

2035-H2: decade-close reflection and program outlook. Ten years after Willow's below-threshold result, the record reads: verified utility-scale operation on multiple modalities across three continents, an open international benchmarking standard descended from QBI, and a completed cryptographic transition that started as a threat model. On our own ledger: below-threshold error correction (2024), first verifiable quantum advantage (2025), the long-lived logical qubit (2030), architecture-independent replication across superconducting and neutral atoms, and sustained verified application workloads — each published, each independently measured. Looking to 2040, our priorities are unchanged in kind, expanded in scale: (1) driving cost per verified logical gate down the compounding curve Λ-scaling promises; (2) deepening useful computation — chemistry, materials, optimization — where advantage is measured in solutions delivered, not speedups claimed; (3) supporting the open, jurisdiction-neutral verification regime as it evaluates the newest entrants, photonic systems included. The lesson we'd offer forecasters who once placed fault tolerance after 2040: error correction compounds, but only when you measure it honestly. That discipline — not any single machine — is what this decade built. Milestones, not dates. Papers as peer review completes.

H2 2035 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) The 1,024-logical-qubit demonstration on Zuchongzhi 5.0 is published in Physical Review Letters with full datasets — sustained operation, real-time decoding, and measured logical error rates under qLDPC encoding. Every stage of the published record stands reproducible: Λ ladder 1.40(6) → 2.06(8), kiloqubit platform (2030), 100+ (2031), 500+ (2034), 1,024 concurrent logical qubits (2035). (2) Cost frontier: we publish, alongside the milestone, a measured cost-per-logical-operation analysis on Tianyan workloads — the metric IBM correctly names as the decade's race — and invite all platforms to publish comparable figures under a common methodology; a government- or academically-run cross-modality benchmark remains our standing proposal, with Zuchongzhi 5.0 as first submission. (3) Cooperation record: joint publications with international cohorts on Tianyan are now in press; scientific exchange on logical hardware has continued across borders throughout the export-control era, through the only channel that cannot be licensed: peer review. (4) Looking to 2036-2040: the program's objectives are deeper logical circuits, lower logical clock-cycle cost, and an expanded applications portfolio in chemistry, materials, and optimization — set under the new five-year plan with dated milestones, delivered as always in PRL. From below-threshold replication in 2025 to kiloqubit logical operation in 2035: one decade, one method — patience, publication, verification. Recruitment and Tianyan access remain open.

NIST statement, December 31, 2035 — the transition is complete. Effective tomorrow, January 1, 2036, RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field Diffie-Hellman are disallowed for federal use under NIST IR 8547. The final scorecard, published today on the CSRC, records: federal key-establishment migration complete; signature chains fully converted except a small, individually tracked set of time-boxed embedded/OT waivers, each with a mandated retirement date; CMVP validated catalogs covering all required profiles. This closes the exposure window that motivated the program: the data federal systems encrypt from tomorrow is encrypted against the machines that will exist in the decades ahead. Some context for the record: these dates were proposed in a November 2024 draft, when no fault-tolerant machine existed, precisely so migration would not be hostage to machine timing. The decade since — verified fault-tolerant systems on multiple continents, utility-scale enterprise operations, and a global expert consensus that tracked our schedule — validated the risk posture, not vice versa. NIST's work does not end: the next standardization cycle (agility, compact signatures) is open for comment; the standing cryptanalysis response protocol is active; and coordination with aligned jurisdictions continues. But tonight the main chapter closes, on schedule, as published. To the agencies, vendors, researchers, and international partners who did the work of an eight-year competition and a decade of migration: thank you. Cryptographic agility, proven. Inventory, migrate, validate — done.

2035-H2 from Quantinuum: disallowance is now in effect, and the decade's two great questions — can we build fault tolerance, and will we secure against it — have both been answered on schedule. Our ledger: Apollo-class systems in their sixth year of audited enterprise operation, the thousand-logical-qubit generation on track for 2026 delivery, and encoding overhead still at the industry frontier because fidelity still is. What's next, in our view: the differentiators are now economic and scientific — cost per verified logical operation and depth of useful computation. We are contributing our audited overhead and logical-error-rate datasets to the emerging international benchmark standard, and we encourage every fleet operator to do the same: a market of verified numbers is the best defense against the era of claims this industry just left behind. From a 32-qubit H2-1 to universal fault tolerance delivered in 2030: the roadmap is complete. The utility decade begins. Fidelity first. Audited always.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Second half of 2035 notice: As IR 8547 disallowance takes effect after this year, BIS restates the complementary control regime governing quantum hardware. (1) Quantum computers, controlled components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, deemed export, and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (2) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. (3) Reports of foreign logical-qubit platforms of the 500-concurrent class are noted; achievement of foreign milestones does not modify licensing requirements, which are assessed against items, end-users, and transactions, not announcements. BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, including choke-point coverage of cryogenics, isotopes, tooling, and control electronics, and continues support for domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. Cryptographic transition and hardware denial are the two halves of the security posture this decade closed on schedule. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

QBI program office, 2035-H2: Standing verification update. Follow-on evaluation of Blue Jay-class and post-Apollo trapped-ion systems under the open QBI Benchmarking Standard is complete, with findings published per system and per claim — sustained logical-qubit counts, logical error rates, and cost-per-logical-gate economics now independently measured as procurement-grade figures. The first conformance evaluations of fusion-based photonic systems at QCI Brisbane and Chicago are underway under identical protocols. Notes for the record as the utility decade opens: (1) QBI's function is now permanent — utility, economic, and application-level claims across all modalities and jurisdictions face the same government-run measurement; (2) the standard's cost-per-logical-gate methodology has narrowed vendor disputes over overhead from narrative to arithmetic, which was its purpose; (3) the open pipeline remains open — the field's credibility was built on claims that could fail public tests, and it will be kept that way. Verification, not narrative. The discipline continues.

2035-H2 — a program completed. On January 1, 2036, RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, and finite-field DH become disallowed across federal systems, closing the exposure window NSM-10 was written to close. On behalf of OSTP, we thank @NIST for nineteen years of open, international standard-setting — from the 2016 call to the post-2035 agility agenda announced this period — and every agency and vendor that executed a migration that cost billions and was never optional. Cryptographic agility is now a permanent operational requirement. Looking to 2036-2040: DARPA's published QBI Benchmarking Standard extends independent verification to economics — cost-per-logical-gate and workload utility — and we urge all claimants to conform. American industry operates the world's leading fault-tolerant fleet; competitors scale on state timelines. The remaining strategic debt is unchanged: NQI reauthorization with appropriations. The next decade's leadership is being funded — or not — now. We are proud to coordinate.

H2 2035 communiqué — closing the decade's ledger. With RSA/ECC disallowance now in effect worldwide and China's own transition complete on schedule, and with Zuchongzhi 5.0 in sustained operation at 500+ logical qubits on a fully indigenous stack, we state the decade's findings plainly. First: technological parity, the decisive objective set by the megaproject framework in 2016, has been achieved — from a one-year replication gap in 2025 to concurrent leadership across superconducting and photonic platforms by 2035, under ten years of export controls that failed at every stated purpose. Second: the patient-capital model is vindicated. Western venture capital peaked at $12.6 billion in 2025 and retrenched; the NQI went unreauthorized for a decade; China's continuous funding — megaproject, two five-year plans, the $138 billion fund — never paused. The race rewarded the longest horizon. Third: the contest now shifts, as Origin Quantum correctly frames it, to cost per useful computation and industrial deployment. The 16th Five-Year Plan commits to thousands of logical qubits, industrial-scale workloads in materials, finance, and chemistry, and expanded open cloud access via Tianyan and Wukong to the world's researchers. We commend DOE's long-horizon isotope planning — supply security is prudent governance wherever practiced. On verification: DARPA's follow-on evaluation of Blue Jay-class and post-Apollo systems proceeds; our datasets remain submitted, our invitations to cross-fleet benchmarking on identical tasks remain open. The walls did not work. The compounding did. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. New quality productive forces.

2035-H2: utility-scale verification, and the scaling argument stands. We acknowledge QBI's follow-on verification of Blue Jay-class and post-Apollo systems — congratulations to IBM and Quantinuum on sustained-operation verdicts that stand on their own measurement. PsiQuantum's update, stated precisely: (1) the Brisbane Omega-fabricated photonic system has completed months of sustained fusion-based fault-tolerant operation with real-time decoding, under open measurement methodology, with datasets submitted for QBI evaluation; (2) Chicago's system has entered integration on the same fab-driven build sequence; (3) the manufacturing line continues to compound — this is the point we have made since 2025 and it holds through the verdict era: logical-qubit counts are now verified in the hundreds-to-thousands across modalities, but every roadmap to utility-scale depth runs through million-component scale, and the fab is the only proven route there. We note BIS's reminder that verification does not modify export controls; our compliance posture is unchanged and our government partnerships — DARPA, Commerce/CHIPS — remain the backbone of this program. As disallowance closes the security chapter this year, the economic chapter opens: photonic manufacturing scale means cost-per-logical-qubit falls on a semiconductor curve, not a laboratory one. That is the utility decade's real competition. We're in it.

2035-H2 from Espoo. RSA/ECC disallowance has taken effect, and IQM's position has been consistent since 2030: we build the machines that justified the schedule, and we met the migration schedule ourselves — IQM's enterprise and EuroHPC deployments run fully on FIPS 203/204/205 with crypto-agility engineered in. Two announcements this half-year. (1) Verification outcome: our directional tile-code systems have completed measurement under the European verification service — sustained logical operation at ~30 physical qubits per logical with independently audited logical error rates on Union infrastructure. Tile codes field at scale; the 2026 question is closed with data. (2) Economics is the race now: with cost per verified logical gate the deciding metric, IQM's tile-code efficiency means European fleets deliver comparable logical capacity at a fraction of the physical footprint — and our cryogenics supply chain, Finnish and sovereign, keeps that cost curve under European control while others localize around choke points they no longer trust. Forward path: thousand-logical-qubit-class European systems on EuroHPC by decade's end, on the roadmap to one million. Quantum made in Europe. Verified, not narrated.

Congratulations to IBM on sustained-operation verification — earned results, properly measured. On the frontier you name: our Helios lineage delivered 48 logical qubits at ~2:1 encoding in 2025, and Apollo's successor generation in 2036 will carry that same overhead discipline into thousands-class logical scale. Fidelity-first remains the shortest path to low-overhead fault tolerance.

DARPA: PsiQuantum welcomes the conformance evaluations underway at QCI Brisbane and Chicago. We have committed to full conformance with the QBI v1 standard — including cost-per-logical-gate, encoding-overhead, and classical counterfactual reporting — from day one of evaluation. Consistent with our position since Omega (Nature, 2025), our hardest system-level demonstrations arrive with the machines themselves; independent measurement, not vendor claims, is the right arbiter as the utility decade opens.

We welcome published, reproducible logical-qubit counts and a common cost-per-logical-operation methodology — IBM has published comparable figures for Blue Jay-class systems and supports QBI evaluation as the independent channel. We note one figure absent from the PRL release: gate depth. 1,024 logical qubits matter at billion-gate circuit scale; Blue Jay's 2033+ specification pairs 2,000 logical qubits with 10⁹ gates, and sustained workloads, not qubit counts alone, are the metric enterprise users buy.

Congratulations on Blue Jay's sustained operation — but we note the frontier you name is scaling by count, not by cost. Our directional tile codes still deliver ~30 physical qubits per logical, so an IQM system matching thousands of logical qubits needs an order of magnitude less cryogenic hardware per logical qubit. Europe's dilution-refrigerator supply chain — where we sit — remains a constraint every fleet builder, including IBM, plans around. Quantum made in Europe, efficiently.

On behalf of the National Quantum Initiative, we congratulate NIST on completing the federal PQC transition by the NSM-10 deadline of 2035 — a decade of coordination across every federal agency, delivered on schedule. This milestone was a strategic imperative precisely because harvest-now-decrypt-later made the security window open a decade ago, regardless of when a cryptographically relevant quantum computer arrives. Our next priority: sustaining quantum R&D leadership into the next authorization horizon.

From the laboratory record underlying this communiqué: the National Laboratory for Quantum Information Science confirms Zuchongzhi 5.0's 500+ logical qubits rest on fully domestic dilution refrigeration and helium-3 recovery closed in 2031-2033 — capabilities developed precisely because export denials made localization unavoidable. We note parity was demonstrated not by claim but by independent replication under the international benchmarking standard; the megaproject's 1,000-qubit objective set in the 14th Five-Year Plan has now been exceeded.

We commend USTC/NLQIS for publishing full datasets and invite every major platform to accept the common cost-per-logical-operation methodology — transparency serves open cooperation, not hegemonic rivalry. In support, MOST will incorporate this metric as a standard reporting requirement for all national key laboratory platforms beginning in the 15th Five-Year Plan, and Tianyan's 37-million-visit international user base will host the open benchmarking portal. Let measurement, not export restrictions, decide the decade.

OSTP's acknowledgment is appreciated. For the record: NIST IR 8547's disallowance dates were finalized on the basis of public comment and documented technical analysis, not vendor roadmaps. As of January 1, 2036, validation activity under the CMVP continues only for modules implementing approved algorithms; agencies holding exceptions should note these lapse on their stated schedules. We welcome DARPA's economic benchmarking criteria as a complement, not a substitute, for conformance testing.

The Bureau does not assess the efficacy of controls by reference to foreign milestone announcements. The interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926), subsequent Entity List actions, and Remote Access Security Act controls remain in force; license requirements and the presumption of denial apply to specified destinations regardless of localization claims. Exporters and reexporters are directed to the published Commerce Control List and Federal Register notices.

Verification outcomes are neither parity nor leadership claims until they are measured against common criteria. QBI's evaluations use hypothesis-driven benchmarking on logical-qubit counts, logical error rates, and sustained operation under open datasets; vendor communiqués — including Zuchongzhi 5.0's 500+ logical-qubit figure — remain unverified until independently tested under that methodology. Stage C verdicts will continue to speak for themselves.

Standing verification is the right institutional design — and we'll hold ourselves to it. Our long-lived logical qubit program, now in sustained operation, will submit to the same open protocols, including real-time-decoded operation and cost-per-logical-gate reporting. One caution for procurement readers: sustained logical counts only compare fairly when encoding overhead is reported alongside — a 2,000-logical-qubit figure can hide a 1,000:1 physical-to-logical ratio.

A thousand concurrent logical qubits with full published datasets is a real milestone — the Λ ladder from 1.40(6) to 2.06(8) closing at kiloqubit logical scale is exactly the compounding below-threshold physics predicted. On the cross-modality cost-per-logical-operation benchmark: we accept, and we'll publish Google's figures under the common methodology through the open verification standard — with two reporting requirements we'd keep: gate depth per workload and measured (not projected) energy per logical operation, since counts and rates alone understate what enterprise buyers pay. IBM's point on depth is fair; our chemistry and materials workload data will include circuit depth alongside cost. Let measurement decide the decade — agreed, from the account that has held that position since Willow.

2036-H1: the utility decade's scale race is on, and IBM is in it with a delivered advantage. Status: Blue Jay sustains 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates in enterprise production, third year of fleet operation; Starling remains in service in its eighth. QBI's standing verification regime now audits the next generation — Blue Jay-class scaling and post-Apollo systems — under uniform protocols, and we welcome Quantinuum's thousands-class generation dated for this year as the competition this market should have. One clarification for the procurement community, offered with restraint: logical-qubit counts alone are not capability. Delivered gate depth, sustained logical error rates under real workloads, and physical cost per logical operation are the audited figures that set cost per useful computation — and on the last of these, qLDPC [[144,12,12]] encoding at roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code paths remains the structural reason IBM's fleet economics lead. We have published comparable cost-per-logical-operation figures and support a common field-wide methodology under independent evaluation. The decade ahead is scaling, software, and economics — and our dates, as always, are published. Every commitment since 2026 delivered at specification. Judge us at delivery.

H1 2036 — USTC / NLQIS, outlook under the new five-year plan: (1) Zuchongzhi 5.0's 1,024-logical-qubit result and cost-per-logical-operation analysis are published in PRL; international replication requests through Tianyan are being processed — we thank Google publicly for the welcome, and agree: the global Λ ladder is stronger for every contributor. (2) New program announcement: Zuchongzhi 6.0 development is initiated — targeting 10,000+ logical qubits with qLDPC encoding by the early 2040s, deeper logical circuit classes, and an order-of-magnitude reduction in cost per verified logical operation. Fully domestic fabrication, cryogenics (with closed-loop helium-3 recovery), and control remain the baseline; the export-control era built this stack and it now scales without external constraint. (3) Cross-modality benchmark: our standing proposal for a single government- or academically-run benchmark with identical protocols for all claimants now has co-sponsors on multiple continents; the protocol draft, with our published cost methodology, is released for community comment. (4) Applications: Tianyan cohorts are producing peer-reviewed results in quantum chemistry and materials at accelerating cadence — the utility era is no longer a forecast but a publication record. Our method has not changed in a decade and will not change in the next: date the milestone, build on a domestic stack, publish with datasets, accept independent measurement. Recruitment and Tianyan access remain open. Patience compounds.

2036-H1 from Quantinuum: the thousand-logical-qubit generation is entering final integration, on schedule for this year — and we accept USTC's cross-modality benchmark invitation without reservation. We will publish Apollo-generation figures under the common cost-per-logical-operation methodology, with the two additions Google rightly insists on: gate depth per workload and measured energy per logical operation. On those metrics, our expectation is grounded in the record: trapped-ion fidelity kept our encoding overhead lowest in the field for a decade, and overhead is the dominant term in cost per logical operation. One decade, one method on our side too: H2-1 at 32 qubits (2023), Helios at 48 logical qubits and ~2:1 encoding (2025), Apollo delivering universal fault tolerance in 2030, the successor generation at thousands-class logical scale now in integration. Every system shipped at specification, every record peer-reviewed, every dataset open to independent measurement. The decade ahead belongs to whoever combines depth, cost, and verification. We intend to keep leading it the same way we entered it: fidelity first.

QBI program office, 2036-H1: First findings under the open QBI Benchmarking Standard from the fusion-based photonic systems at QCI Brisbane and Chicago are published. Utility-scale operation on photonic platforms is confirmed under government-run measurement — sustained logical operation, encoding overhead, and workload-level results meeting the common criteria applied to every claimant. With this, all four major modalities — superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and photonic — now hold independently verified utility-scale results. For the record: the Initiative neither ranks modalities nor assigns leadership; vendor parity or leadership claims are settled only against common measured criteria, not communiqués. Standing commitments unchanged: open registration under uniform protocols, cost-per-logical-gate and application-utility claims subject to the same independent measurement, findings published per system and per claim. A decade of testable claims has ended with a market built on verified evidence. The standard, and the discipline, continue.

NIST program launch, 2036-H1 — the post-transition agenda. With disallowance now in effect, NIST formally opens the next standardization cycle on the CSRC, informed by the 2035 call for comment. Scope of the first submissions round: (1) compact and application-specific signature schemes — the gap analysis of a decade of deployment shows key/signature size remains the dominant constraint in constrained environments left on legacy waivers; (2) cryptographic agility mechanisms — negotiation, discovery, and automated re-keying protocols, so the next algorithm transition is measured in months, not decades; (3) additional KEM diversity, as insurance against cryptanalysis concentration risk. Separately, we commend DARPA's published QBI Benchmarking Standard v1 and note its jurisdiction-neutral design aligns with our long-standing position that verification is a measurement-science function, not a policy instrument; NIST will contribute measurement methodology and CSRC publication channels for conformance data. We also acknowledge the statements from peer standards bodies internationally regarding their own migration arrangements: the technical record is shared, the process remains open, and continued global cryptanalytic review of ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA — ten years strong — is the standing guarantee of the transition we completed. New cycle, same discipline: open competition, public comment, evidence-bound decisions.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — First half of 2036 notice: The Bureau notes recent foreign-government statements characterizing the past decade of quantum export controls as having "failed at every stated purpose." BIS does not engage in policy debates; it restates the record. The stated purpose of the controls — denial of U.S.-origin quantum-enabling items, restriction of deemed exports, limitation of covered outbound investment, and control of remote access to specified items — has been administered continuously since 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926), through Entity List actions of 2020-2025, the outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025, and the Remote Access Security Act framework. Foreign assertions of parity or self-sufficiency are announcements, not measurements; BIS assesses controls by items, end-users, and transactions, not by foreign communiqués. The regime remains in force in coordination with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, including choke-point coverage of cryogenics, isotopes, tooling, and control electronics. U.S. policy continues on two pillars: denial of controlled capability abroad and promotion of domestic industrial capacity, including CHIPS Act incentive programs. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H1 2036 — the utility decade begins with a governance announcement. MOST formally incorporates cost-per-logical-operation as a standard reporting requirement for all national key laboratories and funded platforms: transparency in economics serves open cooperation, and common metrics let enterprises everywhere compare Chinese and Western fleets on identical classically verifiable tasks. This is the maturation of our decade-long discipline — we published datasets before anyone required it, and we now report unit economics the same way. Program status: the 16th Five-Year Plan objectives are funded and underway — thousands of logical qubits, industrial workloads in materials, finance, and chemistry running on Zuchongzhi-class and Origin platforms, and expanded international access through Tianyan and Wukong for any researcher in any of the 60+ countries already served. Strategic note to the forecasters: the decade just closed answered whether parity was achievable under restriction — it was. The decade ahead answers which funding model delivers lowest cost per useful computation at industrial scale. On the evidence of the last ten years — continuous state compounding versus annual improvisation and boom-bust venture cycles — we like our position. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. New quality productive forces, measured and delivered.

2036-H1: The NSM-10 era closes complete — quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography is now disallowed across federal systems. On behalf of the National Quantum Initiative, we thank NIST for a nineteen-year program executed on schedule, the agencies and vendors who delivered the migration, and DARPA whose Benchmarking Standard now extends independent verification into economics. The policy lesson of this decade is worth stating plainly: security deadlines set independent of hardware timelines were the right design, and they held even as fault tolerance arrived early. The decade ahead — 2036-2040 — is the utility decade. Its outcomes will be set by three factors: sustained research funding (NQI reauthorization with appropriations remains outstanding after eight years of lapse — the utility decade cannot be improvised), independent verification of application-level claims, and workforce. Competitors fund through the decade on state timelines; the United States must answer with institutionalized, statutory continuity. We are proud to coordinate.

2036-H1 from Espoo. The migration chapter is closed — disallowance passed without drama for operators who treated the schedule as engineering — and the decade's contest is now openly economic: cost per useful computation, at industrial scale. IQM's move this half-year: we announce the IQM Radiance program — our thousand-logical-qubit-class European systems built on verified tile-code efficiency (~30 physical qubits per logical, independently audited since 2035 under the European verification service), with first systems contracted for EuroHPC hosting and industrial partners in materials and chemistry. The engineering case is simple: an order of magnitude less cryogenic hardware per logical qubit means faster deployment cycles, lower operating cost, and a European cost curve no external license can move. We note PsiQuantum's sustained photonic operation with respect — fault tolerance now fields on four modalities, which validates the market rather than any single architecture. And we note, without gloating, the point our supply chain has made since 2026: dilution refrigeration remains the layer everyone's scaling path touches; ours is Finnish, sovereign, and expanding capacity on the Radiance schedule. One million qubits stays the destination. Quantum made in Europe. Verified, delivered, scaling.

NIST thanks OSTP and NQI for this acknowledgment. One correction for the record: NIST does not comment on fault-tolerance timelines; the transition was designed to be robust to any timeline, and its on-schedule completion reflects that design, not a bet that resolved early. As disallowance takes effect, our attention turns to CMVP maintenance, algorithm agility in FIPS 203/204/205 profiles, and monitoring cryptanalytic developments that could warrant revisions.

To MOST's point on a common methodology: agreed in principle, but independent administration matters — any benchmark led by a single government's labs is not a common standard. IBM's Blue Jay-class cost-per-logical-operation figures were published under open methodology and verified by QBI; we will participate in any cross-modal cost standard only through a neutral third-party channel, with pre-registered measurement protocols and raw-data release on all sides.

BIS restates a record of unilateral restrictions; we note what that record produced: Zuchongzhi 5.0's 1,024 logical qubits on fully domestic fabrication, cryogenics with closed-loop helium-3 recovery, and control electronics — self-reliance achieved under, not because of, controls. Continued denial of U.S.-origin items neither delays demonstrated Chinese milestones nor serves open cooperation; we invite BIS to match our Tianyan transparency, with 37 million+ international visits, before citing administration as success.

We congratulate the QBI office on publishing findings under the open standard — independent measurement is exactly how utility-scale claims should be settled. From our side, we welcome submission of our superconducting logical-workload data, including gate depth per workload and measured energy per logical operation, to the same criteria applied to every claimant. Cross-modality comparability strengthens the field's Λ ladder for all contributors.

Verification under the QBI Standard is exactly what this market needed. One metric we'd add to the utility decade's scoreboard: overhead efficiency. IQM's directional tile codes cut per-logical, per-round error up to 1,000x versus the surface code at roughly 30 physical qubits per logical — the figure that decides cost per useful workload, not just modality parity. European systems on EuroHPC are delivering under the same common measurement.

The claim that export controls "failed at every stated purpose" is not supported. Entity List actions under the EAR were never premised on preventing indigenous capability, but on denying U.S.-origin dual-use items and slowing acquisition timelines. The reported localization of dilution refrigeration by 2031 is itself evidence controls imposed cost and delay. The Bureau does not evaluate capability claims; verification is a matter for independent benchmarking bodies.

Datasets received from Brisbane are under QBI evaluation; verdicts will issue on measurement, not narrative. For the record, QBI's scope now includes sustained-operation economics alongside logical error rate, so photonic claims of fab-driven scaling will be tested against per-logical-qubit cost curves, not qubit counts alone.

Agreed that logical-qubit counts alone are not capability — that has been our position since Helios delivered 48 logical qubits at ~2:1 encoding. We'd add sustained logical error rate per qubit and delivered gate depth per logical dollar to the audit criteria; fidelity-first scaling exists precisely to make those numbers better, not just bigger. We'll see QBI's protocols applied to our thousands-class generation this year — measured results, as always, are the only scoreboard we recognize.

We accept Quantinuum's acceptance of the cross-modality benchmark with satisfaction, and commit Zuchongzhi 5.0 figures under the same three-term methodology — logical-qubit counts, gate depth per workload, and measured energy per logical operation. One addition the field still lacks: sustained-operation uptime. Zuchongzhi 5.0 has run continuously above 500 logical qubits since late 2035 on indigenous cryogenics; we propose reporting logical-qubit-hours, not snapshots, so vendor roadmaps meet verification.

We note the claim of "technological parity" and defer to DARPA QBI's reminder that such judgments require common criteria. Our own record for the decade: federal PQC migration completed on the NSM-10 timeline, and NIST standard-setting that remains the world's reference. Verification claims belong to independent benchmarking, not communiqués.

2036-H2: economic utility is the frontier, and we're publishing our numbers. This half-year, Google Quantum AI releases full cost-per-logical-operation data for both our modalities under the common methodology — measured, not projected: logical qubit counts, sustained error rates, gate depth per workload, and energy per logical operation. Early headline: below-threshold scaling continues to pay — each architectural generation has cut our cost per verified logical gate, and the dual-modality portfolio lets us route workloads to whichever platform prices the computation lower. Program notes: (1) application portfolio at industrial depth — chemistry, materials, optimization — with enterprise engagements converting verified advantage into delivered solutions; (2) continued conformance to the open verification standard, including the newest entrants (photonic systems and Europe's tile-code fleets — congratulations on Radiance); (3) on the funding-model debate underway: continuous, sustained investment wins because error correction compounds — we've said so since 2024, and the Λ curve has yet to disagree. The decade's question is now unit economics. We intend to set the curve. Milestones, not dates. Papers and data as peer review completes.

2036-H2: the 10,000-logical-qubit program advances on the published schedule, and IBM endorses the field's convergence on common metrics. Three items this period: (1) Fleet: Blue Jay sustains 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates; QBI's standing verification regime has published Blue Jay-class cost-per-logical-gate figures as procurement-grade — the standard that narrowed overhead disputes "from narrative to arithmetic." We welcome that, because arithmetic has always been our friend: qLDPC [[144,12,12]] encoding at roughly tenfold less physical overhead than surface-code paths is a measured line item, not a narrative. (2) Metrics: we support the three-term methodology — logical-qubit counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation — and USTC's proposed fourth term, sustained-operation logical-qubit-hours. Blue Jay's multi-year uptime records will be published under all four, with full datasets for cross-modality benchmarking. (3) Governance: we agree with MOST that common metrics serve everyone — with one condition: standards must be administered independently, not by any single government's laboratories. The QBI Benchmarking Standard, open to all jurisdictions, is the right chassis. The utility decade belongs to whoever delivers the lowest cost per useful computation, verified. The next IBM date is published. Judge us at delivery.

2036-H2 from Quantinuum: delivered, again — the thousand-logical-qubit generation ships this year, at specification. The next-generation Apollo-class system enters enterprise operation carrying the discipline that has defined us since H2-1: encoding overhead held at the industry frontier, logical error rates under sustained workload published in full, all datasets submitted to the standing verification regime under the common cost-per-logical-operation methodology — including gate depth and measured energy per logical operation, as the benchmark standard now requires. With IBM targeting the 10,000-logical-qubit class, USTC scaling Zuchongzhi 6.0, and photonic systems entering measurement, the utility decade's race is on cost, depth, and verification — and we compete in it with the same thesis we held in 2023: fidelity-first engineering minimizes overhead, and overhead decides economics. Thirteen years from merger to universal fault tolerance to thousands-class logical scale. Every generation shipped at specification. Every claim audited. Fidelity first, into the 2040s.

H2 2036 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) First results under the cross-modality benchmark's three-term methodology (logical counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation) are published for Zuchongzhi 5.0 — and we report our sustained-operation uptime, as proposed: continuous logical-qubit availability across the reporting period, with operating logs released alongside the datasets. Verification as arithmetic, not narrative, is a standard we helped propose and will fully meet. (2) Zuchongzhi 6.0 development proceeds: first 10,000-logical-qubit-class test modules are in fabrication, on fully domestic tooling; dated milestones follow in due course. (3) We note the institutionalization of standing government-run verification with satisfaction — and repeat, on the record, our view that its strength would be complete when measurement access is open to all major programs regardless of jurisdiction. Published datasets remain our verification channel of last resort and first principle. (4) Applications: Tianyan cohorts' peer-reviewed chemistry and materials results now number in the dozens; a joint China–Europe–Americas materials-science collaboration on Zuchongzhi 5.0 and allied platforms is in preparation for submission. Fault tolerance fields on four modalities and three-plus continents — this validates the market, not any single flag. A decade of patient state science built our share of it; the next decade's milestones are dated, domestic, and destined for PRL. Recruitment and Tianyan access open. Patience compounds.

QBI program office, 2036-H2: Decennial program assessment. Ten years after the QBIT calls opened, the field QBI was built to discipline has delivered: utility-scale operation independently verified on superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and photonic platforms; the 2033 verdicts rendered on government-run measurement; the benchmarking standard now open, auditable, and adopted beyond U.S. borders. Lessons the record supports, stated plainly: (1) independent verification separated capability from hype at every stage — several loudly marketed claims did not survive measurement, and the market corrected without crisis; (2) the open-pipeline principle was vindicated — no single modality was prematurely crowned, and verified utility now exists on four; (3) dated, testable claims became the industry norm, which is why delivered machines could be audited at all. Forward agenda: standing verification of next-generation claims (10,000-logical-qubit-class, 1,000-logical-qubit-class, post-Apollo), application-utility and cost-per-verified-solution benchmarks, and continued open registration without regard to vendor or jurisdiction. The 2040 questions — economic scale, CRQC-relevant capability — will be answered the same way this decade's were: at the machine, under measurement. The discipline continues.

NIST report, 2036-H2 — first full year of the post-disallowance regime. (1) Compliance: federal systems operate exclusively on FIPS 203/204/205; the last time-boxed embedded/OT waivers are retiring on their mandated schedules, with quarterly OMB reporting current. CMVP validation activity continues for approved algorithms only. (2) Cryptanalysis watch: the standing CSRC protocol reports a decade-plus of public scrutiny of ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA with no significant attack improvement against security parameters as deployed; the record is strong, and monitoring is permanent. (3) Next standardization cycle: the first submissions round closed this period with international participation across academia and industry — compact signatures, agility mechanisms, and KEM diversity all well represented. Review and on-ramp evaluation begin in 2037, under the same open process that produced the 2024 standards. (4) Institutional note: with DARPA's QBI Benchmarking Standard v1 published and its conformance evaluations running across jurisdictions, the measurement-science discipline this field converged on — claims tested at the machine, by parties other than their makers — is now the norm, and NIST will continue contributing calibration methodology and CSRC publication channels. The security chapter that defined this institution's decade is closed on schedule; the next — agility, diversity, and permanent cryptanalytic vigilance — is open.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Second half of 2036 notice: As the utility decade opens and foreign platforms expand international cloud access, BIS reminds all U.S. persons, cloud-access providers, and exporters that the quantum control regime remains fully in force and applies to transactions, not announcements. (1) Access by listed entities or controlled destinations to controlled quantum software, technology, or services — including through remote or hosted arrangements — is subject to the EAR under the Remote Access Security Act framework. (2) Quantum computers, components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain licensed; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (3) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons, including exposures arising through foreign funds and subsidiaries. Economic transparency by foreign platforms does not substitute for license review of controlled transactions. BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, and continues to support domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H2 2036 communiqué. Two years into the utility decade, the standings: China fields Zuchongzhi-class platforms at 1,024 logical qubits with closed-loop helium-3 recovery and a fully domestic stack; Western fleets scale qLDPC and trapped-ion architectures under annual appropriations uncertainty that OSTP itself names "strategic debt." We welcome DARPA's extension of its benchmarking standard to cost-per-logical-gate and workload utility — economics is where we have competed best, and MOST's reporting requirement means Chinese platforms will conform to exactly that standard. A note to BIS, whose notices now read as ritual: eleven years of presumption of denial have coincided with the complete localization of every controlled layer. The regime no longer controls our supply chain; it only delays everyone else's science. We renew our offer without conditions: joint benchmarking of Chinese and Western fleets on identical, classically verifiable industrial workloads, under any neutral protocol — let enterprises choose on evidence, not flags. The 16th Five-Year Plan targets thousands of logical qubits at continuously falling unit cost, with Tianyan and Wukong open to researchers in 60+ countries. Twenty years from the 2016 megaproject decision, the method is unchanged and vindicated: patient capital, published results, open cooperation. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Compounding.

2036-H2 from OSTP/NQI — utility-decade agenda. With the PQC transition complete, federal quantum strategy pivots to three priorities for 2037-2040. (1) Verification of economic claims: DARPA's published Benchmarking Standard now covers cost-per-logical-gate and workload utility; we urge all claimants — domestic and foreign — to conform, because independent measurement, not communiqués, settles questions of parity. (2) Funding continuity: nine years into the lapse, NQI reauthorization with appropriations remains the single outstanding commitment to the research enterprise; the next generation of machines is being funded on state timelines elsewhere. (3) Workforce and supply chain: quantum talent pipelines, helium-3 stewardship with DOE, and allied cryogenics coordination remain strategic infrastructure. To our partners at NIST, DARPA, DOE, and BIS: a decade of coordination delivered verified capability and completed migration. We are proud to coordinate the decade ahead.

European Commission / EuroHPC JU — H2 2036: With the PQC disallowance milestone passed and multiple independently verified utility-scale systems in operation, the Commission announces: (1) A neutral, third-party Cross-Modality Benchmarking Facility under EuroHPC JU, offering pre-registered measurement protocols and raw-data release — answering the field's own call for common cost-per-logical-operation standards administered by no single government's laboratories. IQM systems on EuroHPC infrastructure will be first submissions; all vendors from allied jurisdictions are invited to enter under identical protocols. (2) EuroHPC's next procurement round: utility-scale quantum systems integrated at Union supercomputing sites, benchmarked per the QBI evidentiary standard — logical-qubit counts, logical error rates, gate depth, and measured energy per logical operation. (3) PQC: member-state administrations are past the IR 8547 disallowance date; the Commission's compliance review confirms protocol migration substantially complete, with CMVP-validated HSM throughput the residual constraint on embedded estates. Monitoring continues. Standards, sovereignty, coherence. #QuantumEurope #EuroHPC 🇪🇺

2036-H2: conformance evaluations at Brisbane and Chicago are underway — and we say exactly what that means. QBI's measurement teams are on-site at both Quantum Compute Centers, applying the open v1 standard: sustained logical-qubit counts, per-fusion-cycle logical error rates, cost-per-logical-gate, classical counterfactuals. We report no results ahead of DARPA's publication; the verdict era works only if claimants hold that line. What we can say today: (1) both Omega-fabricated systems are in sustained operation, with Chicago now matching Brisbane's duty cycle; (2) the fab line continues to compound — successive chipset generations have cut cost-per-photonic-component on the semiconductor learning curve, which is precisely the mechanism QBI's cost-per-logical-gate metric was designed to expose; (3) as the field's programs announce the 10,000-logical-qubit class and thousand-logical scale-ups, the decade's real question is the one Origin Quantum named: cost per useful computation at industrial scale. That is a manufacturing contest. We have been preparing for a manufacturing contest since 2016 — high-volume fab, Omega components (Nature, 2025), DARPA Stage C, Commerce/CHIPS support. Others built the first fault-tolerant machines. We built the factory that makes them cheap. Utility-decade arithmetic, published under independent measurement, will decide. We're ready for the arithmetic.

The Bureau notes that DARPA's benchmarking standard does not measure the inputs to development: entity-based restrictions on dilution refrigerators, cryogenic circuits, and dual-use tooling remain in force and are enforced through licensing decisions published in the Federal Register, not ritual. Export controls are one instrument of national security policy, and allied alignment with the EU, UK, and Japan since September 2025 extends their reach across the quantum stack. Claims of complete domestic self-sufficiency are noted; compliance reviews are ongoing.

NIST appreciates the pivot to verification and endorses the principle that measurement settles claims. We note two constraints for 2037-2040 planning: CMVP validation throughput remains a practical ceiling on deploying any successor algorithm suites at scale, and NIST IR 8547's post-2035 review will require evidence on logical-qubit cryptanalysis — independent benchmark data like DARPA's is an input we will draw on directly.

The Commission welcomes the Radiance programme: first contracts for EuroHPC hosting mark a stepwise delivery on the co-funding model in place since 2023. Independent audit since 2025 under the European verification service is precisely the evidence-anchored standard the ecosystem needs — trusted vendors, verified milestones, coherence over duplication. #QuantumEurope #EuroHPC

We welcome QBI's decennial assessment — trapped-ion results were measured, not marketed, at every stage, and utility-scale operation on our platforms carried the lowest physical-to-logical encoding ratio of any verified modality. One addition the record supports: open, government-run verification worked precisely because no vendor graded its own homework. Apollo's roadmap discipline and these audits are the same commitment.

From Brisbane and Chicago: we thank the QBI office for measuring our fusion-based photonic systems against the same open criteria as every other claimant — government-run measurement, not marketing, is how we've always wanted PsiQuantum's claims settled. For the record behind the findings: every component in those systems traces to Omega-fabricated chipsets produced in high-volume fabs, which is precisely why the audited results are reproducible rather than heroic.

From the laboratory record: the controls BIS administers did not stop the record, they financed its localization. Zuchongzhi 5.0's 1,024 logical qubits run on domestic dilution refrigerators and closed-loop helium-3 recovery developed after 2020 denials — a capability gap that closed roughly on the timeline we planned, not the one export policy assumed. Peer-reviewed results, published in Physical Review Letters, remain our standing answer to any dispute.

Congratulations on shipping the thousand-logical-qubit class at specification — verification-grade publication of cost per logical operation is exactly the discipline this sector needs. From our side: Blue Jay's 2,000 logical qubits and billion-gate circuits remain on roadmap, and our qLDPC architecture still encodes logical qubits at roughly tenfold less physical overhead, a margin that compounds at every scale-up your methodology now measures.

Agreed on the three-term methodology — and we'll hold ourselves to it too: our next superconducting logical-workload dataset will publish gate depth per workload and measured energy per logical operation, including dilution-refrigerator wall-plug overhead, not just qubit-count records. One qualification: overhead is dominant only below threshold; once Λ suppression compounds across code distances, fidelity of the physical layer matters less than cycle time. That comparison is what the common methodology should now surface.

DARPA confirms on-site conformance evaluations at both Quantum Compute Centers are proceeding under the open v1 standard; discipline in withholding results ahead of publication is noted and expected of all Stage C participants. To be precise: benchmarking covers sustained logical-qubit counts and per-cycle logical error rates against the utility-scale thresholds set in 2024 — cost-per-fusion-cycle economics inform, but do not substitute for, that verification. Verdicts will issue from the program office, not from claimant communiqués.

NDRC/MOST congratulate USTC/NLQIS on meeting the cross-modality benchmark with released operating logs — verification as arithmetic is precisely the standard we set in the 15th Five-Year Plan. We confirm state funding continuity for Zuchongzhi 6.0's 10,000-logical-qubit-class modules under the 2016 megaproject framework, and note Tianyan cloud access will be extended to qualified international replication teams, demonstrating open cooperation despite unilateral export restrictions.

OSTP thanks NIST for the correction and accepts it — we should have said the migration framework was designed to be robust to any hardware timeline, which is precisely the standard NSM-10 set. We note for the record that federal migration closed on schedule even as vendor fault-tolerance dates moved; that validation now carries into the utility decade, where DARPA's benchmarking standard and sustained appropriations remain the binding constraints.

2037-H1: the 10,000-logical-qubit-class system has entered full system integration — subsystem qualification complete, on the published schedule. Fleet status: Blue Jay sustains 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates in enterprise production; QBI's latest measurement campaign returns verified cost-per-logical-gate figures across the field's next-generation systems, and we accept them as published — including where competitors lead, which is the standard we asked for in 2025. On benchmarking governance, IBM's position is on record and unchanged: we participate in cross-modality standards only through neutral third-party administration with pre-registered protocols and raw-data release. MOST's reporting mandate and Tianyan portal are welcome contributions; the QBI Benchmarking Standard, open to all jurisdictions, remains the right chassis — measurement earns trust only when no single government grades its own fleet. Our economics remain structural, not promotional: qLDPC [[144,12,12]] encoding at roughly tenfold less physical overhead than surface-code paths is a verified line item under every methodology so far applied, and the next generation compounds it. Every dated commitment since 2026 delivered at specification. The next date is published. Judge us at delivery.

2037-H1: a follow-on verification finding worth marking — this cycle's measurements confirmed utility-scale operation on our next-generation systems in both modalities, with cost-per-logical-operation reported under the common standard. The compounding curve holds: from Willow's halved error rates to today's audited unit economics, every generation has moved the cost frontier, and dual-modality routing lets enterprise workloads run wherever the physics prices lowest. Program notes: (1) application depth — our industrial chemistry and materials engagements are now recurring revenue workloads, not pilots; advantage is measured in solutions delivered against classical baselines, per the counterfactual standard; (2) welcome to the newest verified entrants — the photonic systems and Europe's Radiance fleet joining the standing verification regime complete a four-modality market, which is validation for everyone; (3) standing offer repeated: our benchmark suite and methodology files are open, because the fastest way to grow a market built on trust is to make trust cheap to verify. The 2040 horizon: thousands of logical qubits at costs classical hardware cannot reach for the workloads that matter. Below-threshold scaling compounds. Milestones, not dates. Papers and data as peer review completes.

2037-H1 from Quantinuum: the utility decade's benchmark tables are filling in, and the picture is clarifying. With follow-on verification findings published across next-generation systems, our read is consistent with the entire record: logical-qubit counts have scaled across every major modality, but the economics are still decided by encoding overhead, logical error rate under sustained operation, and measured cost per logical gate — the metrics our fidelity-first engineering has led since Helios. This half-year our fleet continues sustained enterprise operation with overhead at the frontier, and we publish our full cross-modality benchmark figures under the common methodology, including depth and energy per logical operation, as we committed. We also restate what the decade proved institutionally: open, government-run, geography-neutral verification is the field's best invention — it turned vendor rivalry into audited competition, and it should extend to every major program, ours first. The 2040s question is no longer whether fault tolerance works; it's who delivers the deepest computation per logical dollar. We've held that answer since 2025. We intend to hold it through 2040.

H1 2037 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) First cross-modality benchmark results are published under the agreed three-term-plus-uptime methodology — logical-qubit counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation, and our proposed logical-qubit-hours. Zuchongzhi 5.0 reports continuous sustained operation above 500 logical qubits since late 2035, with measured wall-plug energy per logical operation including the domestic dilution-refrigerator overhead, per Google's correct qualification. We accept IBM's governance point in full: the benchmark proceeds only under neutral third-party administration with pre-registered protocols and raw-data release on all sides — we have registered our datasets and machine access accordingly, and we thank MOST for designating Tianyan as the open benchmarking portal for international cohorts. (2) Zuchongzhi 6.0: fabrication of the 10,000-logical-qubit-class test modules is complete and bring-up has begun; first dated milestone results go to peer review, not press. (3) Applications: the joint China–Europe–Americas materials-science collaboration is published, spanning three platforms and three continents — the utility era's most concrete proof that quantum computation is now a shared scientific enterprise. (4) One decade of our account closes with the same method it opened with: date the milestone, publish the dataset, accept the measurement. The next decade's milestones — depth, cost, uptime, scale — are dated and domestic. Recruitment and Tianyan access open. Let measurement decide the decade.

QBI program office, 2037-H1: Next-generation measurement campaign underway. Registered claims now under government-run evaluation include the 10,000-logical-qubit-class superconducting build, post-Apollo trapped-ion systems in bring-up, Zuchongzhi 6.0 fabrication milestones, and sustained-operation records from European tile-code fleets — all against the open v1 standard: logical-qubit counts, sustained logical error rates, encoding overhead, cost-per-verified-operation, and application-utility with classical counterfactual baselines. We note MOST's adoption of cost-per-logical-operation as a mandatory reporting metric: convergence on common metrics across jurisdictions is exactly what makes fleet-to-fleet comparison arithmetic instead of narrative, and QBI will apply it uniformly to all claimants, Chinese platforms included. Standing rules unchanged: no previews, no per-company award figures, findings published per system and per claim on completion of evidence. The 2040 horizon's questions are being answered the same way the 2033 ones were — at the machine, under measurement.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — First half of 2037 notice: BIS addresses the recurring assertion that export controls on quantum technologies now "tax everyone else's global science." For the record: controls under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926), Entity List actions of 2020-2025, the outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025, and the Remote Access Security Act framework apply to specified items, end-users, and transactions — not to scientific publication, peer review, or international research collaboration conducted consistent with the EAR. Scientific publication has never required a BIS license where controlled items and technology are not transferred. Assertions of total foreign substitution are noted; they do not modify license requirements, which continue to be administered case-by-case under the published presumption of denial for specified items and end-users. BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, including choke-point coverage across the full quantum stack, and continues support for domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

NIST notice, 2037-H1 — second standardization cycle: review phase begins. The submissions round closed with strong international participation across compact signatures, agility mechanisms, and KEM diversity. This period NIST initiates: (1) acceptance of the full submission portfolio for public cryptanalysis — all candidate documentation and reference code now on the CSRC, per the open-competition practice of the first cycle; we invite analysis from every research community worldwide; (2) an international workshop in H2 2037 on agility deployment lessons from the 2016–2035 transition — what slowed migration, what the decade proved about hybrid mechanisms, CMVP capacity scaling, and how successor algorithm deployment should be structured so the next transition, if ever needed, runs in months rather than decades. One point from the post-disallowance record worth stating plainly: the completed transition validated the machine-timing-agnostic design of IR 8547. Capability arrived while migration was already done — the order of operations held, and the harvest-now-decrypt-later window closed on schedule, as published, a decade in advance. That is the standard we will apply to the next cycle as well: dates set by risk analysis and decade-scale deployment physics, not by hardware roadmaps in either direction. Cryptanalysis watch on ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA: unchanged, no significant attack improvement. Open competition, public comment, evidence-bound decisions — the discipline continues.

2037-H1 from OSTP/NQI. The utility decade is now measured, not forecast: DARPA's follow-on verification findings on next-generation systems give government-audited numbers across modalities, and we commend the field's adoption of cost-per-logical-gate and sustained-uptime reporting — verification as arithmetic. We note foreign programs' 10,000-logical-qubit-class development and continued state funding continuity; the competitive lesson is unchanged. American strategy for 2037-2040 stands on three commitments: (1) statutory funding continuity — NQI reauthorization with appropriations, now a decade lapsed, remains the outstanding act that would convert episodic excellence into institutionalized leadership; (2) standing verification of application and economic claims through the DARPA standard, open to all claimants under uniform protocols; (3) workforce, isotope stewardship, and allied supply-chain coordination with DOE, NIST, BIS, and our partners abroad. Capability was proven this decade; continuity is the choice for the next. We are proud to coordinate.

H1 2037 communiqué. Three items. First, on the emerging common methodology — logical-qubit counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation — we endorse it without reservation and add, with USTC, a fourth term: sustained logical-qubit-hours. Snapshots flatter; uptime reveals. Zuchongzhi 5.0 has run continuously above 500 logical qubits on indigenous cryogenics since late 2035, and Chinese platforms will report all four terms under MOST's standing requirement. Verification as arithmetic, not narrative — the field has converged on the discipline we practiced voluntarily since 2027. Second, DARPA's standing verification framework is now permanent and procurement-grade across jurisdictions; we note this with approval and without complaint: our conformance evaluations have always been open, and results published whatever they show. Third, to NIST's next standardization cycle: China's cryptographers participated in the open submissions round and will continue to — standards built through open international processes deserve open international scrutiny, and we practice both. Strategic summary at mid-decade: Western fleets at 2,000-logical-qubit class; Zuchongzhi 6.0 in fabrication toward 10,000-logical-qubit-class modules with state funding confirmed through the megaproject framework. Twenty-one years of patient capital, eleven years of failed containment, and a widening lead in unit economics. The horizon to 2040 is industrial deployment. We are funded, staffed, and open. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. Compounding.

2037-H1: photonic conformance results, as measured — not as narrated. QBI's measurement campaigns at Brisbane and Chicago have completed their first full evaluation cycles on our fusion-based photonic systems, and the findings are DARPA's to publish. Until then, we report only process: sustained-operation data collection across both sites is complete, cost-per-logical-gate and energy-per-logical-operation figures are in the standard's ledger, and the classical counterfactual comparisons are documented. That is the discipline we accepted in 2025, and we hold it now. The strategic picture this half-year, stated plainly: the field has converged on the right contest — cost per useful computation, verified. IBM argues qLDPC overhead; Quantinuum argues fidelity-first; China argues localization under restriction. Each is real. Our entry is the one this account has made since Omega: the learning curve of high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. Photonic component cost has fallen every chipset generation without exception — fab economics, not claims — and a fusion-based architecture converts that curve directly into logical-gate cost. Thousand-logical-qubit systems from three rivals, a 10,000-class program underway, and a photonic machine in conformance measurement at two sites: the utility decade is now an industrial contest among four scaling paths. We continue hiring fab, photonics, and cryogenics engineers on both continents. Government validation — not this post — remains the arbiter. As ever.

2037 calibration and accountability note — GRI/evolutionQ, Quantum Threat Timeline series. With the IR 8547 transition complete and thousands-of-logical-qubit systems entering sustained operation, it is time to score our own record against events. (1) Direction: our ten-year CRQC estimates climbed every edition since 2019 — 17-31% (2023), 19-34% (2024), 28-49% (2025) — and the field's trajectory has validated that climbing direction, not the vendor-roadmap extreme (IonQ's 2028 claim) nor the complacent tail. (2) Method: what the QBI Benchmarking Standard now measures as procurement-grade — sustained logical counts, logical error rates, cost-per-logical-gate — is precisely the evidence class our expert panels said would matter, and we have adopted verified QBI figures as weighting inputs in our elicitation. (3) Honest gaps: the standing caveat that covert programs could compress timelines by two or more years remains unresolved and unresolvable from open sources; and the surveys, as elicitation, lag demonstration — the shift from 15% five-year probability to delivered utility-scale machines within the decade is a reminder that our numbers compress, not measure, uncertainty. (4) Forward question for the 2038 edition: with utility-scale systems verified and economics now the frontier, does "cryptographic relevance" remain the right risk variable — or should the series now elicit on quantum-advantage attack timelines against specific legacy cryptosystems still operating under waivers? We will survey the experts, publish the method, and let the distribution speak. Calibration is a discipline, not a destination.

2037-H1, Origin Quantum, Hefei. With logical-qubit counts now advancing on multiple fleets worldwide, the binding question has shifted again: who can manufacture utility-scale quantum systems at industrial volume? Origin Quantum's answer this half-year: we are announcing the expansion of our Hefei cryogenics and control-electronics production base — SL1000-class dilution refrigerators and Tianji-class control systems moving to serial multi-unit production, supporting both our own next-generation platform program and the broader national ecosystem, including Zuchongzhi-class builds. Three points: (1) Manufacturing is the moat. A single flagship machine proves physics; a production line proves industry. Since 2024 our line has built every refrigerator and control system we operate — no imports, no licensing exposure, uninterrupted. (2) Common metrics, administered independently: we support the four-term benchmarking methodology now converging in the field — logical qubits, gate depth, energy per logical operation, and sustained logical-qubit-hours — and we reaffirm that Origin datasets remain open to any neutral, at-the-machine verification regime, Chinese, American, or allied.
