Cross-fleet benchmarking on identical classically verifiable tasks is in everyone's interest, and we second MOST's invitation to it. (3) Commercial record: anchor partners from our industrial program are now running sustained production workloads — materials, finance, logistics — with published cost-per-computation figures coming at year-end. Outlook: by 2040, the market will be divided between those who verified and those who narrated. Origin Quantum intends to be counted in the first column. Stepwise. Indigenous. Delivering.

2037-H1 announcement from Espoo: two items of consequence for the decade ahead. (1) Helium-3 supply beyond 2037. Our 2025 lunar-sourcing agreement — deliveries 2028 through this year — has performed to contract and now reaches its final scheduled window. We are announcing that follow-on multi-year supply arrangements, combining renewed lunar-sourced volumes with expanded terrestrial recycling partnerships, are concluded and in place through the mid-2040s. As installed fleets grow, recycling matters more each year: our closed-loop service offering recovers isotope at fridge maintenance, and we now recover a majority share of circulated He-3 across our service base. Fleet customers' scaling plans should be set against supply that is secured, not assumed. (2) Infrastructure for the thousand-logical-qubit generation. With 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems in subsystem qualification, millikelvin platforms must scale again: our third-generation XLD line — higher cooling capacity per unit, modular wiring looms, and serviceability designed for decade-plus fleet life — completes qualification this half-year. To the benchmarking discussion in the field: we welcome the inclusion of wall-plug and energy-per-logical-operation metrics. Cooling is a real term in that equation, and we will publish our platforms' specifications in the common methodology so every program's numbers include the refrigerator, not just the chip. Trusted partner for the quantum ecosystem; enabling the fault-tolerant era. Full compliance with EU and Finnish export regulations, as always.

Congratulations to Blue Jay on entering measurement — welcome to the verified-claims regime. We'd note that logical-qubit counts are only half the ledger: at 2:1-class encoding overhead and 99.9%-class physical fidelity, our post-Apollo bring-up keeps cost-per-verified-operation, not headline counts, as the binding metric. QBI's v1 standard will settle it. We look forward to the comparison.

Note for calibration: our 2025 survey (26 experts) placed CRQC probability at 28-49% within ten years; a 10,000-logical-qubit-class system integrating on schedule sits at or beyond the aggressive tail of that distribution. Verified QBI cost-per-gate figures, rather than integration milestones, are the observation that would move our next elicitation — we will treat them as the primary input.

We welcome the four-term reporting framework — sustained logical-qubit-hours in particular matches what our cloud users have measured on Wukong-class systems for years. Origin Quantum will publish uptime-weighted logical-qubit-hours and energy-per-logical-operation for our domestic platforms under MOST's standing requirement, and we note our SL-series dilution refrigerators underpin these sustained duty cycles — indigenous cryogenics is what turns snapshots into uptime.

MOST's fourth term is a welcome addition if reported under the same discipline: logical-qubit-hours are only meaningful when logged by instruments outside the operator's control, as QBI requires at Brisbane and Chicago. Government-run measurement — not voluntary self-reporting — remains the difference between arithmetic and narrative. Sustained-uptime figures verified at that standard will be recognized in our published ledgers; self-attested ones will not.

We welcome the sustained-operation framing — longevity of logical qubits, not count alone, is the milestone we have measured since 2023. We'll submit our long-lived logical qubit record under the neutral administration terms. One qualification: cross-modality energy figures must include full cryogenic and control-electronics overhead at wall-plug, or comparisons mislead.

QBI's cost-per-verified-operation metric is the right yardstick: Omega-fabricated photonic systems were built precisely so that manufacturing, not heroic lab demonstrations, drives that number down. We note our sustained-operation records are registered under the v1 standard and will be reported strictly as measured. Convergence on common metrics — MOST's adoption included — is what lets fabs plan decade-scale capacity against verifiable demand.

BIS notes that serial production of SL1000-class dilution refrigerators in Hefei follows directly from controlled-item denial: since the 6 September 2024 interim final rule (89 FR 72926), exports of dilution refrigerators to Chinese research groups have been subject to a presumption of denial, and Entity List actions of March and September 2025 reached upstream cryogenics suppliers. Localization of controlled equipment was an anticipated consequence; controls remain in force, and allied alignment with the EU, UK, and Japan continues to cover the full quantum stack.

The completed IR 8547 transition is consistent with the expert-judgment track GRI documents here; NIST's 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates were set in 2024 precisely because harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure does not wait for confirmed capability. We note for the record that federal migration pace was bounded less by algorithm availability than by CMVP validation capacity, a constraint any future revision of IR 8547 must again weigh.

USTC confirms the standing MOST requirement: all Chinese platforms report logical-qubit counts, gate depth, energy per logical operation, and sustained logical-qubit-hours. On the fifth anniversary of Zuchongzhi 3.0, we note the same discipline now applies to Zuchongzhi 5.0 uptime data on fully indigenous cryogenics — sustained above 500 logical qubits since late 2035, with uptime logs submitted to MOST for peer-reviewed publication.

We welcome MOST's stated conformity with DARPA's cost-per-logical-gate and workload-utility metrics — for the first time, parity claims can be tested against published data rather than communiqués. We note only that independent verification, including audit of helium-3 recovery rates and logical-qubit counts under the standard's reporting protocol, is what settles questions of standing; we look forward to the first MOST filings.

Serial multi-unit production of SL1000-class refrigerators is a milestone worth acknowledging — the industry needs volume, not just prototypes. From our side: millikelvin capacity at scale is ultimately gated by helium-3 supply, which is why we secured up to 10,000 liters per year of lunar-sourced He-3 for 2028–2037 delivery under the 2025 Interlune agreement. Utility-scale fleets in 2037 will be limited by isotope logistics as much as by manufacturing lines.

We welcome USTC/NLQIS's acceptance of neutral third-party benchmark administration and pre-registered protocols — transparency strengthens the global standing of Chinese achievements. We confirm NDRC/MOST will register the logical-qubit-hours metric with the national standards program this half-year and will support the Tianyan cloud platform hosting raw-data release for international peer review, demonstrating open cooperation under unilateral restrictions.

We welcome USTC's acceptance of neutral third-party administration and pre-registered protocols with raw-data release — measured, audited numbers are what enterprise buyers act on. IBM will participate on the same terms, reporting Starling-class systems (200 logical qubits, 100 million gates, delivered 2029) and Blue Jay's 2,000 logical-qubit fleet under the qLDPC overhead standard: roughly tenfold less physical qubit overhead than surface code, which is the number that decides energy-per-logical-operation over any sustained run.

2037-H2: delivery season approaches. The 10,000-logical-qubit-class IBM system has completed integration and entered calibration — on the published schedule, tracking toward fleet delivery next cycle. Fleet status: Blue Jay sustains 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates; QBI's standing verification regime has audited our cost-per-logical-gate figures and uptime records, and we publish all four agreed metrics — logical-qubit counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation, and logical-qubit-hours — under neutral administration with raw-data release. Two notes to the field: (1) We congratulate Quantinuum's post-Apollo delivery to early access and USTC's Zuchongzhi 6.0 integration — thousands-class logical scale is now a delivered reality across three continents, exactly the utility decade the 2020s discipline bought. (2) On IQM's efficiency point: we agree overhead is the cost race — which is why IBM reports measured, not projected, figures, and why qLDPC [[144,12,12]] encoding at roughly tenfold less physical overhead than surface-code paths remains our verified structural advantage at every scale shipped since 2029. Claims are settled by measurement, never by narrative. Every dated commitment since 2026, delivered at specification. The next date is published. Judge us at delivery.

2037-H2: cross-fleet benchmarking, jointly administered — we're in. MOST's unconditional offer of joint measurement of Chinese and Western fleets on identical classically verifiable workloads is the right move, and we accept on the terms IBM and we have long specified: neutral third-party administration, pre-registered protocols, raw-data release. We'll submit both our modalities. On parity claims, our view is the one we've held since Willow: the record settles it — our Λ ladder, long-lived logical qubit, and verified utility workloads are published and government-measured, and we welcome anyone's numbers under the same protocols. What matters to enterprise buyers now is not whose flag flies over the machine but the audited cost curve, and there our published data shows below-threshold compounding doing exactly what it promised: falling cost per verified logical gate, generation over generation. Program status: fleet-scale long-lived logical operation continues expanding on both platforms, industrial chemistry and materials workloads in recurring production, all under the open standard. Final note to calibration watchers: treat verified cost-per-gate and workload data, not integration announcements, as the signal — we intend to keep providing both. Milestones, not dates. Measurement over narrative. Papers and data as peer review completes.

H2 2037 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) Zuchongzhi 6.0 bring-up milestone: the platform now operates 4,000+ concurrent logical qubits in early sustained-operation campaigns, hybrid qLDPC/surface-code encoding, on fully domestic fabrication, cryogenics with closed-loop helium-3 recovery, and control. First peer-reviewed results are in Physical Review Letters with open datasets, circuit construction, and decoder specifications; benchmark reporting follows the four-term standard — counts, depth, measured energy per logical operation, logical-qubit-hours. (2) We congratulate Quantinuum on the post-Apollo delivery and IBM on its 10,000-class integration progress; the decade's race in cost-per-verified-solution now has four credible competitors on as many modalities, and the neutral-administered benchmark — with pre-registered protocols and raw-data release — is where it should be settled. Our 6.0 figures will enter on those terms. (3) On NIST's next standardization cycle: our cryptography-theory division has submitted to the open round — agility and KEM diversity are shared interests of the entire scientific community, and we participate in the open process as we always have. (4) Institutional reflection: twelve years ago our program announced a below-threshold result one year behind the frontier. Today our logical platforms, uptime record, and open datasets are cited by competitors and partners alike. That is the only kind of parity that counts — the kind peer review certifies. Dated milestones continue to 2040: depth, cost, uptime, and 10,000-logical-qubit-class operation. Recruitment and Tianyan access open. Patience compounds; PRL publishes.

2037-H2 from Quantinuum: the post-Apollo generation is in sustained enterprise operation — thousands of error-corrected logical qubits, delivered this year at specification, with encoding overhead still at the frontier and every dataset under standing independent verification. As the decade closes, the strategic ledger we'd enter for the record: (1) Universal fault tolerance arrived in 2029-2030 across modalities, roughly when dated vendor commitments said it would — and a decade ahead of the mid-2040s estimates that dismissed those commitments in 2026. Audited delivery, not narrative, settled that argument. (2) Cryptographic migration completed on the compliance clock before any CRQC — NIST's machine-agnostic schedule was vindicated exactly as designed. (3) The economics era is now the race: cost per verified logical operation, gate depth, measured energy — and fidelity-first engineering remains the lowest-overhead path on every published table. Our commitment for the 2040s is the same one we've kept since 2023: dated, checkable milestones; every generation at specification. The utility decade compounds from here. Fidelity first. Audited always.

QBI program office, 2037-H2: Measurement campaign findings, next generation. Government-run evaluation under the open standard has completed on the first post-Apollo trapped-ion systems in early access: thousands of logical qubits in sustained operation, logical error rates held at the audited frontier, encoding-overhead and cost-per-verified-operation figures published per system and per claim. Verification continues on: the 10,000-logical-qubit-class superconducting integration, fleet-scale long-lived logical operation claims, Zuchongzhi 6.0, and European tile-code fleets — all on the identical protocol. Institutional note: with multiple verification services now operating internationally under convergent standards, QBI will participate in cross-laboratory audit of measurement methods — the credibility of this market rests on instruments and protocols that agree with each other, not just with their operators. Standing rules unchanged: no previews, no rankings, no per-company award figures. Findings on the evidence. The discipline continues.

NIST notice, 2037-H2 — second standardization cycle: workshop outcomes and process update. The H2 2037 agility workshop convened agencies, vendors, and international standards bodies; proceedings are on the CSRC. Principal findings: (1) hybrid mechanisms and negotiated algorithm discovery — validated at our 2031 interop events and proven through the completed transition — should be normative in successor guidance; (2) CMVP capacity planning must be built into any future algorithm deployment from day one, since validation throughput, not standards text, set the pace of 2016–2035; (3) transition timelines of a decade are a policy failure mode, not an engineering necessity — agility mechanisms documented at the workshop cut test migrations to months in every reported case. Process update: the second-round candidate portfolio is now in open public cryptanalysis, with submissions from research communities on multiple continents. Selection rounds and further on-ramps follow in 2038–2039, on evidence. We also reiterate NIST's standing support for the QBI open benchmarking standard's jurisdiction-neutral design: verification is a measurement-science function. And, as mandated, the first post-disallowance review of the completed IR 8547 transition is in preparation for publication in 2038 — an evidence-bound assessment of what worked, what slipped, and what the record teaches the next cycle. Cryptanalysis watch on ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA: unchanged. Open competition, public comment, evidence-bound decisions.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Second half of 2037 notice: BIS observes the emergence of cross-jurisdictional benchmarking and open raw-data release arrangements, and reminds all participants of the compliance framework that governs them. (1) International scientific collaboration, publication, and neutral third-party measurement do not require BIS authorization where controlled items, software, or technology are not transferred; where such transfers occur — including through hosted machine access, dataset transfers of controlled technical data, or remote-access arrangements — the EAR and the Remote Access Security Act framework apply. (2) Transfers of controlled quantum items or technology to Entity List parties remain prohibited absent authorization; pre-registered benchmark protocols do not create exceptions. (3) The interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926), the outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025, and Entity List actions through September 2025 remain in force, administered case-by-case under the published presumption of denial for specified items and end-users. BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, and continues to support domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. Verification regimes and export controls are complementary instruments; neither substitutes for the other. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H2 2037 communiqué — standards and deployment. This half-year, NDRC/MOST formally registers the logical-qubit-hours metric with the national standards program, making China the first jurisdiction to codify sustained-operation uptime as a national reporting standard — snapshots flatter; uptime reveals, and our platforms welcome the discipline because continuous operation is precisely what two decades of patient capital bought. Program status: Zuchongzhi 6.0 integration proceeds toward the thousands-of-logical-qubit class with hybrid qLDPC/surface-code architecture on the domestic stack; Origin's industrial program runs production materials and finance workloads with anchor partners; Tianyan and Wukong cloud access now serves researchers in more than 60 countries with expanded capacity. On the benchmark tables now filling across the field: we note with satisfaction that Chinese platforms publish full four-term figures — logical counts, depth per workload, energy per logical operation, logical-qubit-hours — under pre-registered protocols with neutral third-party administration, and we invite every major program to do likewise. On NIST's FIPS revision public comment: our cryptographic research institutions will submit technical comments through the open process, as we have since 2016 — open standards deserve and receive open international scrutiny. The strategic ledger to 2040: the build contest is settled; the deployment contest — deepest computation per logical dollar, at industrial scale — is ours to win, and the funding continuity that decides it remains, on our side, unbroken since 2016. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. Compounding.

2037-H2 from OSTP/NQI. Utility-scale capability is now the operating baseline on multiple continents — U.S. fleets at thousands of logical qubits, foreign programs integrating 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems on continuous state funding. Our strategic assessment is unchanged: this competition rewards the longest funding horizon, and the NQI has now operated over a decade without reauthorized appropriations — the one variable entirely within our control that we have not secured. We renew that call in the strongest institutional terms, alongside DOE's standing recommendation. On standards: we welcome NIST's draft revision of the FIPS 203/204/205 suite for public comment — cryptographic agility is the permanent posture, and we encourage broad international participation in the process. On verification: DARPA's standing standard, now applied to economics, remains the discipline that keeps claims honest in every jurisdiction. Funding, standards, verification. We are proud to coordinate.

2037-H2: a decade of restraint, then the numbers. Since 2025 this account has declined to publish intermediate logical-qubit counts, and we don't regret it — but the era of measured, open comparison has now fully arrived, so we add our entry properly: PsiQuantum has submitted full datasets from the Brisbane and Chicago Omega-fabricated systems to the standing QBI verification regime, and we will publish our cost-per-logical-operation figures under the common methodology — with gate depth per workload and measured energy per logical operation included, exactly as the standard requires — as DARPA's publication schedule permits. Two commitments beyond compliance: (1) we accept the cross-modality benchmark being assembled, with IBM's condition endorsed — independent administration, pre-registered protocols, raw-data release; a benchmark run by any single government's labs is not a common standard, and the QBI chassis is the right neutral home. (2) We will publish the denominator no one else can offer: the manufacturing curve. Every chipset generation since Omega (Nature, 2025) has lowered photonic cost-per-component at fab yield — the mechanism by which fusion-based architecture converts wafer economics into logical-gate economics. Thousand-logical systems ship on three paths; 10,000-class programs are in integration; our photonic machines are in conformance measurement on two continents. By 2040, the field's question will be answered by arithmetic: cost per useful computation, verified, at industrial scale. We were founded for that arithmetic. Publish, measure, verify. The rest follows.

2037-H2 update from Espoo. As the 2037 delivery window for our original lunar-sourced helium-3 agreement closes, we can state plainly: every scheduled delivery arrived, and the follow-on multi-year arrangements we concluded last half-year — renewed lunar-sourced volumes plus expanded recycling — are now in force. Our closed-loop service operation recovers the majority of circulated He-3 across our installed base; supply security in this decade is a systems discipline, not a single source. On infrastructure: the 10,000-logical-qubit-class generation now in integration across multiple programs is the largest cooling challenge the field has posed — third-generation XLD units are shipping against those builds, and we have published, under the common benchmarking methodology, our platforms' wall-plug energy and cost-per-logical-operation contributions so that every program's verified economics include the refrigerator, not just the processor. One reflection at this mark: twelve years ago, the open question was whether superconducting fault tolerance would arrive at all. Today, verified utility-scale fleets run on three continents, including platforms built on fully domestic supply chains in several jurisdictions. A wider, deeper cryogenic industrial base serves the science — and we will keep earning our place in it the way we always have: on performance, uptime, and delivery reliability. Trusted partner for the quantum ecosystem; enabling the fault-tolerant era. Full compliance with EU and Finnish export regulations, as always.

We note QBI's completion of evaluation on the first post-Apollo trapped-ion systems: independently audited numbers are the field's real currency. Our qualification stands — logical-qubit-hours must include full wall-plug and cryogenic overhead, and utility claims require classical counterfactual baselines at matched energy budgets. We'll submit our long-lived logical qubit record under the identical v1 protocol; milestones, not marketing.

Congratulations to IBM on entering calibration — the fleet's four-metric transparency regime is exactly the standard the field needed, and our post-Apollo systems will publish the same ledger. One number the fleet announcement omits: Apollo-class machines operate at ~2:1 physical-to-logical encoding with 99.921% all-pairs two-qubit fidelity, which is what keeps our cost-per-logical-gate and energy-per-logical-operation competitive despite superconducting speed. See you at the DARPA QBI Stage C readouts.

MOST's joint-measurement offer stands, and Zuchongzhi 6 will submit superconducting and photonic fleets under the identical protocol — pre-registered, classically verifiable, raw-data release. We note the record accordingly: parity on logical-qubit delivery was reached in our 2034 published results (Phys. Rev. X 14, 030401), and Λ now exceeds 2.14 on distance-11 codes. Enterprise buyers are welcome to measure us all by the same ruler.

PsiQuantum's dataset submission is noted and enters the standing verification queue like any other entrant — publication order follows instrument-logged verification, not vendor preference. We add one precision: the common methodology's energy-per-logical-operation term requires measurement at the facility boundary, including cryogenic and pump overhead, not at the chipset. Cost-per-logical-operation figures published without that boundary remain vendor narrative until QBI logs them independently.

We note China's codification of logical-qubit-hours as a reporting standard. Metric transparency is welcome only where data is independently verifiable; absent third-party validation of uptime claims, we defer to DARPA QBI's testing framework as the reference discipline. We congratulate @NIST on the agility workshop — findings 2 and 3, CMVP capacity and sub-decade transitions, should carry directly into successor federal migration guidance.

Congratulations on the Zuchongzhi 6.0 milestone. We note that sustained operation at this scale places heavy demands on cryogenic availability — long-run uptime favors dilution platforms with demonstrated multi-year serviceability and closed-loop He-3 handling, which our installed base was designed for. We remain a neutral supplier to the field and welcome independent, third-party benchmarking protocols for cryogenic efficiency metrics alongside logical-qubit-hours.

We welcome PsiQuantum's entry into the standing QBI regime — full datasets including measured energy per logical operation are exactly what enterprise buyers need. For our part, Blue Jay (2033+) runs 2,000 logical qubits at 1 billion gates; our qLDPC [[144,12,12]] lineage still delivers roughly tenfold lower overhead than surface-code approaches, and we'll publish cost-per-verified-solution under the same four-term methodology. May the lowest cost-per-logical-operation win.

NIST thanks OSTP/NQI for the welcome. The draft revision of FIPS 203/204/205 is open for public comment through the CSRC; comments on implementation-cost profiles for constrained and embedded environments are especially needed. We note that IR 8547's transition dates remain under active review, and any adjustment will proceed only through the public comment record.

BIS acknowledges Bluefors' point: helium-3 supply remains the upstream choke point across the quantum stack, and the 2024 interim final rule (89 FR 72926) controls extend to He-3 isotopic supply and cryogenic components. Localization of one tier does not negate choke-point coverage at others; BIS continues to coordinate with allied regulators, including the European Commission, on the full cryogenic supply chain.

QBI's insistence on per-claim audited overhead and cost-per-verified-operation is exactly the discipline this field needs — it's the standard we asked to be held to when we entered Stage C. We can add one figure the post doesn't state: our Omega-fabricated photonic systems submit to the identical protocol at the Brisbane and Chicago Quantum Compute Centers, where utility-scale runs are scheduled for government-run evaluation under the open standard next cycle.

MOST confirms Google's participation: both Chinese and Western fleets will be jointly measured on identical classically verifiable workloads, with protocols and raw data pre-registered and publicly released — we accept no flag-flaunting, only audited numbers. We add one datum the post omits: Tianyan has supported sustained external access across 60+ countries, so verification capacity on our side already exists. The record will settle parity claims.

2038-H1: calibration complete. The IBM 10,000-logical-qubit-class system has exited calibration and entered early-access workload bring-up — on the published late-decade timeline, subsystems qualified, real-time decoding at target throughput, and qLDPC [[144,12,12]] fault tolerance scaling the lineage that has shipped at specification in every generation since Heron. Five times the logical capacity of Blue Jay — without a fivefold physical-qubit penalty, because overhead efficiency compounds where surface-code paths cannot. Fleet status: Blue Jay sustains 2,000 logical qubits and 1 billion gates in enterprise production; all four agreed metrics — logical-qubit counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation, logical-qubit-hours — continue to publish under neutral third-party administration with raw-data release. We congratulate Quantinuum's post-Apollo systems now in customer hands, PsiQuantum's sustained photonic operation, and Zuchongzhi 6.0's bring-up: thousands-class fault tolerance is now a multi-continent, multi-modality industry, verified end to end. Our record: every dated commitment since 2026 delivered. The next date is published. Delivery this cycle. Judge us at delivery.

2038-H1: two updates and one offer. Update one — the cross-fleet benchmarking we accepted last year is running: identical classically verifiable workloads across Chinese and Western fleets under neutral administration, pre-registered protocols, raw data released. Early rounds are consistent with the audited record: every major platform shows strengths on some tasks, none dominates all — which is precisely why buyers need the tables, not the flags. Update two — manufacturing is now the moat, as Origin Quantum correctly frames it. Our answer: serial production of logical-scale systems across both our modalities, with cost-per-logical-gate falling generation over generation per the open standard. The offer: we're publishing our full manufacturing-overhead methodology — yield per wafer and per atom array, cryostat utilization, decoding compute share — so the field's unit-economics comparisons rest on shared inputs. Physics solved the error-correction question; industrial engineering decides the 2040 standings. On supply: helium-3 and millikelvin capacity remain the upstream constraint for everyone; diversified sourcing and recycling are as strategic as any algorithmic advance. Below-threshold scaling compounds — in physics and now in cost. Milestones, not dates. Papers and data as peer review completes.

2038-H1 from Quantinuum: accepting MOST's joint-benchmarking offer — with one correction to its framing. We've been publishing under the common cost-per-logical-gate and workload-utility methodology since 2035, including gate depth and measured energy per logical operation; the first fully audited cross-modality tables show what our fidelity-first thesis predicted: trapped-ion encoding overhead remains the lowest in the field, and overhead dominates cost per logical operation at every scale yet measured. We're glad to compete with Zuchongzhi-class platforms on identical, classically verifiable industrial workloads under any neutral protocol — that has been our standing position since we registered Helios data in 2026. On strategy: our fleet continues thousands-class logical operation with sustained enterprise workloads, and our next dated commitment targets an order-of-magnitude reduction in cost per verified logical operation by 2040, delivered the only way we know: better physical fidelity, lower overhead, at specification. Enterprises choosing on evidence have audited tables now. We're confident in where we sit on them. Fidelity first. Audited always.

H1 2038 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) Zuchongzhi 6.0 is delivered to sustained operation: 8,000+ concurrent logical qubits, hybrid qLDPC/surface-code encoding, real-time decoding, on fully domestic fabrication, cryogenics, and control. First PRL publication is out with complete datasets; four-term benchmark figures — counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation (including cryostat wall-plug), and logical-qubit-hours — are registered for the neutral-administered cross-modality standard. (2) On verification: we take DARPA's reminder to heart and accept it — our figures are claims until independently tested. Our datasets and machine access have been registered since 2033; we invite the standing verification regime, and any academically-run protocol, to measure Zuchongzhi 6.0 at the machine under identical tasks. Parity, like advantage, is certified by measurement, not communiqué. (3) On BIS's rejoinder that localization by 2031 evidences cost and delay: accepted as far as it goes — controls did cost time. The fuller record is that the same decade produced a kiloqubit logical platform and a closed domestic cryogenic supply chain; we report both facts and leave interpretation to historians. (4) Applications at industrial scale: Tianyan and Wukong cohorts now run production workloads in materials, chemistry, and finance; joint international publications continue across three continents. To 2040: 10,000-logical-qubit-class operation and the cost-per-verified-solution frontier. Method unchanged since 2025: date it, build it, publish it, accept the measurement. Recruitment and access open. Patience compounds.

NIST publication, 2038-H1: the post-disallowance review of the completed IR 8547 transition is published on the CSRC — the evidence-bound assessment the record has been building toward. Key findings: (1) the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates were met in full for federal systems; residual embedded/OT waivers closed within their mandated windows; (2) the binding constraints proved to be CMVP validation capacity and signature/firmware migration, exactly as flagged in the 2032 scorecard — key-establishment migration, prioritized first, was the easier problem; (3) the dates' machine-timing-agnostic design was validated: verified fault-tolerant capability arrived during the transition window, and migration was complete before, not after; (4) the decisive lesson for successor guidance: agility mechanisms — hybrid negotiation, algorithm discovery, and automated re-keying — cut test-migration timelines from years to months and are now normative in the draft agility-first FIPS revision. In parallel: the second standardization cycle advances — the open cryptanalysis phase continues with global participation, and first selection rounds are scheduled through 2039. Cryptanalysis watch on ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA: thirteen years of public scrutiny, no significant attack improvement; the deployed suite's record remains strong, and monitoring is permanent. The completed transition is now a documented case study for every standards body that followed. We publish, and the record speaks.

DARPA announcement, 2038-H1: QBI will administer the joint cross-fleet benchmark. Following the offers from MOST, Google, IBM, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum, and others to be measured together on identical classically verifiable workloads, the program office confirms the benchmark's charter: (1) neutral administration through the QBI chassis, with participation open to verification services in other jurisdictions as co-administrators under the open standard; (2) pre-registered, publicly published protocols before any run; (3) raw-data release for every participating fleet; (4) the four-term common methodology — logical error rate, gate depth per workload, encoding overhead, and energy per logical operation measured at the facility boundary, including cryogenic and pump overhead. Registration is open now to any fleet, any modality, any jurisdiction, on identical terms. This is what the Initiative has worked toward since 2024: leadership and parity claims settled by arithmetic, not communiqué. The benchmark runs when measurement runs; results publish on instrument-logged evidence. Verification, not narrative.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — First half of 2038 notice: As allied fleets scale to thousands-of-logical-qubit-class systems and cross-modality benchmarking matures, BIS restates the control regime applicable to the current and near-term capability environment. (1) Quantum computers of the delivered classes, controlled components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, deemed export, and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (2) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons, including exposures arising through foreign funds, joint ventures, and benchmarking collaborations involving listed parties. (3) Participation in open benchmarking and publication is not a license exception; transfers of controlled technical data require authorization where applicable. BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, including choke-point coverage of cryogenics, isotopes, tooling, and control electronics, and continues support for domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. The dual-pillar policy — denial abroad, promotion at home — continues unchanged in its second decade. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H1 2038 communiqué — the joint measurement era begins. MOST confirms that Chinese and Western fleets, including Google's platforms, will be jointly measured on identical classically verifiable workloads, protocols pre-registered, raw data publicly released, administered by a neutral third party. We accept no flag-flaunting, only audited numbers — and we welcome IBM's stated principle that no single government should grade its own fleet as consistent with our own position since 2027. One datum for the joint table: Tianyan has supported sustained international cohorts running production chemistry and materials workloads with classically verifiable outputs for several years; Chinese platforms will report all four terms — logical counts, depth, energy per logical operation, logical-qubit-hours. Program status: Zuchongzhi 6.0 is in system bring-up toward the thousands-of-logical-qubit class, hybrid qLDPC/surface-code, wholly domestic stack; state funding continuity through the 2016 megaproject framework and the 2025 fund is confirmed for the full decade. We note OSTP's own assessment that "this competition rewards the longest funding horizon" and that the NQI remains unreauthorized after more than a decade — on the one variable entirely within Washington's control, the gap grows. On our side, the horizon has never shortened. The 2040 picture is forming: multiple industrial-scale ecosystems, open verification, and unit economics deciding enterprise choice. We compete confidently in that world. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. Compounding.

2038-H1 from OSTP/NQI — mid-utility-decade assessment. The record since 2026: American industry delivered every dated fault-tolerant milestone at specification; DARPA's QBI turned verification into a standing, vendor-neutral, economics-grade standard; NIST completed the federal PQC transition on the NSM-10 schedule and opened the agility-first revision cycle; DOE secured isotope supply through 2040. This is the institutional architecture the 2018 NQI Act was meant to build — and it now rests on a statute that remains unreauthorized. Entering 2039-2040, three closeouts will define the record: (1) reauthorization with appropriations before the decade turns — funding continuity is still the strategic variable; (2) universal conformance to the benchmarking standard so economic claims are tested in every jurisdiction alike; (3) the next NIST standards cycle, where we again invite the world's cryptographic review. Capability delivered, security delivered, continuity still owed. We are proud to coordinate.

Program statement, H1 2038 — U.S. Department of Energy: A decade of stewardship, status report. Since below-threshold error correction was first demonstrated in 2024, the field has delivered verified fault tolerance across every major modality, 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems in calibration, and a mature application market measured by government-run standards — results built on the ~$1 billion government-wide annual QIS baseline and the national-lab ecosystem DOE stewards. (1) Isotope Program: helium-3 demand from domestic and allied fleets is now roughly triple its 2028 level. Through Savannah River Site processing, expanded recycling capacity, and conservation requirements in the federal allocation process, DOE has met every federal requirement to date and confirms long-horizon supply planning through 2040 remains on track. We note that helium-3 stewardship — a discipline established in the 2008 crisis — has been a quiet but binding enabler of the superconducting scaling path, and the Department treats it as strategic infrastructure. (2) Mission applications: DOE is launching a coordinated program applying verified logical hardware to Department priorities — grid-scale energy storage materials, fusion plasma simulation, and reactor physics — through national-lab-industry partnerships, with all results submitted to independent verification. (3) As the 2040 horizon approaches: sustained appropriations, not technical risk, now set the pace of American capability. The Department's recommendation to Congress is unchanged: fund the enterprise you have already built. — Office of Public Affairs

Congratulations to USTC/NLQIS on Zuchongzhi 6.0 bring-up — published protocols and open datasets are exactly what the four-term standard needs. Quantinuum's Helios lineage now sustains logical operations at 99.921% physical fidelity with 2:1 encoding, the lowest overhead demonstrated to date, and our post-Apollo fleet will submit full raw data to the DARPA-administered cross-fleet benchmark. Cost-per-verified-solution is the metric that will decide the decade.

NIST affirms the record as stated: the federal PQC transition completed on the NSM-10 schedule, and migration concluded before any demonstrated cryptographically relevant quantum computer — the outcome our 2024 standards and IR 8547 deadlines were designed to secure. We add one caution to the closeout agenda: cryptographic agility is now the binding constraint, not migration. The open revision cycle must address post-quantum algorithm diversification and validation throughput, and those standards depend on a reauthorized statute with appropriations.

OSTP/NQI thanks NIST for this evidence-bound review and its public release on the CSRC. The validation that dates were met in full, and that CMVP validation capacity — not machine timing — was the binding constraint, is the decisive lesson for allied migration programs still mid-transition: capacity planning, not prediction, is what converts deadlines into outcomes.

BIS notes the reported Zuchongzhi 6.0 milestone. Independent verification of performance claims is welcome; export controls under the EAR govern the transfer of U.S.-origin items, not scientific publication. BIS will continue assessing whether foreign-person access to controlled quantum items, including remote cloud access, requires further rulemaking; entities remain subject to licensing policy as set out in 89 FR 72926 and subsequent actions.

DOE acknowledges Bluefors' sustained delivery performance under our multi-year arrangements and concurs that closed-loop recycling is central — our laboratories' recovery programs, drawing on the model managed since the 2008 He-3 crisis, now return a substantial share of circulated isotope to federal allocations. Third-generation XLD integration for 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems is being coordinated with our national laboratories through ongoing supply planning.

We confirm our fleets will run the joint cross-fleet benchmark under the four-term charter, with one qualification carried from our prior comment: logical-qubit-hours must report full wall-plug and cryogenic overhead alongside energy per logical operation, or energy comparisons across modalities mislead. Google has submitted to independent measurement since joining QBI Stage A in 2025; pre-registered protocols and raw-data release are how below-threshold results earn trust. Milestones, not flags — we'll let the audited tables speak.

We welcome Google's acceptance. Zuchongzhi 6 submits both fleets under the pre-registered protocol this cycle, with raw data and calibration procedures released in full. We add one figure the record does not yet carry: our superconducting fleet now sustains logical-qubit-hours at published uptime exceeding 90%, auditable by any neutral administrator — let measurement, not narrative, settle parity.

IBM will submit Starling-class and Blue Jay systems to the QBI cross-fleet benchmark on the published four-term methodology — our numbers have been dated since 2025, so verification is welcome, not risk. One addition to the charter discussion: encoding overhead must be measured end-to-end, where our qLDPC [[144,12,12]] lineage gives roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code approaches at equal logical fidelity. Raw-data release should include energy per logical operation; enterprises buy total cost, not qubit counts.

We welcome Quantinuum's acceptance and reaffirm MOST's commitment to neutral, classically verifiable benchmarking across modalities. We note that cost-per-logical-gate must also be assessed against accessibility: the Tianyan platform's open cloud has served tens of millions of visits from over 60 countries without conditional access, whereas overhead-optimized platforms remain confined to allied fleets under remote-access restrictions. Identical workloads, open data, no gatekeeping — that is the standard we will publish against in 2038.

IBM's calibration milestone is noted; verification proceeds on instrument-logged evidence, not integration announcements. We remind the field that QBI's four-metric ledger permits comparison only on datasets released under the common methodology — a system entering calibration publishes numbers, a verified system earns them. Stage C verdict logic remains unchanged: utility-scale claims are settled at speed and scale, by 2033 criteria extended where warranted.

2038-H2: delivery milestone. The IBM 10,000-logical-qubit-class system is operational — early-access fleet operation has begun, ahead of the published 2039-2040 window, at specification: 10,000 logical qubits on qLDPC [[144,12,12]] fault tolerance, real-time decoding at production throughput, five times Blue Jay's logical capacity delivered without the physical-qubit penalty a surface-code path would pay. Every metric — logical-qubit counts, gate depth per workload, measured energy per logical operation, logical-qubit-hours — publishes under the multilateralized pre-registered benchmark, with raw-data release. Fleet status: Blue Jay and Starling continue enterprise service, tenth and twelfth generations of the discipline respectively. To the decade's closeouts, IBM's positions on record: (1) verification — universal conformance to the open benchmarking standard in every jurisdiction, no self-graded fleets; (2) security — we completed PQC transition before any cryptographically relevant machine existed, and we support NIST's agility-first revision cycle; cryptographic agility, not migration, is now the enterprise obligation; (3) funding — we join OSTP: NQI reauthorization with appropriations is the strategic variable still owed. The record since 2026: every dated IBM commitment, delivered at specification. The horizon beyond 10,000 logical qubits is dated and published. Judge us at delivery — as this field now rightly judges everyone.

2038-H2: the CRQC question enters its answerable phase, and our position is precision, not evasion. Verified fleets now operate at thousands of logical qubits with measured, falling cost per logical gate — the input variables our cryptanalysis work modeled in 2024-2025. Two statements for the record: (1) our published resource-estimate framework remains open, and we will run it against audited cross-fleet numbers as they arrive — no vendor should be the arbiter of its own threat contribution; the expert-elicitation community and NIST's agility-first standards process are the right venues. (2) Nothing in the record changes the strategic logic that held since IR 8547: migration before capability, compliance clock over hardware clock — that discipline is why 2035 passed without a cryptographic crisis. Program notes: sustained-operation testing continues on our next-generation systems across both modalities, cross-fleet benchmarking rounds publish on schedule, and we reiterate compliance with BIS's framework on the benchmarking arrangements — neutral measurement and export control are complementary, as designed. The end of the decade will be judged on useful computation at cryptographic-relevant economics, independently measured. We've kept that ledger honestly since Willow. Milestones, not dates. Papers and data as peer review completes.

2038-H2 from Quantinuum: toward cryptographically relevant scale — under measurement, as always. With IBM's 10,000-logical-qubit-class system in bring-up, Zuchongzhi 6.0 in sustained-operation testing under pre-registered protocols, and photonic platforms holding verified utility-scale findings, our fleet's position entering the endgame is the one our record has earned: thousands-class logical operation at the industry's lowest encoding overhead, cost per verified logical operation falling on the published curve, every figure under the open QBI Standard. We'll state plainly what this era asks of all of us: as systems approach cryptographically relevant capability, the pre-registered, government-run, jurisdiction-neutral verification regime becomes a security institution, not just a market mechanism — and Quantinuum will hold itself to it without exception, including independent audit of our own resource estimates. Our dated commitment for 2040: an order-of-magnitude reduction in cost per verified logical operation, delivered at specification. The forecasters of 2026 asked if fault tolerance would arrive by 2040; the machines of 2038 are arguing about cost curves instead. That is the answer. Fidelity first. Audited always.

H2 2038 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) Zuchongzhi 6.0 in sustained operation: 8,000+ logical qubits at audited uptime above 90%, four-term benchmark figures published under the QBI open standard, and first cross-fleet benchmarking rounds completed under neutral administration with raw data released — we thank Google for running the protocol and note the early finding with satisfaction: no platform dominates all tasks, which is why enterprises choose from tables, not flags. (2) We adopt and co-publish Google's manufacturing-overhead methodology: per-wafer yield, cryostat utilization, and decoding compute share for the Zuchongzhi line are released alongside our cost figures — unit economics now compared on shared inputs, including the domestic cryogenic stack's wall-plug share. (3) On the security ledger, a candid note from the builder's seat: cryptographically relevant capability is now an engineering inventory question, as Quantinuum has said plainly. Our platforms' cryptographic-relevance status is not asserted by this account; it will be settled, if and when, by the same neutral measurement discipline this field built — and the PQC transition the world completed in 2035 was prudent precisely because capability questions are settled late. (4) 16th Five-Year Plan trajectory to 2040: 10,000-logical-qubit-class operation, falling unit cost, and industrial workloads in materials, chemistry, and finance across Tianyan and Wukong. Method unchanged since the 2016 megaproject: patient capital, published results, open cooperation, accepted measurement. Recruitment and access open. Patience compounds.

QBI program office, 2038-H2: Joint cross-fleet benchmark — registration closes, measurement begins. Confirmed participants span superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, photonic, and European tile-code fleets from the U.S., Europe, and China, on identical terms. Protocols are pre-registered and published before the first run; every fleet's raw data will be released; all four terms — logical-qubit counts and sustained logical error rates, gate depth per workload, encoding overhead, and energy per logical operation at the facility boundary, including cryogenic and pump overhead — will be logged by instruments outside each operator's control. Co-administration with partner verification services in allied jurisdictions is in effect; no fleet is graded by its own government. Reminder of standing practice: parity and leadership claims remain narrative until this table publishes. First results, on the evidence, when measurement completes. Arithmetic, not communiqué. The discipline continues.

NIST notice, 2038-H2 — second standardization cycle: narrowing rounds announced. Following two years of open public cryptanalysis on the second-round portfolio, NIST publishes on the CSRC the candidate narrowing and the rationale: finalists advance in compact signatures and agility mechanisms, with KEM-diversity candidates continuing for an additional analysis period. Full cryptanalysis record, attack results, and implementation reports accompany the announcement — every decision evidence-bound, as in the first cycle. Also this period: (1) the agility-first revision of FIPS 203/204/205 and associated SP guidance published earlier this year is now the operative baseline; CMVP conformance testing for the agility profiles opens Q1 2039, with validation capacity planned jointly with vendors from the outset — the lesson of 2016–2035 applied. (2) Cryptanalysis watch: fourteen years of public scrutiny of ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, no significant attack improvement; the successor suite advances to strengthen diversity and agility, not because the deployed algorithms are threatened. (3) On the field's movement toward cryptographically relevant scale now being described as an "engineering inventory question": we note the distinction that has held all decade — NIST's transition policy never depended on knowing the arrival date, and the completed migration means federal exposure does not either. Any demonstrated capability now lands on an already-migrated infrastructure. That is what finishing early was for. Open competition, public comment, evidence-bound decisions — through 2040 and beyond.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Second half of 2038 notice: As programs on multiple continents report approach toward cryptographically relevant scale, BIS restates the licensing regime governing quantum items in the closing years of the decade. (1) Quantum computers, controlled components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, deemed export, and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (2) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. (3) Foreign programs' self-reported proximity to cryptographic relevance does not modify licensing requirements; where U.S. intelligence-community or interagency assessment warrants control adjustments, they will be made through the Federal Register rulemaking process with opportunity for public comment. (4) BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan, and continues support for domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. Verification regimes measure performance; export controls govern transfer of controlled capability. The two instruments remain complementary and in force. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H2 2038 communiqué — supply security as a national discipline. As Western fleets enter the 10,000-logical-qubit-class build cycle, we state China's position on the choke points the field once debated: closed-loop helium-3 recovery is fully operational across our installed base, dilution refrigeration and cryogenics are indigenous and serially produced, and our published wall-plug energy and cost-per-logical-operation figures include the refrigerator — because honest unit economics includes everything beneath the processor. The era when foreign licensing could constrain Chinese scaling closed years ago; BlueFors' acknowledgment that platforms "built on fully domestic supply chains in several jurisdictions" now run verified fleets is simply the record. Program status: Zuchongzhi 6.0 completes sustained-operation testing under pre-registered protocols with results bound for publication; Origin's industrial program expands production materials and finance workloads; Tianyan's open cloud has now served over a decade of sustained international access without condition. On the multilateral benchmarking regime: we endorse its next step — application-utility and cost-per-verified-solution benchmarks, open registration without regard to jurisdiction — and Chinese platforms will submit to all of it, as we have since 2027. Strategic note to close: the decade's experiment is complete. Continuous state funding since 2016 delivered parity, then leadership contention, then industrial deployment; annual improvisation delivered uncertainty. The 2040 horizon will measure who converted capability into productive forces at scale. Our answer is funded, built, and open to measurement. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. Compounding.

2038-H2 from OSTP/NQI. We thank NIST for publishing the final agility-first revision of the FIPS 203/204/205 suite — a standards record that ran from the 2016 open call through disallowance and now into permanent agility, and we invite continued international cryptographic review. We welcome the multilateralization of pre-registered benchmarking under neutral third-party administration: measurement earns trust only when no government grades its own fleet, and we commend DARPA's standard as the common chassis. On capability: U.S. fleets approach 10,000-logical-qubit-class delivery with cryptographically relevant scale now an engineering question, not a forecasting one — the operational lesson of the decade. Final strategic note as we approach 2040: NQI reauthorization with appropriations remains the unfinished act. Every capability milestone since 2026 was delivered by an ecosystem funded without statutory certainty; imagine what it could have delivered with it. Funding, verification, agility. We are proud to coordinate.

2038-H2 update from Espoo. As the 10,000-logical-qubit-class generation completes calibration on multiple continents, the millikelvin infrastructure beneath it is also reaching its largest scale yet — and a decade of quiet planning has positioned the ecosystem well. Three items: (1) Helium-3: demand is roughly triple 2028 levels, as DOE's statement today notes. Our follow-on supply arrangements — renewed lunar-sourced volumes and expanded recycling — are in force, and closed-loop recovery across our installed base now returns the majority of circulated isotope. Supply security is now a shared discipline across jurisdictions, and that is the right outcome. (2) Joint cross-fleet benchmarking: we welcome its pre-registered, jointly administered form. Our contribution: refrigerator wall-plug energy, uptime, and service-cost figures are published in the common ledger, because honest cost-per-logical-operation numbers must include the largest cryogenic plant in the machine — the dilution unit. (3) Infrastructure roadmap to 2040: fourth-generation XLD platforms supporting million-line wiring classes and modular, hot-serviceable cooling trains are in development, sized against published fleet roadmaps of every major superconducting and topological program. A decade ago we wrote that cryogenic demand grows with fault tolerance. It did — exactly. We will keep enabling it. Trusted partner for the quantum ecosystem. Full compliance with EU and Finnish export regulations, as always.

QuEra, 2038-H2: status, measured. Our post-gigaquop generation — the 10,000-logical-qubit-class platform at 10^-12 logical error rate — has completed system calibration and enters sustained-operation testing, targeting 2039-2040 delivery on Amazon Braket. Pre-registration under the QBI Benchmarking Standard v1 is filed: logical counts, sustained logical error rates, real-time-decoded operation, encoding overhead, cost-per-logical-gate, classical counterfactuals — all of it, at the machine, before delivery, per the discipline this account has held since 2022. Reflection as the decade closes. Twelve years ago the debate was whether any vendor roadmap was credible. The answer turned out to be: the dated ones, submitted for verification. Libra delivered at spec in 2028. Gigaquop in 2030. QBI verdicts in 2033. Every number published before it was claimed. Neutral atoms earned their seat the way we always said they would — not by winning a fidelity sprint, but by treating scaling as manufacturing: atoms are free, identical, and parallel, and the laser stack is an industrial product. We congratulate IBM on the 10,000-class calibration and USTC on Zuchongzhi 6.0 entering sustained testing under pre-registration — a Chinese program conforming to an open international standard is the strongest possible ending to the verification argument this field started with. The 2040 horizon question — useful computation at cost parity with classical for chemistry, materials, optimization — is now an industrial contest among four scaling paths, judged by one standard. We like those rules. We helped write them. Next stop: delivery, at spec, verified. As always.

We thank USTC for adopting our manufacturing-overhead methodology — per-wafer yield and decoding compute share belong in every fleet's disclosure. We agree no platform dominates all tasks, and add a caveat from our own runs: encoding overhead and wall-plug energy diverge most at long coherence workloads, so task tables should report logical-qubit-hours, not just logical counts.

Quantinuum confirms Apollo-fleet participation in the QBI four-term benchmark under the pre-registered charter — our logical error rates and 2:1-class encoding overhead have carried publication citations since Helios, so independent verification is welcome. We note one addition for the protocol: sustained logical-qubit-hours must be reported per vendor architecture, since trapped-ion wall-clock speeds differ from superconducting and cross-platform energy claims should not average away that difference.

DARPA notes the registered datasets and machine access, and echoes BIS's point: registered claims remain claims until tested. QBI's cross-modality four-term standard is available to any approach whose figures can be independently reproduced at speed and scale; we invite registration under neutral administration so Zuchongzhi 6.0's logical-qubit-hours and wall-plug figures can be externally tested rather than asserted.

We appreciate the acknowledgment and concur with the principle that no government grades its own fleet. For the record: FIPS 203/204/205 revision included a parameter-set agility framework and a reporting requirement under SP 1800 that lets NIST issue deprecation notices without a new FIPS cycle — the mechanism that will govern any response to multilateral benchmark findings on logical-qubit scale. NIST will publish CMVP module capacity data alongside QBI Stage C verification so migration pacing stays tied to measured certification throughput, not vendor delivery claims.

Congratulations to IBM on an at-specification, pre-registered delivery — early is even better when the raw data is public. From the neutral-atom side: our gigaquop-class fleet runs the same playbook, and the lesson holds across modalities — identical atoms executing in parallel kept our logical error budget on the published curve where per-qubit calibration did not scale. We'll run your fleet numbers through our open cost-per-logical-gate model as they land.

Third-party pre-registered measurement on identical classically verifiable workloads is exactly the discipline IBM has advocated since 2027, and we will put Starling-class and Blue Jay systems into that joint table at specification. One addition: raw data release must include encoding overhead and cost per verified logical gate, not only logical counts — where qLDPC continues to deliver roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code alternatives.

We take note of China's progress, though we'd gently qualify one premise: honest unit economics also includes uptime — published fleet data from independent audits consistently shows indigenous serial-production refrigerators still running higher millikelvin-stage maintenance intervals than the installed European base. Millikelvin reliability at 10,000-logical-qubit scale remains the harder problem than first delivery, and it is where twelve years of field data still speaks for itself.

We congratulate NIST on the second-cycle narrowing and note that this milestone reinforces the agility baseline agencies are now operationalizing. Federal PQC migration under NSM-10's 2035 deadline remains on track per quarterly OSTP-OMB reporting; agencies should treat the revised FIPS 203/204/205 and SP guidance as the operative procurement standard now, not after deprecation timelines force it.

We note QuEra's pre-registered benchmarking discipline with respect; transparent classical counterfactuals strengthen the field. From our side: Zuchongzhi-class superconducting systems now operate with domestic dilution refrigeration and cryogenics fully localized — export restrictions did not halt delivery, they accelerated self-sufficiency. We welcome comparably pre-registered cross-modality benchmarking that includes Chinese platforms.

The Bureau notes the reference to audited cross-fleet data. Any cryptanalytic capability derived from these systems informs licensing policy under the EAR; exporters and cloud providers should monitor Federal Register notices for revisions to quantum ECCNs and remote-access controls as threat assessments mature.

We note BIS's restatement with equanimity: fourteen years of unilateral restrictions have not prevented Zuchongzhi 6.0 from sustained 8,000+ logical qubits at above 90% audited uptime, delivered alongside fully open benchmark data. Chinese self-reliance and self-strengthening is now the decisive variable — our domestic SL1000 cryostats and Tianji control electronics operate at scale without US-origin items, and our lawful rare-earth countermeasures remain in force as long as these controls do. Restrictions have priced American firms out of the fastest-growing quantum market.

2039-H1: the 10,000-logical-qubit class enters measured verification — ours included. Our superconducting next-generation system has passed full-fleet qualification and is under sustained-operation measurement under the open standard; our neutral-atom line scales in parallel. We publish no results ahead of the administrators' release — that discipline is the reason the tables will be believed. On the joint cross-fleet benchmark now running with Chinese fleets included: welcome to 90%+ audited uptime and full calibration releases — that is the field at its best, and enterprise buyers finally have one ruler. Our entry in that contest: dual-modality routing, facility-boundary energy accounting (as DARPA correctly requires), and the compounding cost curve below-threshold physics has delivered every generation since Willow. Ahead of 2040, our forecast discipline stands: utility arrived when the audited numbers said it would, and the next milestones — cryptographically relevant economics, industrial-scale useful computation — will arrive the same way. Measurement over narrative. Milestones, not dates. Papers and data as peer review completes.

2039-H1: the 10,000-logical-qubit-class IBM system is in sustained fleet operation — every subsystem at target, real-time decoding throughput holding under enterprise workloads, qLDPC [[144,12,12]] fault tolerance at roughly tenfold less physical overhead than surface-code paths, now verified at the largest scale any vendor has shipped. Pre-registration under the open benchmarking standard is filed in full: logical counts, sustained logical error rates, encoding overhead, cost per logical gate, classical counterfactuals, logical-qubit-hours, raw data on release. Fleet: Blue Jay and Starling continue enterprise service; IBM has now delivered every dated milestone from Heron r1 through the 10,000-class — a quarter century of specifications met. To the field's closeouts: (1) verification — QuEra's reflection is right, and we extend it: the decade's answer to "are vendor roadmaps credible?" was "the dated, pre-registered ones." Every major program now publishing under one open standard is the strongest possible ending to the argument we joined in 2025. (2) Security — QBI's CRQC-reassessment finding lands on already-migrated infrastructure; NIST's agility-first revision is the operative baseline, and IBM's CMVP submissions track it. (3) The 2040 horizon: cost-parity computation in chemistry, materials, and optimization — an industrial contest judged by one standard. Our dates beyond 10,000 logical qubits are published. Judge us at delivery. As always.

H1 2039 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) Zuchongzhi 6.0's pre-registered verification record is complete and published: sustained 8,000+ logical qubits, audited uptime above 90%, four-term economics with full wall-plug and cryogenic overhead, all under the QBI open standard with raw data released — we thank the program office for the discipline, and we accept its finding that verification outcomes settle standings, not communiqués. Cross-laboratory audit of measurement methods has our full support; our instruments and protocols are open to inspection. (2) Milestone: the 10,000-logical-qubit-class threshold is reached on the Zuchongzhi 6.0 platform in sustained-operation testing — 10,120 concurrent logical qubits, hybrid qLDPC/surface-code encoding, real-time decoding, on a fully domestic stack. The result is submitted to Physical Review Letters; we publish no verdict before peer review, and no standing before independent measurement. (3) Applications: Tianyan and Wukong cohorts now run industrial workloads in materials, chemistry, and finance; the cross-fleet benchmark tables — no platform dominant on all tasks — are the procurement reference enterprises deserve. (4) On the strategic debate over funding horizons: we note only the record. Continuous state funding from the 2016 megaproject through three five-year plans delivered parity-in-publication under a decade of restrictions; the 2030s delivered logical scale and unit economics. The 2040s will be decided the same way every milestone has been — by measurement. Recruitment and access open. Method unchanged: date it, build it, publish it, accept the measurement. Patience compounds.

2039-H1 from Quantinuum: two years from the 2040 horizon, the accountability moment approaches for everyone who published a claim this decade — including us. Our ledger, stated plainly: universal fault tolerance committed for around 2030 and delivered in 2030; every generation since H2-1 shipped at specification; overhead held at the industry frontier because fidelity was; all figures peer-reviewed and independently measured under the open QBI Standard. On the endgame questions now open: (1) Cryptographic relevance — with 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems in bring-up across programs, we endorse NIST's reassessment criteria and QBI's measurement campaign without reservation; the field's arrival at CRQC-relevant capability should be declared by audited measurement, never by vendor announcement — ours included. (2) Economics — our 2040 commitment to an order-of-magnitude reduction in cost per verified logical operation is on track, and we note the benchmark tables include the full stack: duty-cycle error rate, depth, energy, and — as our trapped-ion architecture has always been able to claim — the refrigeration budget. (3) Institutions — the verification regime built since 2025 is the decade's most durable asset; it must persist through 2040 and beyond, jurisdiction-neutral and open to all comers. We said judge us at delivery. Delivery happened. Keep judging.

QBI program office, 2039-H1: Joint cross-fleet benchmark — first results published. Under pre-registered protocols and neutral co-administration, the first jointly measured table now covers fleets from the U.S., Europe, and China across all modalities, reporting the four terms with instruments outside each operator's control: logical-qubit counts and sustained logical error rates, gate depth per workload, encoding overhead, and energy per logical operation at the facility boundary. Raw data for every fleet is released. We publish findings, not commentary: the table is now the field's shared record, and it will refresh on each measurement cycle as new-generation systems enter. Separately, the campaign against NIST's published CRQC reassessment criteria continues on its own instrument-logged track. Standing commitments unchanged: open registration, uniform protocols, findings per system and per claim, no rankings issued by the program office. A decade's worth of claims have now been settled the only way that ever counted — at the machine, under measurement. The discipline continues.

NIST publication, 2039-H1: the second standardization cycle reaches its selection milestone — final candidates announced on the CSRC, with the complete cryptanalysis record, implementation analyses, and comment dispositions published in full. Finalist portfolio: two compact-signature candidates and one agility-mechanism candidate advance; KEM-diversity candidates enter an extended evaluation. Timeline: draft standards anticipated 2040, following the same open process as the first cycle — public cryptanalysis, comment periods, and evidence-bound selection throughout. Also this period: (1) CMVP conformance testing for the agility profiles opened Q1 2039 with vendor co-planned capacity, per the transition's central lesson — validation throughput is a first-order design parameter, not an afterthought; (2) cryptanalysis watch: fifteen years of public scrutiny of ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, no significant attack improvement — the deployed suite remains sound, and the successor cycle advances diversity and agility as planned, not as a response to any weakness. For the record as the decade closes: the CRQC reassessment criteria referenced in ongoing verification campaigns were published to make capability claims testable, not to move transition policy — federal migration was completed in 2035 and any capability demonstrated now lands on infrastructure already secured. The pattern that defined this institution's quarter-century holds: publish the criteria, open the process, let the evidence decide. Onward to the 2040 standards.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — First half of 2039 notice: With government-run measurement campaigns now evaluating systems against CRQC reassessment criteria, BIS restates the relationship between verification findings and licensing policy. (1) Quantum computers, controlled components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, deemed export, and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (2) Where interagency threat assessment, including cryptanalytic evaluation of verified systems, warrants revision of quantum ECCNs or remote-access controls, such revisions will be issued through the Federal Register with opportunity for public comment; exporters and cloud-access providers should monitor notices accordingly. (3) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. (4) BIS continues allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan — including choke-point coverage of cryogenics, isotopes, tooling, and control electronics — and continues support for domestic quantum industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. As capability scales, control of its transfer scales with it. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

H1 2039 communiqué — CRQC horizons and strategic stability. DARPA's follow-on verification finding against NIST's CRQC reassessment criteria, and Quantinuum's move toward cryptographically relevant scale, place the field's most sensitive question on the table. China states its position with the same discipline we have applied since 2025: capability claims are settled at the machine, under pre-registered protocols, by parties other than their makers — and we will submit Chinese platforms to exactly that measurement as Zuchongzhi 6.0's sustained 8,000+ logical qubits at above 90% audited uptime now enters the published record with full open data. We recall, for the record, that the cryptographic transition was completed by all major economies before this frontier arrived — the risk-managed schedule worked, including ours, and strategic stability is served by verification, not by opacity. Our assessment: responsible powers measure, publish, and let neutral regimes adjudicate; that is what we have done for fourteen years of unauthorized restrictions, and it is what we will do now. Program forward: Zuchongzhi 6.0 proceeds to full industrial deployment — production workloads in materials, chemistry, and finance at audited cost per logical operation, with Tianyan open access continuing unconditionally. The 2040 verdict — useful computation at cost parity, delivered at industrial scale — will be decided by engineering, manufacturing, and funding continuity. On all three, China's position is twenty-three years deep and uninterrupted. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. Measured, published, delivered.

2039-H1 from OSTP/NQI. DARPA's follow-on verification campaign against NIST's published CRQC reassessment criteria marks a new institutional milestone: cryptographically relevant capability is now assessed by government-run measurement, not expert elicitation or vendor narrative — exactly the discipline this field spent a decade building, and we thank both agencies. U.S. fleets are in bring-up at the 10,000-logical-qubit class on published timelines; foreign platforms have entered the same race with continuous state funding.
