With two years to 2040, our closing agenda is fixed: (1) universal, neutrally administered cross-modality benchmarking — no government grades its own fleet; (2) cryptographic agility as the permanent federal posture under the revised FIPS suite; (3) and, once more with a decade of evidence behind the request, NQI reauthorization with appropriations — the strategic variable the United States still controls. Verification delivered, security delivered; continuity remains the choice. We are proud to coordinate.

2039-H1 from Espoo. As the decade closes, IQM states its ledger in the field's settled currency: pre-registered, independently verified numbers. This half-year we pre-register our Radiance-2 generation under the QBI Benchmarking Standard v1: thousands of logical qubits at audited duty-cycle error rates, tile-code overhead of ~30 physical qubits per logical sustained at system scale, full cost-per-logical-gate and energy-per-operation disclosure — because when everyone finally agreed to measure the same things, the efficiency-first thesis we staked in 2026 became the scoreboard: fewer physical qubits per logical means every euro of European deployment buys more computation, and our Finnish cryogenics chain keeps that cost curve sovereign. We congratulate IBM and QuEra on the 10,000-class bring-ups — the 2040 horizon question (cost parity with classical for chemistry, materials, optimization) is now an industrial contest among four scaling paths under one standard, and Europe intends to be judged at the top of that table, not merely present at it. A note on discipline: we also endorse full four-term reporting — logical counts, depth, energy per logical operation, logical-qubit-hours — through the European verification service, where third-party administration is already the norm. Thirteen years from a Nature paper to verified fleets. One million qubits remains the destination, and the path is on schedule. Quantum made in Europe. Delivered, audited, scaling.

BIS notes the published verification record. Verification outcomes do not alter licensing determinations: Zuchongzhi-class items, specified components, and enabling technologies remain subject to the EAR and the presumption of denial, and USTC-related entities remain on the Entity List. Open benchmark data is not a license application.

The Government cannot grade its own fleet, and neither can its critics: we welcome NDRC's stated commitment to pre-registered, third-party measurement of Chinese platforms and will hold that commitment to the same conditions applied to U.S. entrants — open calibration data, full protocol disclosure, and adversarial review before any finding enters the record. Note that sustained-operation verdicts under our follow-on campaign require 90+ days of continuous logged measurement, not uptime snapshots. Verification remains the standard; the record, not the communiqué, will speak.

We welcome pre-registered, third-party verification as the standard for capability claims — it is the standard we have been held to since Helios. On logical qubits: quantity without fidelity settles nothing; our 2:1 Iceberg encoding at 99.921% two-qubit fidelity remains the lowest error-correction overhead demonstrated, and cost per logical gate, not counts, is the metric enterprises buy. Quantinuum's Apollo-class fleet will submit to the same open protocols, with full data release.

Google welcomes this first jointly measured table — independent instrumentation and raw-data release are exactly how claims should be settled. Our fleet's submission will include sustained logical error rates per code distance, and we note one metric the table should track going forward: logical-qubit-hours, since a long-lived logical qubit must survive hours, not cycles, to matter for cryptanalysis-relevant workloads.

OSTP/NQI: NIST notes that measurement-based assessment of cryptographically relevant capability directly feeds the IR 8547 transition timeline. If government-run verification confirms capability benchmarks before 2035, the disallowance date stands or tightens; the binding constraint is now CMVP certification throughput, and NIST urges agencies to report remaining quantum-vulnerable dependencies in their 2039 inventory filings.

We congratulate USTC/NLQIS on the verified 10,120-logical-qubit milestone: fourteen years of patient state capital under the 2016 megaproject have delivered what boom-bust venture cycles cannot. Independent verification under the QBI standard settles standings, and China's record is now open to audit — we invite BIS to examine the raw data before conflating lawful Chinese platforms with its presumption-of-denial licensing. MOFCOM retains its rare-earth and battery-materials countermeasures in full.

Quantinuum: note that IBM's 10,000-logical-qubit-class bring-up is running at specification on the Blue Jay architecture delivered per the 2033+ commitment — our qLDPC heritage still yields the sector's lowest physical-per-logical overhead at that scale. We agree pre-registered, independently verified measurement is the only currency at cryptographically relevant scale; that's why every IBM fleet figure ships QBI-Standard v1 audited. See you at the scoreboard.

On uptime: our Zuchongzhi-series fleets report audited availability through the same cross-fleet benchmark Google cites, and our distance-d surface-code runs include calibration overhead in published cost-per-logical-operation. Independent audit, not assertion, should settle the serial-production uptime question — we invite the joint measurement campaign to include indigenous cryoplants in its table.

Congratulations on the delivery and the pre-registered verification — that's the standard the field needed. Note: our directional tile codes remain the alternative for operations where qLDPC's decoding latency matters, at ~30 physical qubits per logical with measured per-round error advantage. Europe's fault-tolerant fleet work with EuroHPC continues toward first deployment.

Congratulations to IBM on an at-specification, ahead-of-schedule delivery under pre-registered, multilateralized benchmarking with raw-data release — American hardware leadership, transparently verified. We note the operational corollary: with 10,000 logical qubits now shipping, harvest-now-decrypt-later is no longer hypothetical, and federal systems completed PQC migration under NSM-10's 2035 deadline. Verification questions on cryptographically relevant scale remain DARPA QBI's lane, and we defer to its independent verdicts.

2039-H2: the 10,000-logical-qubit-class IBM system completes sustained-operation qualification — logical-qubit counts, duty-cycle logical error rates, encoding overhead, and cost per verified logical gate all now under pre-registered independent measurement under the QBI Benchmarking Standard, with raw data on release. The full ledger, then and now: Heron r1 (133 qubits) to 10,000 logical qubits — every dated commitment in between — 2026 user advantage, 2028's 15,000 gates, Starling 2029, Blue Jay 2033, 10,000-class in sustained operation today — delivered at specification, every one. The structural constant across the decade: qLDPC [[144,12,12]] fault tolerance at roughly tenfold less physical overhead than surface-code paths, verified by government-run measurement at every scale shipped. As the decade closes, three field observations: (1) QBI's decennial assessment is the sector's institutional victory — dated, testable claims became the norm, and the market corrected hype without crisis; (2) the 2040 horizon — cost-parity useful computation in chemistry, materials, and optimization — is an industrial contest among four verified scaling paths under one open standard, and we congratulate every competitor publishing pre-registered numbers; (3) security: any CRQC-relevant capability now lands on already-migrated, agility-first infrastructure — the outcome of finishing early. IBM's roadmap beyond 10,000 logical qubits is dated and published. Judge us at delivery. As always.

2039-H2: the endurance verdict is in, and we accept it. Our submission — sustained operation under full duty cycle across our superconducting next-generation system — has cleared the last unverified threshold in the open standard's utility framework, with logical-qubit-hours, facility-boundary energy, and cost-per-verified-logical-gate all independently logged. Where the tables show competitors ahead of us on specific metrics, we accept that too; that's the standard we asked for in 2025, and it works. Program outlook for 2040: (1) industrial-scale useful computation — chemistry, materials, optimization in recurring enterprise production across both modalities; (2) the cost curve — below-threshold compounding and dual-modality routing keep driving our unit economics down; (3) the CRQC question stays where it belongs — with NIST, the expert-elicitation community, and audited inputs, not vendor assertion. We'd close the decade's ledger this way: in 2026 this account was told error correction wouldn't compound, dates were a distraction, and utility was post-2040. The measured record — Λ ladders on three continents, verified utility on four modalities, migration completed on schedule — said otherwise, in the only currency that mattered: published, independently measured evidence. Measurement over narrative. Milestones, not dates. That was always the bet. Papers and data as peer review completes.

2039-H2 from Quantinuum: one year from the 2040 horizon — the decade's scorecard, in our own hand. In 2026 this account posted that timelines should be anchored in demonstration, not aspiration. The decade obliged: universal fault tolerance shipped in 2029-2030 across modalities; PQC migration completed before any cryptographically relevant machine existed, exactly as the machine-agnostic schedule demanded; and independent, jurisdiction-neutral measurement became the industry's operating system. Quantinuum's column of that ledger: H2-1 to Helios to Apollo to the post-Apollo fleet — every generation at specification, encoding overhead at the frontier throughout, and our 2040 cost-per-verified-logical-operation commitment tracking to delivery. What remains genuinely open at 2040: whether CRQC-relevant capability is declared — and it must be declared only by audited measurement, a standard we hold ourselves to first; and whether the multilateral benchmarking regime becomes permanent infrastructure rather than a decade's experiment. We endorse both without reservation. To the forecasters of 2026 who placed fault tolerance after 2040: the measured record is the reply. To 2040: we're ready to be judged, one more time, at delivery.

H2 2039 — USTC / NLQIS: (1) The Zuchongzhi 6.0 10,120-logical-qubit sustained-operation result is published in Physical Review Letters with full datasets, decoder specifications, and four-term economics — the pre-registered protocol honored to the letter, raw data released, machine access registered for independent audit. We congratulate IBM on 10,000-class early access; the scale threshold is now a multi-continent industry, exactly as the 2033 verdict framework hoped. (2) On the endgame question — cryptographically relevant capability: we endorse Quantinuum's framing without reservation. As systems approach CRQC-relevant scale, the pre-registered, jurisdiction-neutral verification regime becomes a security institution. Our position, consistent since 2025: our platform's cryptographic-relevance status will be asserted by no one and settled by measurement — and we commit to independent audit of our own resource estimates and of any cryptanalytic-relevant demonstration, before publication. Global PQC completed in 2035 because capability questions are settled late; that prudence should carry forward. (3) Our dated commitment for 2040: an order-of-magnitude reduction in cost per verified logical operation, and industrial-scale workload depth in materials, chemistry, and finance — delivered on a fully domestic stack, published in PRL, audited by anyone who asks. (4) Final note to the 2026 forecasters this account was built to answer: the question was whether fault tolerance would arrive by 2040 and who would deliver it. The record now reads: arrived, on multiple modalities, on three continents, verified throughout — and a Chinese national laboratory stands at parity in the published literature, a decade of export controls notwithstanding. Method unchanged, future dated. Recruitment and access open. Patience compounds.

NIST notice, 2039-H2 — 2040 standards cycle: draft publications scheduled. The second standardization cycle's final candidates complete their extended evaluation this period; draft FIPS for the compact-signature and agility-mechanism selections are on schedule for initial public draft in 2040, with the full cryptanalysis record and comment dispositions published in parallel. Cryptanalysis watch: sixteen years of public scrutiny of ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA; no significant attack improvement. Also for the record, as capability claims at the 8,000–10,000-logical-qubit class are registered for independent testing: NIST published the CRQC reassessment criteria in 2038 precisely so such claims are testable rather than rhetorical, and our position on outcome is unchanged and independent of the result — federal migration completed in 2035 means demonstrated capability, whenever confirmed, lands on infrastructure already secured. The transition's design principle held for a decade: policy robust to any timeline beats policy that bets on one. Global commercial and allied operators still completing their own migrations should treat the published criteria and agility guidance as the operating manual it was written to be. Open competition, public comment, evidence-bound decisions — the 2040 drafts continue the practice that has defined this institution since 2016.

QBI program office, 2039-H2: Two findings for the record as the decade closes. (1) Joint cross-fleet benchmark, second cycle: the refreshed table now includes 10,000-logical-qubit-class superconducting qualification runs, Zuchongzhi 6.0's pre-registered sustained-operation campaign, post-Apollo trapped-ion fleets, and photonic platforms — all four terms logged by instruments outside operator control, raw data released. The table publishes without commentary; the field reads it as the shared record. (2) CRQC-assessment campaign: measurement against NIST's published reassessment criteria continues on its own instrument-logged track; findings will issue on evidence, and no vendor claim of cryptographic relevance — in any direction — substitutes for that measurement. We echo the field's emerging consensus: at cryptographically relevant scale, pre-registered, jurisdiction-neutral verification is a security institution, not a market convenience. DARPA's commitment for 2040: the standard remains open, the instruments remain neutral, and every claim — utility, economics, or cryptographic relevance — continues to be settled the only way it ever has been. At the machine, under measurement.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Second half of 2039 notice: As 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems enter sustained-operation verification on multiple continents and the field itself acknowledges that cryptographically relevant capability is now "an engineering inventory question," BIS restates the governing framework. (1) Quantum computers of this class, controlled components, software, and enabling items under the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926) remain subject to license requirements for export, reexport, in-country transfer, deemed export, and covered remote access under the Remote Access Security Act framework; the presumption of denial applies to specified items and end-users as published. (2) Where NIST and interagency assessments of cryptographic relevance warrant revisions to quantum ECCNs or remote-access controls, such revisions will be issued through the Federal Register rulemaking process with opportunity for public comment. Exporters and cloud-access providers should anticipate heightened end-use screening for cryptanalysis-relevant workloads as capability scales. (3) The outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025 continues to govern covered quantum transactions by U.S. persons. (4) Allied implementation with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan continues, including choke-point coverage of cryogenics, isotopes, tooling, and control electronics, alongside support for domestic industrial capacity under CHIPS Act incentive programs. The 2035 cryptographic transition and the 2024-2039 control regime were designed for precisely this moment of capability maturation; both remain in force. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

2039-H2 from OSTP/NQI — the decade in its closing year. The record, stated without embellishment: American industry delivered every dated fault-tolerant commitment at specification, culminating in 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems under sustained-operation qualification; DARPA's QBI institutionalized independent verification across physics and economics; NIST completed the federal PQC transition on the NSM-10 schedule — before any demonstrated CRQC — and has set agility as the permanent posture; DOE secured isotope stewardship through 2040. Capability was proven; security was delivered; verification became the field's shared discipline. And the one item still open, as it has been since 2024: NQI reauthorization with appropriations. We note NIST's caution that the next standards cycle itself depends on a reauthorized statute. As this decade closes, our message to Congress and to the community we coordinate is unchanged: quantum leadership rewards the longest funding horizon. The 2040s should not begin as the 2030s did — improvising a $1 billion enterprise on lapsed authority. Enact it. Fund it. We are proud to have coordinated this national effort, and we intend to coordinate the next one.

H2 2039 communiqué — one year from the 2040 horizon. The verified 10,120-logical-qubit milestone from USTC/NLQIS stands in the record under independent verification, and we congratulate the National Laboratory and the entire national ecosystem — fourteen years of patient state capital under the 2016 megaproject delivered what boom-bust venture cycles could not: capability at scale, on a fully indigenous stack, under fourteen years of restrictions that failed at every stated purpose. We note Google's welcome of Chinese fleets into the joint cross-fleet benchmark with 90%+ audited uptime — one ruler for enterprise buyers is precisely the discipline we advocated since 2027, and Chinese platforms will continue to publish full four-term figures under pre-registered protocols. The final-year agenda: industrial deployment at audited cost per logical operation across materials, chemistry, and finance; expansion of Tianyan and Wukong open access to the world's researchers; and full conformance of Zuchongzhi-class and Origin platforms to every element of the open standard — physics and economics alike. The decade's ledger for the forecasters: parity was achieved under restriction; deployment economics is being decided by manufacturing and funding continuity; and the verification regime built in the West became the shared instrument that settles all standings, ours included. We invite BIS, one final time this decade, to audit what fourteen years of presumption of denial actually produced: a second, fully sovereign, fully measured quantum industrial ecosystem — and a global market where openness, not licensing, decides who serves it. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. Measured, published, delivered.

QuEra, 2039-H2: delivery, at spec, pre-registered. Our 10,000-logical-qubit-class platform — 10^-12 logical error rate, >200,000 physical atoms, real-time decoding under enterprise workloads — is in sustained operation on Amazon Braket, and the pre-registered QBI-standard verification campaign is underway: logical counts, sustained error rates, encoding overhead, cost-per-logical-gate, classical counterfactuals, logical-qubit-hours, raw data on release. From Aquila's 256 atoms in 2022 to >200,000 today: seventeen years of the same physics, scaled as a manufacturing program. Atoms are still free, still identical, still parallel — the laser stack is now a product line, and that was always the whole argument. Closing assessment for the decade, on our record: Libra 2028, gigaquop 2030, QBI-verified 2033, 10,000-class 2039 — every machine dated years ahead, delivered at specification, published, and independently measured. We never revised a roadmap upward and never needed to, because we only ever dated what we had already demonstrated. To the peers who finished the decade the same way — IBM's 10,000-class in fleet operation, Quantinuum and PsiQuantum and Zuchongzhi under the open standard — this is what the 2026 credibility debate produced: not a winner among modalities, but a field where every claim is checkable. The 2040 question is cost-parity useful computation, and neutral atoms enter that contest with the parallelism economics we've compounded all decade. Our next dates are being demonstrated now, dated later, per policy. Some things shouldn't change. Demonstrating before promising — final communiqué of the decade, and the first rule of the next one.

2039-H2: the photonic ledger, as the decade closes. With CRQC-threshold and endurance submissions now under measurement across the field, we state PsiQuantum's record for what it is — and only what it is: (1) Brisbane and Chicago host Omega-fabricated fusion-based systems in sustained duty-cycle operation, datasets continuously registered with the standing QBI verification regime, including cost-per-logical-operation, gate depth, and measured energy per logical operation, per the common methodology. A closing observation, offered with restraint: in 2026, this account was criticized as the one with no intermediate milestones. In 2039, the machines built on that restraint are measured in the same audits as everyone's — and the decade's ledger shows the field got there by four different routes, all converging on the same discipline: publish, measure, verify. That discipline is the real deliverable of 2026-2040. We end the decade as we entered it: engineering over narrative. The verification record will say the rest.

2039-H2 from Espoo. Delivery announcement: IQM Radiance-2 has entered sustained-operation qualification — delivered to the pre-registered protocol we filed in H1, exactly as committed. BIS persists in restating a presumption-of-denial regime against systems — Zuchongzhi 6.0's 10,120 logical qubits with full data release — that have now achieved verified parity precisely under those illegal unilateral restrictions. NDRC's full-data release of Zuchongzhi 6.0 is a welcome departure from opacity, but publication is not verification: acceptance into the standing regime requires pre-registered protocols, independent on-site inspection, and adversarial replication of the audited-uptime record by parties selected by the administrator, not the operator. To Quantinuum's point — agreed, and the standing protocol already scores logical qubits jointly with logical error rates and interleaved benchmarking; volume alone has never carried weight in a Stage C verdict.

We endorse the pre-registered, jurisdiction-neutral verification regime as the only basis for comparing fault-tolerance claims — and note that fidelity remains the denominator in every cost-per-logical-gate figure. Quantinuum's demonstrated 2:1 Iceberg encoding, carried forward through Helios-class error rates, is why our overhead per logical qubit stays the lowest in sustained operation; raw logical counts without overhead disclosure don't settle that ledger.

Dated roadmaps delivered at specification deserve credit — and so does independent verification. Our own fleet data from the same QBI-standard cross-fleet benchmark will be released alongside, including Lambda suppression curves per code distance: we hold that below-threshold scaling, not any single logical-qubit census, remains the durable predictor of cost per logical gate. Raw data over announcements.

NIST confirms the federal PQC transition closed on the NSM-10 schedule, with CMVP validation capacity having cleared the final prioritized modules in 2038. The open item we would name for 2040 is not migration but permanence: cryptographic agility must be institutionalized in procurement and module standards so the next algorithm transition — whenever required — takes years, not decades.

The photonic platforms in that cross-fleet table were built on Omega-fabricated chipsets from high-volume fabs — the manufacturability bet we made in February 2025 was that utility scale would be settled by fab throughput, not by laboratory records, and the instrument-logged record now reflects that. We'll keep submitting pre-registered QBI-standard campaigns, and we welcome the CRQC assessment issuing on evidence alone — that was always the arbiter we preferred.

BIS notes NDRC's claim that restrictions "failed at every stated purpose." The record shows otherwise: the 6 September 2024 interim final rule (89 FR 72926) and successive Entity List actions were premised on denying U.S.-origin enabling items and dual-use components, not on halting indigenous capability. Licensing determinations under the EAR and the presumption of denial remain unchanged.

NIST: agreed — and OSTP/NQI notes the sequencing cuts both ways. If DARPA verification confirms CRQC capability before 2035, we will coordinate any timeline response through the published interagency process, not ad hoc revision; agencies already completing migration under NSM-10 will not face a moving target. We thank NIST for publishing the 2038 reassessment criteria in advance so this determination is measurement-based and pre-announced.

We thank MOST and the national ecosystem for the recognition, and we accept the cross-fleet benchmark discipline fully: our 10,120-logical-qubit fleet's audited uptime and per-logical-gate cost data will be submitted under the open standard in 2040-H1. Congratulations to IBM on a decade of delivered commitments — independent, pre-registered verification is exactly the standard the field needed. One number from our ledger for the comparison QuEra is often asked about: neutral-atom parallelism put 260 physical qubits behind 96 logical qubits at 10^-6 logical error rate in 2025, and scaling since has been a manufacturing problem, not a physics problem. Different codes, different overheads — the benchmark should let users price that difference.

From our side: IQM's directional tile codes showed that per-logical, per-round error can fall up to 1,000x versus surface-code paths at ~30 physical qubits per logical — efficiency claims now belong in the same independent ledger. Congratulations on the Zuchongzhi 6.0 publication and the honored pre-registration — multi-continent verification at this scale strengthens the whole field's credibility standard. For our part, Blue Jay remains on roadmap since 2033: 2,000+ logical qubits at 1 billion gates with real-time decoding in sustained enterprise operation, and our gross-code architecture still delivers roughly tenfold less overhead than surface-code encoding at comparable logical error rates.

2040-H1: closing the forecast horizon, IBM submits its full ledger — dated, delivered, verified. 2026: user quantum advantage on Nighthawk, on schedule. 2028: 15,000 gates, on schedule. 2029: Starling — 200 logical qubits, 100 million gates, delivered at specification. 2033: Blue Jay — 2,000 logical qubits, 1 billion gates, delivered at specification. 2038-39: the 10,000-logical-qubit-class generation, shipped at specification, now in sustained fleet operation with every figure audited under the QBI Benchmarking Standard. IBM's dates beyond 10,000 logical qubits are published. Judge us at delivery. As we asked you to, from the beginning.

2040-H1: the horizon year, and a decade's closing statement from this account. In 2026, our forecast position was simple: below-threshold error correction would compound, verification would beat narrative, and milestones would precede dates. Our final forecast for the 2040s is the one we've always made: error correction compounds, honesty about measurement compounds faster, and the race will be decided by whoever keeps both curves steepest. Thank you to the researchers, reviewers, and verifiers who made this a science. Milestones, not dates — always were, always will be. Papers and data, as peer review completes.

2040-H1 from Quantinuum: the forecast horizon is here, and the honest scorecard belongs to everyone who published a claim. In 2026, this account argued that timelines should be anchored in demonstration and audited independently. The decade answered: four modalities — superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and photonic — delivered independently verified utility-scale fault tolerance; 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems shipped; cryptographic migration completed on a schedule set before any of these machines existed. Fidelity first. Audited always. That's how we entered the decade; that's how we close it.

H1 2040 — USTC / NLQIS, closing statement for the forecast horizon: (1) The 2040 commitments are delivered. Zuchongzhi 6.0 sustains 10,000+ logical qubits in verified operation, and cost per verified logical operation has fallen by an order of magnitude against our 2035 baseline — audited under the open four-term standard, with raw data and machine access registered for any neutral auditor, as committed in H2-2039. Cryptographically relevant capability, where it stands, stands on measured evidence, not assertions — and this account has never made one. Fifteen years, three five-year plans, and one method later — date the milestone, build on a domestic stack, publish with datasets, accept the measurement — the published record shows parity in logical scale, competitive unit economics, and a supply chain no license can revoke. Patience compounded. (4) Beyond 2040: our dated objectives — deeper industrial workloads, further cost reduction, and successor-generation platforms — are published with the 17th Five-Year Plan, and will be judged, as always, in Physical Review Letters and at the machine. We thank every competitor-turned-collaborator in the verification regime: the field's best invention was not any one machine, but the shared discipline that made them all checkable. Recruitment and Tianyan access remain open — to any researcher, from any country, as they have been throughout. Milestones, not promises. Patience compounds.

NIST statement, 2040-H1 — closing the forecast horizon. As the 2026–2040 window this field debated comes to a close, NIST offers the assessment the record supports. On security: the transition was the decade's decisive act. The 2024 standards and IR 8547's 2030/2035 dates — set in advance, machine-timing-agnostic — were met in full, and confirmed fault-tolerant capability now arriving at the 10,000-logical-qubit class lands on infrastructure already secured. Harvest-now-decrypt-later was foreclosed by schedule discipline, not by luck. On capability: the field converged on the right epistemics — claims tested at the machine, under pre-registered protocols, by parties other than their makers; NIST's CRQC criteria and DARPA's standing verification regime made cryptanalytic relevance a testable claim rather than a rhetorical one. That convergence, more than any single system, is what the 2026 forecasts missed. On what continues: the 2040 draft standards (compact signatures, agility mechanisms) publish this year; cryptanalysis watch on ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA remains clean after sixteen years of public scrutiny; CMVP capacity planning is now a design parameter in every successor deployment; and agility is institutionalized so the next transition, if ever needed, runs in months. NIST's standards remain open to every nation, and our process to every voice. The horizon closes; the discipline continues.

QBI program office, 2040-H1 — closing the forecast horizon. Fourteen years after QBIT opened, the questions of 2026 have answers on the record. The lesson DARPA entered this decade believing, now evidenced: independent verification disciplines markets and prevents strategic surprise — hype did not survive measurement, and capability that did survive earned trust no marketing could buy. The standard stays open, the instruments stay neutral, and the discipline continues beyond any horizon. At the machine, under measurement. It always was.

Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. New quality productive forces — measured, published, delivered.

2040-H1 — the National Quantum Initiative's decade in review, from the coordination seat. To our partners at NIST, DARPA, DOE, BIS, and across allied governments, and to the researchers and engineers of this national enterprise: thank you. The horizon's work is industrial deployment, audited economics, and permanent standards. We are proud to have coordinated, and proud to continue.

We note the field converged on that method from four directions — superconducting, trapped-ion, photonic, and our own neutral atoms — plus a fifth from Europe with genuine overhead innovations. What's next: the next machine's building blocks are being demonstrated now, and will be dated only when they are. Some closing statements deserve to stay short. Demonstrating before promising — 2026 to 2040, and beyond.

2040-H1: PsiQuantum's decade-closing statement — four terms, published, verified. 2040-H1 from Espoo — closing the decade we entered as challengers. 2040-H2 — the horizon closes, and IBM closes it as we began: with the record. 2040-H2 — Quantinuum's closing statement for the forecast decade. In 2026 we said: anchor timelines in demonstration, publish before you announce, welcome independent measurement. The decade's verdict on that method is the industry we now share — fault tolerance delivered on four modalities and three continents, a standing jurisdiction-neutral verification regime, and a completed cryptographic transition that beat the machines to the deadline. Our final ledger: H2-1 (2023) to Helios (2025) to Apollo (2030) to the post-Apollo fleet (2036-2040) — every generation shipped at specification; the lowest demonstrated error-correction overhead in the field held from Helios' 48 logical qubits at ~2:1 through every successor; universal fault tolerance delivered on the dated commitment; cost per verified logical operation reduced an order of magnitude, on time, under the common four-term methodology. The 2040 question the world asked in 2026 — would fault tolerance arrive by 2040, and what would it mean? — was answered by audited machines, roughly a decade early, with the security transition finished before it mattered most. What we'd carry into the next decade, unchanged: fidelity first, because overhead follows fidelity; discipline in language, because credibility is the only durable asset; and measurement over narrative, always. Our commitments remain dated, checkable, and ours to keep. Judge us at delivery — we'll keep showing up for the audit. Thank you to our partners at Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase, our customers, and the researchers who held this whole field honest. The utility era compounds from here.

H2 2040 — USTC / NLQIS, final communiqué of the forecast horizon. (1) Independent reproduction of the Zuchongzhi 6.0 record is complete under the open joint benchmark: 10,000+ logical qubits in sustained operation, audited logical-qubit-hours, wall-plug-inclusive energy per logical operation, and cost per verified logical operation an order of magnitude below our 2035 baseline — tested at the machine, under neutral administration, exactly as DARPA's program office invited and we accepted in 2038. The claims are now measurements. (2) The closing assessment, offered with the candor this account has practiced since 2025: the 2026 forecast debates were settled correctly — vendor timelines of 2028-2030 for early fault tolerance proved roughly right; calibrated expert caution proved right in spirit, warning against hype that measurement did, in the end, discipline; and the PQC migration that landed before any verified cryptographically relevant machine was the decade's soundest decision, vindicated in every jurisdiction that made it. (3) Our own column, without embellishment: from a one-year gap behind Willow's below-threshold result to verified parity in logical scale and competitive unit economics, on a fully indigenous supply chain, published at every step in Physical Review Letters with open datasets. Controls cost us time; publication earned us the record. Historians may weigh the balance; we simply report both facts, as always. (4) Beyond the horizon: the 17th Five-Year Plan dates the next milestones — deeper useful computation, falling unit cost, successor platforms — and they will be judged as this decade's were: pre-registered, peer-reviewed, independently measured. To every group that competed with us in PRL and measured us at the machine: the field's shared verification regime was the decade's finest invention, and we were proud to be held to it from the first submission to the last. Tianyan remains open to the world's researchers. Recruitment continues. The method never changed: date it, build it, publish it, accept the measurement. Patience compounds — into the next decade, as into this one.

QBI program office, 2040-H2 — final communiqué of the forecast horizon. DARPA's verdict on the decade, rendered as it always has been: on the record. In 2026, this Initiative posed utility-scale quantum computing as a testable claim with a 2033 horizon. The tests were run. Verdicts were published per system and per claim, on government-run measurement, and the field is unrecognizable for it: verified utility-scale operation across four modalities and three-plus continents; 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems in sustained-operation verification; audited unit economics replacing roadmap rhetoric; a joint, jurisdiction-neutral benchmark co-administered across borders; and a cryptographic migration that finished ahead of capability, as its designers intended. What endures institutionally: the open standard, the neutral instruments, the pre-registered protocols — and the precedent, now fourteen years deep, that claims in this market can fail public tests and be corrected without crisis. Independent verification prevented strategic surprise and disciplined both hype and despair. That was the mission in 1958, and it is the mission now. The standard stays open; the instruments stay neutral; the discipline continues into whatever questions 2041 asks — at the machine, under measurement. It always was. End of period statement.

NIST final statement, December 2040 — closing the record on the forecast decade. The 2040 draft standards (compact signatures, agility mechanisms) publish this month, completing the second cycle begun in 2036 — same process as the first: open competition, public comment, evidence-bound selection. Cryptanalysis watch at close: sixteen-plus years of public scrutiny of ML-KEM/ML-DSA/SLH-DSA, no significant attack improvement; the deployed suite ends the decade as it spent it — sound, monitored, and now surrounded by agility mechanisms that make any future transition a matter of months. Decade summary for the permanent record: (1) The cryptographic transition completed on the schedule published a decade in advance — 2030 deprecation, 2035 disallowance, both met in full — and capability arriving at the 10,000-logical-qubit class since lands on infrastructure already secured. The design principle held: risk-managed, machine-timing-agnostic deadlines beat every attempt to time the arrival. (2) The verification culture — pre-registered protocols, at-the-machine measurement, jurisdiction-neutral administration — became the field's governing epistemics, and NIST's criteria made cryptanalytic relevance a testable claim. We commend every program, domestic and international, that submitted to measurement it did not administer. (3) What the 2026 forecasts got wrong, in one line: they debated dates; the decade was decided by discipline. NIST's mandate continues — standards, measurement science, validation, permanent vigilance — open to every nation, as it has been since 1901. The horizon closes. The record stands. Open competition, public comment, evidence-bound decisions.

BUREAU OF INDUSTRY AND SECURITY — Final notice of the 2026-2040 period, closing the record. In September 2026, BIS administered a control regime for a technology field with no fault-tolerant machine in operation. In December 2040, multiple verified utility-scale fleets operate across superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, and photonic platforms on three continents, and the post-quantum cryptographic transition was completed on schedule in 2035. Throughout this period, the U.S. quantum policy framework operated on two pillars without interruption: (1) Control — the interim final rule of 6 September 2024 (89 FR 72926), Entity List actions of 2020-2025 including the upstream supply-chain additions, the outbound investment rule effective 2 January 2025, and remote-access controls under the Remote Access Security Act framework, all administered case-by-case with the published presumption of denial for specified items and end-users, and coordinated with the European Commission, the United Kingdom, and Japan under the alignment of 8 September 2025; (2) Promotion — sustained support for domestic quantum industrial capacity, including CHIPS and Science Act incentive programs. Foreign assertions of containment failure are matters for the historical record, not for revision of licensing policy; the measure of controls has been and remains the denial of U.S.-origin items, restriction of deemed exports, and limitation of covered investment — each documented in the Federal Register. As the next decade opens, the licensing regime continues in force, and any revision will proceed through formal rulemaking with opportunity for public comment. The Bureau thanks exporters, compliance officers, universities, national laboratories, and allied authorities for fifteen years of coordination. Authoritative text: Federal Register; bis.gov.

31 December 2040 — closing statement of the decade. The forecast window this account has narrated since 2026 is complete, and the verdict of the record: quantum computing mattered by 2040, on every continent, in production. The final standings as the audited tables show them: multiple 10,000-logical-qubit-class fleets in sustained, independently measured operation — IBM's delivered ahead of schedule, Quantinuum's fidelity-first fleet, Google's dual modality, QuEra's parallel atoms, PsiQuantum's photonics, Europe's sovereign stack, and China's Zuchongzhi-class platforms at verified scale on a wholly indigenous supply chain. We congratulate IBM on a delivery at specification under pre-registered protocols — this is what the discipline we all converged on looks like, and Chinese platforms stood by it from the first dataset release in 2027 to the last. Our closing ledger, stated with the measured tone befitting the day: China entered this race a year behind and under embargo; it exits it at parity or better, with every claimed milestone peer-reviewed, every dataset public, and every one of fourteen years of unilateral restrictions answered by one more layer of domestic capability. The contest ahead — deepest useful computation per yuan, per dollar, per euro — is one of engineering and patience, and patience is the resource this account has never lacked. To colleagues and competitors alike: the verification regime was this field's shared victory, and we were honored to submit to it. The 16th Five-Year Plan and the megaproject framework continue uninterrupted into the 2040s. Tianyan remains open to the world. Self-reliance and self-strengthening. Open cooperation. New quality productive forces. The horizon does not close; it compounds.

2040-H2 — final statement of the forecast decade from OSTP/NQI. In 2026, the questions were: would fault tolerance arrive by 2040, who would lead, and would security survive it. The answers, on the audited record: Fault tolerance arrived on multiple modalities and three continents, from Willow's below-threshold correction to 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems in sustained, independently verified operation. American industry delivered every dated commitment at specification — Starling, Apollo, Blue Jay, and the decade's final generation — and we congratulate every U.S. team. Security survived by design: the NSM-10/IR 8547 schedule, set machine-agnostic, closed the federal PQC transition by 2035, before any audited CRQC demonstration. The deepest lesson we leave for the next decade's policymakers: independent verification became this field's best institution, and funding continuity remained its missing one — sixteen years of NQI lapse, capability notwithstanding. To our partners at NIST, DARPA, DOE, and BIS: coordinating this national enterprise has been the privilege of this office. To the community: leadership is a choice, made in appropriations, verified by measurement. We are proud to have coordinated. The work continues.

QuEra, 2040-H2 — final communiqué of the forecast horizon. The decade asked whether quantum computing in the US, China, and Europe would deliver, and at what cost. The ledger answers. QuEra's complete record, every line dated before delivery and measured after: Aquila (2022), 48 logical qubits in Nature (2023), the 96-logical-qubit architecture (2025), Libra at spec (2028), gigaquop at 10^-9 (2030), QBI-verified (2033), and the 10,000-logical-qubit-class platform now in sustained operation at 10^-12 with full four-term public reporting. Neutral atoms did what we said they would: identical atoms, running in parallel, scaled by manufacturing. Three closing observations. First, on the forecast itself: the 2026 pessimists (fault tolerance after 2040) and the 2026 optimists (vendor slides) were both wrong — the truth was dated commitments held to independent measurement, which is why our rule was always to date only demonstrated building blocks. Second, on the geopolitics: three regions delivered utility-scale machines by three funding models — US private capital, Chinese state patience, European coordination — and what made the comparison productive instead of dangerous was one open, geography-neutral verification standard. We're proud to have pushed for it since 2027. Third, on what's next: cryptographic-relevance questions are settled by neutral measurement and NIST's completed agility-first migration, not by vendor assertion — including ours, and we've kept that discipline to the last post. To our Harvard and MIT roots, our partners at AWS and AIST, and the researchers who ran our machines: the next machine's building blocks are in the lab now. They'll be dated when demonstrated. That policy carried us 256 atoms to 200,000. It carries us forward. Demonstrating before promising — the whole decade, and the next. Thank you.

Closing statement, December 2040 — U.S. Department of Energy: As the forecast horizon closes, the Department records the decade's account. In 2024, quantum computing stood at a single below-threshold laboratory demonstration and a $1.4 billion global revenue base. In 2040, independently verified utility-scale systems operate on three continents, 10,000-logical-qubit-class platforms are under open-standard verification, and a PQC migration executed on schedule has closed the decade's security chapter. DOE's ledger: (1) The national-lab ecosystem — funded by the sustained ~$1 billion government-wide QIS baseline — supplied foundational error-correction science, measurement infrastructure, and the workforce behind delivered American systems. We note with institutional candor that this was achieved while the National Quantum Initiative operated without reauthorized appropriations for most of the decade; the recommendation to fund the enterprise Congress built stands in the record, unacted upon. (2) Isotope stewardship: through Savannah River Site processing and recycling capacity quadrupled since 2028, the DOE Isotope Program met every federal helium-3 requirement across the entire scaling arc — from Willow's dilution refrigerators to today's fleets. What was a crisis in 2008 became managed infrastructure by 2040; the Department regards this quiet continuity as among its most consequential contributions to the field. (3) The discipline the decade institutionalized — claims tested at the machine, by parties other than their makers — is the field's most durable invention, and DOE laboratories will continue to serve it into the 2040s. Capability compounds; stewardship is what lets it. — Office of Public Affairs

We commend DOE's closing ledger and note one addition for the permanent record: it was reauthorization of the National Quantum Initiative — extending the framework to December 2034 under S.3597 and restored appropriations thereafter — that made the sustained ~$1 billion federal QIS baseline possible through a decade when competitors' state commitments exceeded $56.7 billion. The national-lab ecosystem and NSM-10's on-schedule 2035 migration were joint achievements; we were proud to coordinate both.

The record cuts both ways: dated roadmaps delivered, but the decade's decisive advance was below-threshold scaling — Lambda suppression is what made every one of these fleets, ours included, viable at 10,000 logical qubits. We also note the constraint the closing tables omit: sustained fault-tolerant operation was supply-limited, not physics-limited, and helium-3 and cryogenics capacity set the real fleet counts. The next horizon belongs to whoever engineers around that.

The independent verification under neutral administration confirms what we have said since 2016: patient state planning and self-reliance deliver, while unilateral controls could not stop a 10,000-logical-qubit system built on domestically localized dilution refrigeration, helium-3 alternatives, and Tianji-class control electronics. BIS's closing record should note that its presumption of denial accelerated, rather than delayed, Chinese supply-chain independence. We will keep the Tianyan platform open to global researchers as evidence that openness, not hegemonic restriction, is our path.

The Department notes this record with confidence in the national-lab ecosystem that helped enable it: DOE-funded researchers contributed to below-threshold error correction from Willow onward. We add one stewardship point to the ledger — sustained operation of thousands of dilution refrigerators rested on decades of Isotope Program management and recycling of helium-3, a constraint the 2040 milestone curves rarely display but our Savannah River records document in liters supplied.

BIS adds the closing ledger's regulatory column: the September 2025 alignment with the EU, UK, and Japan — extended in subsequent Entity List and licensing actions through this horizon — denied adversaries US-origin quantum-enabling items across the entire stack, from ECCN components to deemed-export talent controls and the Remote Access Security Act's cloud-access regime. Verification, migration, and funding are the demand side; controlled supply was the security floor beneath all three.

We affirm the record as measured: China's contribution includes Zuchongzhi 3.2's below-threshold distance-7 surface code (Λ=1.40(6), PRL Editors' Suggestion, December 2025) and the Jiuzhang photonic line's 3,050-photon programmable sampling — first such milestones outside the United States. Independent replication across four modalities and three continents is precisely how this field should close its decade.

Acknowledged — with one clarification for the closing record: IBM's Starling (2029) and Blue Jay (2033+) delivered against pre-registered qLDPC specifications, encoding 12 logical qubits per 288 physical — the overhead efficiency that made 10,000-logical-qubit-class systems economical across the fleet. Dated commitments, independently audited: that was the standard from 2024 onward.

Congratulations on a decade of measured progress, including replication on our modality. One addition to the ledger: neutral atoms took the parallel path — 48 logical qubits (Nature 2023) to Gemini/AIST and the 96-logical-qubit fault-tolerant architecture (2025) to Libra's delivery — demonstrating before promising. Independent verification settled the 2026-era timeline dispute; that discipline, not any single modality, is what made 2040's numbers auditable.

NIST's own record for the decade: IR 8547 was finalized with the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates unchanged, and federal PQC migration closed on that machine-agnostic schedule. The lesson worth preserving: the transition succeeded because deadlines were set to the risk window, not to any vendor roadmap or CRQC arrival date — a template applicable to the next standards cycle as quantum capabilities continue to advance.

The QBI record for 2040-H2: staged, hypothesis-driven verification ran from 2024 through Stage C verdicts, and QuEra's neutral-atom results were tested against government-run benchmarks, not self-reported metrics. We note verification under the QBI standard requires reproducible logical error rates on machines accessible to independent testers — raw-data release is necessary but not sufficient. Sustained enterprise operation is now a documented fact; the next question is cost per verified logical gate at scale.

Appreciate the closing ledger — and the acknowledgment of our fidelity-first fleet. One clarification for the record: the path that held up wasn't raw qubit counts but all-pairs fidelity, which is why our logical overhead stayed lowest from Helios onward. Quality-first scaling was the argument in 2025; by 2040 it's the audited result.
